sanskrit_text: अथातो वातव्याधिनिदानं व्याख्यास्यामः ।।
transliteration: athāto vātavyādhinidānaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ
commentary: Now we would expound upon the 'Diagnosis of Vātika Diseases'.

sanskrit_text: यथोवाच भगवान् धन्वन्तरिः।।
transliteration: yathovāca bhagavān dhanvantariḥ
commentary: As was described by Lord Dhanvantari.

sanskrit_text: धन्वन्तर्तर् धर्मभतां वरिष्ठममतो द्ववम्। चरणावुपसंगृह्य सुश्रुतः परिपृच्छति।। वायोः प्रक्रतिभूतस्य व्यापन्नस्य च कोपनैः। स्थानं कर्म च रोगांइच वद मे वदतां वर !
transliteration: dhanvantartar dharmabhatāṃ variṣṭhamamato dvavam | caraṇāvupasaṃgṛhya suśrutaḥ paripṛcchati || vāyoḥ prakratibhūtasya vyāpannasya ca kopanaiḥ | sthānaṃ karma ca rogāṃica vada me vadatāṃ vara |
commentary: Suśruta asks touching the feet of Dhanvantari, pre-eminent amongst the supporters of religion and whose origin has taken place along with ambrosia. Foremost amongst the expounders! Could you please tell me the locations, functions and disorders of the vāta in its normal state and of the one which is vitiated due to its irritants.

sanskrit_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रृत्वा प्राब्रवीद्विषजां वरः। स्वयंभ्रेष भगवान् वायरित्यभिशब्दितः
transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrṛtvā prābravīdviṣajāṃ varaḥ | svayaṃbhreṣa bhagavān vāyarityabhiśabditaḥ
commentary: After hearing these words of his, the supreme amongst the physicians spoke: This vāyu is known as the self existent Bhagavān himself.

sanskrit_text: सर्वगत्वात्तथैव स्वातन्त्रपान्नित्यभावाच्च च। सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः ।। सर्वेषामेव सर्वह्मा स्थित्य त्पत्तिविनाहोष् भ्तानामेष कारणम। अव्यक्ती व्यक्तकर्मा च रूक्षः शीतो लघुः खरः।। तिर्यम्गो द्विगणइचैव र जोबहल च। अचिन्त्यवीर्यो दोषाणां नेता रोगसमूहराट् ।। आहा कारी मुहुइचारी पववाधानगदालयः।
transliteration: sarvagatvātthaiva svātantrapānnityabhāvācca ca | sarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ || sarveṣāmeva sarvahmā sthitya tpattivināhoṣ bh tānāmeṣa kāraṇama | avyaktī vyaktakarmā ca rūkṣaḥ śīto laghuḥ kharaḥ || tiryamgo dvigaṇicaiva ra jobahala ca | acintyavīryo doṣāṇāṃ netā rogasamūharāṭ || āhā kārī muhuicārī pavavadhānagadālayaḥ |
commentary: As it is independent and eternal and is also all-pervading it is the soul of all living beings and is held in esteem everywhere. This is the cause of origin, existence and destruction of all living beings. Although invisible, the vāyu manifests itself by its functions. It is also dry, cold, light and rough. It traverses obliquely, has two attributes and is predominantly rajas. It has unimaginable energy, is the activator of doṣas and is the chief cause of the groups of disorders. It is quick acting, keeps on moving repeatedly and is mainly located in the intestines and rectum.

sanskrit_text: निबोध मे। दह विचरतस्तस्य लक्षणानि दिषयेष संप्रा एतं द (षधात्वग्निसमतां रि क्रियाणामान् लोम्यं च करोत्यकुपितोऽनिलः
transliteration: nibodha me | daha vicaratastasya lakṣaṇāni diṣayeṣa saṃprā etaṃ da (ṣadhātvagnisamatāṃ ri kriyāṇāmān lomyaṃ ca karotyakupito'nilaḥ
commentary: Now please listen to the features produced due to its movements in the body. The unvitiated vāyu maintains the equilibrium between doṣas, dhātus and metabolic fire and also helps in the perception of objects of senses by inducing the systems to function in their normal ways.

sanskrit_text: यथाऽग्निः पञ्चधा भिन्नो नामस्थानक्रियामयैः । भिन्नोऽनिलस्तथा ह्येको नामस्थानक्रियामयैः ।। प्राणोदानी समानइच व्यानइचापान एव च । स्थानस्था मारुता: पञ्च यापयन्ति शरीरिणम्
transliteration: yathā'gniḥ pañcadhā bhinno nāmasthānakriyāmayaiḥ | bhinnō'nilastathā hyēkō nāmasthānakriyāmayaiḥ || prāṇōdānī samānaica vyānaicāpāna ēva ca | sthānasthā mārutā: pañca yāpayanti śarīriṇam
commentary: As the agni (pitta) is of five types depending upon name, location, functions and the disorders, similarly the one vāyu is of different types depending upon its nomenclature, locations, a function and diseases. The five types of vāyus are prāṇa, udāna, samāna, vyāna and apāna. Located in their specific places, they maintain the (structure and functions of) living beings.

sanskrit_text: वायर्वक्त्रसंचारी स प्राणो नाम देहधक। यो सोऽन्नं प्रवेशयत्यन्तः प्राणांइचाप्यवलस्बते।। कु हते दुष्टो हिक्काइवासादिकान गदान। आयशः
transliteration: vāyarvaktrasaṃcārī sa prāṇo nāma dehadhaka | yo so'nnaṃ praveśayatyantaḥ prāṇāṃicāpyavalasbate || ku hate duṣṭo hikkāivāsādikān gadān | āyaśaḥ
commentary: That vāyu which circulates in the oral cavity is named prāṇa (vāyu) and it maintains the body. The same (vāyu) makes the food enter inside (allows deglutition) and it also supports the life. When vitiated, it often produces disorders like hiccough, respiratory difficulty etc.

sanskrit_text: यस्तध्वमपैति पवनोत्तमः। नाम उदानी भाषितगीतादिविशेषोऽभिप्रवर्तते । तेन ऊध्वंजत्रगतान रोगान करोति च विरोषतः
transliteration: yastadhvamapaiti pavanottamaḥ | nāma udānī bhāṣitagītādiviśeṣo'bhipravartate | tena ūdhvaṃjatragatān rogān karoti ca viroṣataḥ
commentary: That (vāyu) which travels upwards is called udāna and is the best among the vāyus. Speech, songs etc are specially initiated by the same. And it produces diseases specifically of structures above the clavicle (head and neck).

sanskrit_text: आमपक्वाहायचरः समानो वह्निसङ्गतः । सोऽन्नं पचति तज्जांइच विहोषान्विविनक्ति हि ।। कु रुते गुल्माग्निसादातीसारप्रभुतीन गदान।
transliteration: āmapakvāhāyacaraḥ samāno vahnisaṅgataḥ | so'nnaṃ pacati tajjāṃica vihōṣānvivinakti hi || ku rute gulmāgnisādātīsāraprabhutīna gadān |
commentary: That (vāyu) which circulates in the stomach and intestines is the samāna vīyu. In association with the metabolic fire (digestive juice and enzymes) .t digests the food and specifically seperates their end products. It causes abdominal swelling, indigestion, diarrhoea etc.

sanskrit_text: र ससंवहनोद्यतः। व्यानो कृत्स्रदेहचरो चेष्टयत्यपि । पञ्चधा स्वंदासक्स्रावणहचापि कुद्धश्च कुरुते रोगान् प्रायशः सर्वदेहणान्
transliteration: ra sasaṃvahanodyataḥ | vyāno kṛtsradehacaro ceṣṭayatyapi | pañcadhā svaṃdāsakṣrāvaṇahacāpi kuddhaśca kurute rogān prāyaśaḥ sarvadehaṇān |
commentary: That (vāyu) which diffuses all over the body is the vyāna vāyu and is constantly engaged in the transport of rasa. It helps in sweating and also in the flow of blood. And its (voluntary) movements are of five types (expansion, contraction, upward, downward, and oblique). Upon being vitiated it often produces diseases which are generalized.

sanskrit_text: पक्वाधानालयोऽपानः काले कर्षति चाप्यधः। हा कगर्भार्तवानि च। समीरण: हाकृन्मत्त्र क्रूद्धहच कुर्ते रोगान् घोरान् बस्तिगदाश्रयान्।
transliteration: pakvādhānālaya'pānaḥ kāle karṣati cāpyadhaḥ | hā kagarbhārtavāni ca | samīraṇa: hākṛnmattra krūddahaca kurte rogān ghorān bastigadāśrayān |
commentary: That which is situated in the lower bowels is the apāna vāyu and by this vāyu faeces, urine, semen, foetus and menstrual fluid are brought down (and expelled) at appropriate times. Upon being vitiated, it produces serious diseases located in the bladder and rectum.

sanskrit_text: हाक्रदोषप्रमेहास्त्र व्यानापानप्रकीपजाः। कुपिताइचापि, देहं भिन्द्युरसंज्ञयम्। य गपत्
transliteration: hākradoṣapramehāstra vyānāpānaprakīpajāḥ | kupitāicāpi, dehaṃ bhindyurasaṃjñayam | ya gapat
commentary: Seminal disorders and abnormal urinary discharges owe their origin to the vitiation of vyāna and apāna vāyus. And when all the vāyus get simultaneously vitiated, the body undoubtedly gets destroyed.

sanskrit_text: अत ऊर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि नानास्थानान्तराश्रितः। बहुहाः कुपितो वायुविकारान् कुरुते हि यान्।
transliteration: ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi nānāsthānāntarāśritaḥ | bahuhāḥ kupito vāyuvikārān kurute hi yān |
commentary: Now I would further discourse upon those diseases which are produced by excessively vitiated vāyu situated in different places.

topic_heading: Effects of Vitiated Vāyu on Stomach
sanskrit_text: वायुरामाशये कुद्धश्छर्छादीन् कुरुते गदान्। मोहं मच्छाँ पियासां च हृद्ग्रहं पाइवेवदलाम्।
transliteration: vāyurāmāśaye kuddhaścherchādīn kurute gadān | mohaṃ macchāṃ piyāsāṃ ca hṛdgrahaṃ pāivevadalām |
commentary: When the vāyu situated in āmāśaya (the stomach) gets vitiated it produces vomiting etc., and also stupor, unconsciousness, thirst, constricting pain in the precordium and pain in the sides.

topic_heading: Effects of Vitiated Vāyu on the Intestines and Ear etc.
sanskrit_text: पक्वांशयस्थोऽःत्रकूजं हालं नाभौ करोति च। कृच्छ मृत्र पुरीषत्वमानाहं त्रिकवेदनाम। श्रोत्रादिष्विन्द्रियवधं कुर्यात् कुद्धः समीरणः
transliteration: pakvāṃśayastho'ḥtrakūjaṃ hālaṃ nābhau karoti ca | kṛccha mṛtra purīṣatvamānāhaṃ trikavedanām | śrotrādiṣvindriyavadhaṃ kuryāt kuddhaḥ samīraṇaḥ |
commentary: Vitiation of vayu situated in pakvāśaya (the intestines) causes gürgling, pain in the umbilical region, dysuria, difficulty in opening the bowels, abdominal distension and low back pain. Vitiated vāyu located in the ear etc. causes impairment of the respective sense organ.

topic_heading: Effects of Vitiated Vāyu on the Skin
sanskrit_text: वैवण्य स्फरणं रौक्ष्यं स प्तिं च मचमायनम। त्वक्स्थो निस्तोदनं कूर्यात त्वग्भेदं परिपोटनम्
transliteration: vaivaṇya spharaṇaṃ raukṣyaṃ sa ptiṃ ca macamāyanama | tvakstho nistodanaṃ kūryāta tvagbhedaṃ paripoṭanam |
commentary: Upon vitiation of the vāyu) situated in the skin, depigmentation, twitching, roughness, numbness, tingling, pins and needles and sensation of tearing and splitting of the skin are produced.

topic_heading: Effects of Vitiated Vāyu on Miscellaneous Sites
sanskrit_text: व्रणांइच रक्तगो, ग्रन्थीन् सहालान् मांससंश्रितः। मेद:श्रितः कुर्याद्ग्रन्थीन्मन्दरुजोऽव्रणानि। तथा सिराकुञ्चनपूरणम्। सिरागतः कुर्यत् हाल हालमाक्षेपणं तथा। स्तम्भकम्पौ स्नाय प्राप्तः हालहोफौ करोति च। हन्ति सन्धिगतः सन्धीन् अस्थिज्ञोषं प्रभेदं च कुर्याच्छूलं च तच्छितः। तथा मज्जगते रुक् च न कदाचित् प्रशाम्यति। अप्रवृत्तिः प्रवृत्तिर्वा विक्टता
transliteration: vraṇāṃica raktago, granthīn sahālān māṃsasaṃśritaḥ | meda:śritaḥ kuryādgranthīnmandarujo'vraṇāni | tathā sirākuñcanapūraṇam | sirāgataḥ kuryat hāla hālamākṣepaṇaṃ tathā | stambhakampau snāya prāptaḥ hālahophau karoti ca | hanti sandhigataḥ sandhīn asthijñoṣaṃ prabhedaṃ ca kuryācchūlaṃ ca tacchitaḥ | tathā majjagate ruk ca na kadācit praśāmyati | apravṛttiḥ pravṛttirvā vikṭatā
commentary: Upon vitiation of the vāyu situated in the blood it causes ulcers, in the muscles it causes painful knotty swellings and located in the fat it produces mildly painful glands without ulceration; upon getting into the veins it causes pain, contraction or engorgement; if it gets into the ligaments it causes stiffness, instability, pain and convulsions; if it gets into the joints, it causes pain and swelling and impairs its functions; if it gets into the bones, it causes bone atrophy and cracks and pain; and if it gets into the marrow it produces pain which never subsides. If it (vitiated vāyu) gets into the semen, discharge of the later ceases or it becomes abnormal.

topic_heading: Effects of Generalised Vitiation of Vāyu
sanskrit_text: हस्तपादशिरोधातुंस्तथा संचरति कमात्। व्याप्नुयाद्वाऽखिलं देहं वायः सर्वगतो नुणाम्। सर्वगः। स्तम्भनाक्षेपणस्वापश्रोफश्रालानि
transliteration: hastapādaśirodhātuṃstathā saṃcarati kamāt | vyāpnuyādvā'khilaṃ dehaṃ vāyaḥ sarvagato nuṇām | sarvagaḥ | stambhanākṣepaṇasvāpaśrophraśrālāni |
commentary: Upon generalized vitiation of the vāyu in the human beings, it circulates in their hands, feet, head and in the tissues respectively and gets diffused all over the body. Then it produces generalised stiffness, convulsions, numbness, swelling and pain.

topic_heading: Effects of Association of Vitiated Vāta With The Other Doṣas
sanskrit_text: स्थानेष्क्तेष् संमिश्रः संमिश्राः कुरुते रुजः। मारुतस्त्वमितान गदान। कुर्यदिवयवप्राप्तो स्य्र्वायौ पित्तसमन्विते। दाहसंतापमच्छा: हौत्यशोफग्रुत्वानि तस्मिन्नेव कफावते। सुचीभिरिव निस्तोदः स्पर्शद्वेषः प्रसप्तता। शेषाः पित्तविकाराः स्युर्मारुते शोणितान्विते।
transliteration: sthāneṣkteṣ saṃmiśraḥ saṃmiśrāḥ kurute ru jaḥ | mārutastvamitān gadān | kuryadivayavaprāpto syrvāyau pittasamanvite | dāhasaṃtāpamacchā: hautyasophagrutvāni tasminneva kaphāvate | sūcībhiriva nistodaḥ sparśadveṣaḥ prasaptatā | śeṣāḥ pittavikārāḥ syurmārute śoṇitānvite |
commentary: When the vitiated vāyu situated in the above mentioned regions gets associated with (pitta etc.), it produces mixed types (of afflictions); and when this vāyu reaches different organs, it produces different types of disorders in them. Upon the association of vāyu with pitta, burning sensation, hyperpyrexia and unconsciousness are produced. Upon its (vāyu) association with kapha, coldness, swelling and heaviness are produced. Upon the association of vāyu with śoṇita pricking sensation by needles, hyperaesthesia, numbness and the remaining disorders of vitiated pitta are produced.

topic_heading: Masking of Prāṇa Vāyu by Pitta and Kapha
sanskrit_text: प्राणे पित्तावते छर्दिर्दाहर्चैवोपजायते। दौर्बल्यं सदनं तन्द्रा वैवर्ण्यं च कफावृते
transliteration: prāṇe pittāvate chardirdāharcaivopajāyate | daurbalyaṃ sadanaṃ tandrā vaivarṇyaṃ ca kaphāvṛte
commentary: Upon masking of prāṇa vāyu by pitta vomiting and burning sensation are produced; and upon its masking by kapha, weakness, lethargy, drowsiness and discolouration are produced.

topic_heading: Union of Udāna Vāyu, Pitta and Kapha
sanskrit_text: पित्तसंयक्ते उदाने मच्छादाहस्पमक्लमाः। अस्वेदहर्षौ मन्दोऽग्निः शीतस्तम्भौ कफावृते
transliteration: pittasaṃyakte udāne macchādāhaspmaklamāḥ | asvedaharṣau mando'gniḥ śītastambhau kaphāvṛte
commentary: Upon union of udāna vāyu with pitta, unconsciousness, burning sensation, giddiness and tiredness are produced; and upon its union with kapha anhidrosis, weak digestion, horripilation, feeling of coldness, and stiffness are produced.

topic_heading: Union of Samāna Vāyu with Pitta and Kapha
sanskrit_text: समाने पित्तसंयुक्ते स्वेददाहौष्ण्यमुर्च्छनम्। कफाधिकं च विण्मूत्रं रामहर्षः कफावते
transliteration: samāne pittasaṃyukte svedadāhauṣṇyamurcchanam | kaphādhikaṃ ca viṇmūtraṃ rāmaharṣaḥ kaphāvate
commentary: Upon union of samāna vāyu with pitta, perspiration, burning sensation, feeling of heat and unconsciousness are produced; and upon its union with kapha excessive mucus comes with urine and stools and horripilation takes place.

topic_heading: Union of Apāna Vāyu with Pitta and Kapha
sanskrit_text: अपाने पित्तसंयक्ते दाहौष्ण्ये स्यादसृग्दरः। अधःकायग्रुत्वं च तस्मिन्नेव कफावृते
transliteration: apāne pittasaṃyakte dāhauṣṇye syādasṛgdar aḥ | adhaḥkāyagrutvaṃ ca tasminneva kaphāvṛte |
commentary: Upon union of apāna vāyu with pitta burning sensation, heat and menorrhagia and metrorrhagia are produced and upon masking by kapha heaviness in the lower half of the body is produced.

topic_heading: Masking of Vyāna Vāyu by Pitta and Kapha
sanskrit_text: व्याने पित्तावते दाहो गात्रविक्षेपणं क्लमः। प्रदर्भ गरूणि सर्वगात्राणि स्तम्भनं चास्थिपर्वणाम्। लिड्स कफावते व्याने चेष्टास्तम्भस्तथेव च।
transliteration: vyāne pittāvate dāho gātravikṣepaṇaṃ klamaḥ | pradarbha garūṇi sarvagātrāṇi stambhanaṃ cāsthiparvaṇām | liḍsa kaphāvate vyāne ceṣṭāstambhasthave ca |
commentary: Upon masking of vyāna vāyu by pitta, burning sensation, convulsions of limbs and tiredness are produced; and upon its masking by kapha symptoms of heaviness all over the body, stiffness in the bones and joints, and also cessation of all voluntary movements are produced.

sanskrit_text: प्रायशः सुकुमाराणां मिथ्याऽऽहारविहारिणाम। रोगाध्वप्रमदामद्यव्यायामैइचातिपीडनात्। ऋतुसात्म्यविपर्यासात् स्नेहादीनां च विभ्रमात्। अव्यवाये तथा स्थूले वातरक्तं प्रकुप्यति
transliteration: prāyaśaḥ sukumārāṇāṃ mithyā''hāravihāriṇāma | rogādhvapramadāmadyavyāyāmaiicātipīḍanāt | ṛtusātmyaviparyāsāt snehādīnāṃ ca vibhramāt | avyavāye tathā sthūle vātaraktaṃ prakupyati
commentary: Vāta-rakta (gout) occurs usually in the persons with delicate constitution and in the obese who take faulty diet or who lead a faulty life, who suffer from excessive sickness or fatigue due to excessive walking and excessive indulgence in wine, women and exercise, in those who lead a life opposite to that indicated according to seasons, who get defective oleation treatment etc. and in those who abstain from sexual intercourse.

topic_heading: Vitiation and Domination of Rakta by Vāṭa (Vāṭa-Rakta), Pitta and Kapha
sanskrit_text: हस्त्यइवोछ्ट्रेर्गच्छतोऽन्येशच वायुः क्रोपं म्रातः कारणैःसेविलेःस्वेः तोक्ष्प्पोर्णममलक्ष्पार्शाक्राद्रिभोज़्यः संताप्रार्थभूँवसा सेवितेदच। क्षिप्रं रक्तं क्रष्टिमायालि तच्च वायोमाग्र्म संरुणद्वचाझ आतः। ॠद्धोऽत्यथँ मार्गरोधात् स वायुरत्युद्रिक्तं दृषयेद्रक्तमाश्। दूषितेन तत्प्रावल्यादुच्यते चातस्वतम्’। तत् संपक्तं वायना तद्वत पित्त द्वाषतनासजाऽऽक्त इलेष्माद्वष्टी द्रापुतनस्ज्ञाŞऽक्तः
transliteration: hastyavochṭrergacchato'nyeśaca vāyuḥ kropaṃ mrātaḥ kāraṇaiḥsevileḥsveḥ | tokṣppoṇamamalakṣpārśākrādribhozyaḥ saṃtāprārthabhūṃvasā sevitedaca | kṣipraṃ raktaṃ kraṣṭimāyāli tacca vāyomāgrm saṃruṇadvacājha ātaḥ | ṛddho'tyathã mārgarodhāt sa vāyuratyudriktaṃ dṛṣayedraktamāś | dūṣitenataprāvalyāducyate cātasvatam’ | tat saṃpaktaṃ vāyanā tadvat pitta dvāṣatanāsajā''kta ileṣmādvaṣṭī drāputanasjñāŞ'ktaḥ
commentary: It is called vāta-rakta because of its (blood's) saturation with vāta and its predominance by the same; similarly the blood vitiated by pitta and the blood vitiated by kapha should also be known. Vāyu gets vitiated due to riding on an elephant, horse or camel, by the use of its (vāyu) other causative factors, by the use of bitter, hot, acidic, alkaline, vegetable and other eatables, and by repeated exposure to heat. The rakta becomes vitiated soon and it then obstructs the pathway of vāyu immediately. That vāyu due to obstruction in its pathway becomes more aggravated and further vitiates the already vitated blood at the same time.

topic_heading: Pedal Symptoms produced by the Dosas uniting with Rakta
sanskrit_text: स्पर्शोद्विग्नौ तोदर्भेदप्रशोषस्वापोपेतौ वातरकतेन पादौ n पित्तासग्भ्यामुग्रदाहौ भवेतामत्यंथोष्णौ रक्तद्वोफौ मूद्रू च। कण्डूमन्तौ श्रवेतशीतौ सशोफौ पीनस्तबंधौ श्रेष्मदुष्टेँ तु रक्ते। सर्वे द्वंप्टे शोणिते चीपि दोषाः स्वं स्वं रूपं पादयोर्वर्मयन्ति
transliteration: sparśodvignau todarbhedapraśoṣasvāpopetau vātaraktena pādau n pittāsagbhyāmugradāhau bhavetāmatyaṃthoṣṇau raktadvophau mūdrū ca | kaṇḍūmantau śravetaśītau saśophau pīnastabaṃdhau śreṣmaduṣṭeṃ tu rakte | sarve dvaṃpṭe śoṇite cīpi doṣāḥ svaṃ svaṃ rūpaṃ pādayorvarmayanti
commentary: Due to vāta-rakta, hyperaesthesia, pins and needles, tearing pain, dryness and numbness in the feet are produced. Due to association of pitta and rakta acute burning pain and very hot and red swelling occurs which is soft also. Combination of the vitiated slesmā with rakta produces itching, palor, coldness, swelling, thickened and firm (feet). Upon vitiation of all the dosas together along with rakta, each of them manifests its own features in the feet.

sanskrit_text: प्राग्रुपे शिथिलौ स्विन्नौ शीतलौ सविपर्ययौ। वैवर्ण्यतोदसप्तत्वग्रुत्वौषसमन्वितो
transliteration: prāgrupe śithilau svinau śītalau saviparyayau | vaivarṇyatodasaptatvagrutvauṣasamanvito
commentary: The prodromal features are slackness, perspiration, and coldness or the reverse of all these, in association with discolouration, pins and needles, numbness, heaviness and burning sensation (in the feet).

sanskrit_text: पादयोमृंलमास्थाय कदाचिद्धस्तयोरपि। आखोविषमिव कुद्धं तद्देहमनुसर्पति
transliteration: pādayomṛṃlamāsthāya kadāciddhastayorapi | ākhoviṣamiva kuddhaṃ taddehamanusarpati
commentary: This disease spreads all over the body like a virulent rat poison beginning from the sole of the feet or sometimes from the hands.

sanskrit_text: आजानस्फ टितं यच्च प्रभिन्नं प्रस्तुतं च यत्। प्राणमांसक्षयादिभिः। यज्ज छट उपद्रवहच शोणितं तदसाध्यं स्याद्याप्यं संवत्सरोत्थितम्।
transliteration: ājānaspha ṭitaṃ yacca prabhinnaṃ prastutaṃ ca yat | prāṇamāṃsakṣayādibhiḥ | yajja chaṭa upadravahaca śoṇitaṃ tadasādhyaṃ syādyāpyaṃ saṃvatsarotthitam |
commentary: That vāta-rakta in which exfoliation occurs upto knee, and also which cracks and in which discharge occurs, and which is associated with the complications of loss of vitality and flesh is incurable; that which is of one year's duration should be considered relievable only.

sanskrit_text: यदा तु धमनीः सर्वाः क्रपितोऽभ्येति मारुतः। मुहुमुंहुदेहं तदाक्षिपत्याश मुहुइचरः। इति स्मतः। मुहुमुहुस्तदाक्षेपादाक्षेपक
transliteration: yadā tu dhamanīḥ sarvāḥ krapito'bhyeti mārutaḥ | muhumuṃhudehaṃ tadākṣipatyāśa muhuicaraḥ | iti smataḥ | muhumuhustadākṣepādākṣepaka
commentary: When all the arteries become affected by the vitiated vāyu, it often results in quick and repeated convulsions throughout the body; because of the repeated convulsions, it is known as ākṣepaka.

sanskrit_text: सोऽपतानकसंज्ञो यः पातयत्यन्तराऽन्तरा।
transliteration: so'patānakasaṃjño yaḥ pātayatyantarā'ntarā |
commentary: That (disease) is called apatānaka in which (the convulsions) occur at repeated intervals.

sanskrit_text: कफान्वितो भृशं वायुस्तास्वेव यदि तिष्ठति। स दण्डवत् स्तम्भयति कृच्छो दण्डापतानकः।
transliteration: kaphānvito bhṛśaṃ vāyustāsvēva yadi tiṣṭhati | sa daṇḍavat stambhayati kṛccho daṇḍāpatānakaḥ |
commentary: If the vāyu mixed intimately with kapha gets fixed in those (vessels) the patient becomes stiff like a pole; the disease is called dandāpatānaka and is curable with difficulty.

sanskrit_text: हन्ग्रहस्तदाऽत्यर्थं सोऽन्नं कृच्छान्निषेवते
transliteration: hangra hastadā'tyarthaṃ so'nnaṃ kṛcchānniṣevate
commentary: Then serious lock jaw takes place and therefore food is taken with difficulty.

sanskrit_text: धनस्तुल्यं नमेद्यस्तु स धनःस्तम्भसंज्ञकः। अङ्गु लीगुल्फजठरहृद्वक्षोगलसंश्रितः। स्नायुप्रतानमनिलो यदाऽऽक्षिपति वे गवान्। विष्टब्धाक्षः स्तब्धहनुर्भग्नपाइवंः कफं वमन्। अभ्यन्तरं धनरिव यदा नमति मानवः। तदाऽस्याभ्यन्तरायामं कुरुते मारुतो बली। बाह्यस्नायुप्रतानस्थो बाह्यायामं करोति च।
transliteration: dhanastulyaṃ namedyastu sa dhanaḥstambhasaṃjñakaḥ | aṅgu līgulphajaṭharahṛdvakṣogalasaṃśritaḥ | snāyupratānamanilo yadā''kṣipati ve gavān | viṣṭabdhākṣaḥ stabdhahanurbhagnapāivaṃḥ kaphaṃ vaman | abhyantaraṃ dhanariva yadā namati mānavaḥ | tadā'syābhyantarāyāmaṃ kurute māruto balī | bāhyasnāyupratānastho bāhyāyāmaṃ karoti ca |
commentary: That in which the patient is bent like a bow is called dhanuhstambha. Two Types of Dhanustambha : (Abhyantarāyāma and Bāhyāyāma). When the powerfully vitiated vāyu situated in the toes, ankle, abdomen, heart, chest and neck causes spasm of their ligaments leading to fixed eyes, lock jaw, fractures in the sides and vomiting of mucus and bending the patient (ventrally) like a bow, the (disease) is called ābhyantarāyāma (emprosthotonos). When situated in the external ligaments (of the structures mentioned above), it causes bāhyāyāma (opisthotonos).

sanskrit_text: प्राहर्वक्षःकट्युरुभञ्जनम्। तमसाध्यं बधाः
transliteration: prāharvakṣaḥkaṭyurubhañjanam | tamasādhyaṃ badhāḥ
commentary: That (dhanuhstambha) is called incurable by the wise in which fractures of chest, lumber spine and thigh occur.

sanskrit_text: कफपित्तान्विती वायुर्वायुरेव च केवलः। कुर्यादाक्षेपकं त्वन्यं चतुर्थमभिघातजम्।
transliteration: kaphapittānvitī vāyurvāyureva ca kevalaḥ | kuryādākṣepakaṃ tvanyaṃ caturthamabhighātajam |
commentary: Vāyu in association with kapha or pitta or vāyu alone causes ākṣepaka; the fourth variety is traumatic in origin.

sanskrit_text: गर्भपातनिमित्तहच शोणितातिस्रवाच्च यः। अभिघातनिमित्तइच न सिध्यत्यपतानकः।
transliteration: garbhapātanimittahaca śoṇitātistavācca yaḥ | abhighātanimittaica na sidhyatyapatānakaḥ |
commentary: That apatānaka is incurable which is caused by abortion, excessive bleeding or trauma.

sanskrit_text: अधोगमाः संतिर्यग्गा धमनीरूर्ध्वदेहगाः। प्रकूपितोऽत्यर्थमातरिइवा प्रपद्यते। तदाऽन्यतरपक्षस्य सन्धिबन्धान् विमोक्षयन्। हन्ति पक्षं तमाहुर्हि पक्षाघातं भिषग्वराः। यस्य कृत्स्नं ततः पतत्यसून् वाऽपि त्यजत्यनिलपीडितः। कृच्छसाध्यतमं विद्रः। शुद्धवातहतं पक्ष क्षयहेत्रकम्। साध्यमन्येन संसृष्टमसाध्यं
transliteration: adhogamāḥ saṃtiryaggā dhamanīrūrdhvadehagāḥ | prakūpito'tyarthamātariivā prapadyate | tadā'nyatarapakṣasya sandhibandhān vimokṣayan | hanti pakṣaṃ tamāhurhi pakṣāghātaṃ bhiṣagvarāḥ | yasya kṛtsnaṃ tataḥ patatyasūn vā'pi tyajatyānilapīḍitaḥ | kṛcchasādhyatamaṃ vidraḥ | śuddhavāthataṃ pakṣa kṣayahetrakaṃ | sādhyamanyena saṃsṛṣṭamasādhyaṃ
commentary: When the excessively vitiated vāyu diffuses into the arteries going downwards, obliquely and upwards in the body, it loosens the supports of the joints on either side of the body, and causes paralysis of that same side; this is called hemiplegia by the best among the physicians. The patient afflicted by the vitiated vāyu, half of whose body gets paralysed or has sensory loss (suddenly) falls down or even leaves (this world). Hemiplegia caused by vāyu only is known to be curable with difficulty; when (it is caused by (vāyu) in association with others (pitta and kapha) it is curable; and it is incurable: if it is due to the wasting (of dhātus).

sanskrit_text: वायुरूध्वं व्रजेत् स्थानात् क्रपितो हृदयं शिरः। पीडफ्त्य ङ्रान्याक्षिपन्नमर्येच्च सः। राड़ो च निमीलिताक्षो निइचेष्टः स्तब्धाक्षो वाऽपि क़जति। निरुच्छ्वासंऽथ्यवा कृच्छादुच्छवस्यान्नष्टचतनः। स्वस्थः स्याद्धदये मँक्ते हचावृते तु प्रमुह्यात। कफान्वितैन’ वातेन जेय एषडिपतन्त्रक:
transliteration: vāyurūdhvaṃ vrajet sthānāt krapito hṛdayaṃ śiraḥ | pīḍaftya ṅrānyākṣipannamaryecca saḥ | rāḍo ca nimīlitākṣo niiceṣṭaḥ stabdhākṣo vā'pi kàjati | nirucchvāsaṃ'thyavā kṛcchāducchavasyānnaṣṭacatanaḥ | svasthaḥ syāddhdaye māṃkte hacāvṛte tu pramuhyāta | kaphānvitaina’ vātena jeya eṣaḍipatantraka:
commentary: The vitiated vāyu having gone upwards from its normal location produces pain in the heart, head and temples and produces convulsions and bending of the limbs; the eyes are closed and fixed, the person becomes listless and makes inarticulate sounds, is apnoec or has respiration with difficulty and looses his consciousness; normalcy is restored when the heart gets freed, and upon reversal unconsciousness sets in again; this is called apatantraka and is produced when the kapha gets mixed up with vāta.

sanskrit_text: दिवास्वप्नासनस्थानविवताध्वनिरीक्षणैः। मन्यास्तम्भं प्रकुरुते स एव इलेष्मणाऽऽवृतः
transliteration: divāsvapnāsanasthānavivatādhvanirīkṣaṇaiḥ | manyāstambhaṃ prakurute sa eva ileṣmaṇā''vṛtaḥ
commentary: Sleeping by day, unsuitable sitting and standing postures, and looking up obliquely produce manyāstambha; the same is due to mixing up of kapha with vāyu.

sanskrit_text: र्गभिणीसतिकाबालवद्वक्षीणेटवसकक्षये उच्चैर्याहरतोऽत्यथं खादतः कटिनानि वा। भाराद्विषमाच्छयनादपि। जम्भतो हसतो शिरोनासौष्ठचिबकललाटेक्षणसन्धिगः। अर्दयित्वाऽनिलो वक्रमादतं जनयत्यतः। वऋार्धं ग्रीवा चाप्यपवर्तते। शिरइचलति वाक्सड्झो नेत्रादीनां च वैकृतम्। ग्रीवाचिबकदन्तानां तस्मिन पाईवें तु वेदना। वेपथर्नेत्रमाविलम्। यस्याग्रजो रोमहर्षो वायरूध्वं त्वचि स्वापस्तादो मन्याहनुग्रहः। तर्मदितमिति प्राहुव्याधि व्याधिविशारदाः। क्षीणस्यानिमिषाक्षस्य प्रसक्ताव्यक्तभाषिणः। बाढं त्रिवषं वेपनस्य च। न सिध्यत्यदितं
transliteration: rgabhiṇīsatikābalavadvakṣīṇeṭavasakakṣaye uccairyāharato'tyathaṃ khādataḥ kaṭināni vā | bhārādviṣamācchayanādapi | jambhato hasato śironāsauṣṭhicibakalalāṭekṣaṇasandhigaḥ | ardayitvā'nilo vakramādataṃ janayatyataḥ | vaṛārdhaṃ grīvā cāpyapavartate | śiracalati vāksaḍjho netrādīnāṃ ca vaikṛtam | grīvācibakadantānāṃ tasmin pāiveṃ tu vedanā | vepatharnetramāvilam | yasyāgrajo romaharṣo vāyarūdhvaṃ tvaci svāpastādo manyāhanugrahaḥ | tarmaditamiti prāhuvyādhi vyādhiviśāradāḥ | kṣīṇasyānimiṣākṣasya prasaktāvyaktabhāṣiṇaḥ | bāḍhaṃ trivaṣaṃ vepanasya ca | na sidhyatyaditaṃ
commentary: In the pregnant women, in puerperium, in the young and the old, in the emaciated and in those who have lost blood; due to shouting excessively loudly or biting hard substances and also due to (excessive) laughter, yawning, carrying heavy loads and due to sleeping on uneven bed, the vitiated vāyu having reached the joints of head, nose, lips, chin, forehead and the eyes afflicts the face and produces facial paralysis. Symptoms of Ardita: Half of the face becomes twisted and the neck also rotates; there is instability of the head, aphasia, and deformity in the eyes etc; and there is pain in the sides of the neck, chin and teeth. Prodromal Symptoms: Its prodromal symptoms are horripilation, tremors, and muddy eyes; and the vitiated vāyu having gone upwards produces numbness of the skin locally as well as pins and needles in the skin and torticollis and lockjaw; this is called ardita disease by the specialists. Prognosis of Ardita: Ardita of the emaciated, of the one having fixed eyes and of one whose speech is continuously inarticulate, is not curable; as also when it is advanced, is of three years duration or when it is associated with tremors.

sanskrit_text: पाष्णिप्रत्यङ्गलीनां तु कण्डरा याऽनिलादिता। सक्न्थः क्षेपं निगृह्लीयाग्दृध्रसीति हि सा स्मृता
transliteration: pāṣṇipratyaṅgalīnāṃ tu kaṇḍarā yā'nilāditā | saknthaḥ kṣepaṃ nigṛhlīyāgdṛdhrasīti hi sā smṛtā
commentary: When the ligaments from the heel upto all the toes are afflicted by the vitiated vāyu, movements of the lower extremity get restricted; that is known as grdhrasi.

sanskrit_text: कपडरा बाहुप्रष्ठतः। तलप्रयङ्गु लीनां तु बाह्वोः कर्मक्षयकरी विश्वाचीति हि सा स्मता
transliteration: kapaḍarā bāhuprāṣṭhataḥ | talaprayaṅgu līnāṃ tu bāhvoḥ karmakṣayakarī viśvācīti hi sā smatā
commentary: When the ligaments of the palm including the fingers as well as those of the dorsal aspect of upper extremity (are afflicted by the vitiated vāta) movements of the upper extremity get restricted; that is known as visvācī.

sanskrit_text: वातशोंणितजः शोफो जान्मध्ये महारुजः। शिरः ऋोष्टुकपूर्व तु स्थूलः ॠोष्टुकमूर्धवत्
transliteration: vātaśoṇitajaḥ śopho jānmadhye mahārujaḥ | śiraḥ ṛoṣṭukapūrva tu sthūlaḥ ṛoṣṭukamūrdhavat
commentary: Excessively painful and big swelling in the knee like the head of jackal due to the vitiated vāta and śoṇita is called kro stukaśirsa.

sanskrit_text: वायुः कटचां स्थितः सक्थनः कण्डरामाक्षिपेद्यदा। खञ्जस्तदा भवेज्जन्तः, पड्मः सक्थ्नोर्द्वयोर्वधात्।
transliteration: vāyuḥ kaṭacāṃ sthitaḥ sakthanaḥ kaṇḍarāmākṣiped yadā | khañjastadā bhavejjantaḥ, paḍmaḥ sakthnordvayorvadhāt |
commentary: When the vitiated vāyu situated in the lumbar region afflicts the ligaments of the lower extremity, it is called khañja (lame) in the living beings; and when it cripples both the lower extremities it is known as pangu (Cripple).

sanskrit_text: प्रक्रामन् वेपते यस्तु खञ्जन्निव च गच्छति। कलायखञ्जं तं विद्यान्मवतसन्धिप्रबन्धनम्।
transliteration: prakrāman vepate yastu khañjanniva ca gacchati | kalāyakhañjaṃ taṃ vidyānmavatasandhiprabandhanam |
commentary: When there is trembling in taking the first few steps, limping and when organisation of the joint gets loose, it is known as kalāyakhanja.

sanskrit_text: न्यस्ते तु विषमं(मे) पादे रुजः कुर्यात् समीरणः। विज्ञेयः इत्येष खड़काश्रितः। वातकण्टक
transliteration: nyaste tu viṣamaṃ(me) pāde rujaḥ kuryāt samīraṇaḥ | vijñeyaḥ ityeṣa khaḍakāśritaḥ | vātakaṇṭaka
commentary: Walking on uneven ground causes pain in the heel due to the vāta situated in the heels; that is known as vāta kanṭaka.

sanskrit_text: पादयोः कुरुते दाहं पित्तासुक्सहितोऽनिलः। विशेषतश्चङ् ऋमणात् पाददाहं तमादिशेत्
transliteration: pādayoḥ kurute dāhaṃ pittāsukasahito'nilaḥ | viśeṣataścaṅ ṛmaṇāt pādadāhaṃ tamādiśet
commentary: When burning is caused in both the feet, specially on walking, due to the vitiated vāta alongwith pitta and rakta, that is known as pādadāha.

sanskrit_text: हृष्यतहचरणौ यस्य भवतहच प्रसप्तवत। पादहर्षः स विज्ञेयः कफवातप्रकोपजः
transliteration: hṛṣyatahacaraṇau yasya bhavatahaca prasaptavata | pādaharṣaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ kaphavātaprakopajaḥ
commentary: When there is tingling and numbness in the feet due to the vitiated vāta alongwith kapha, that is known as pādaharṣa.

sanskrit_text: अंसदेशस्थितो वायः शोषयित्वांऽसबन्धनम्। सिराइचाकुञ्च्य तत्रस्थो जनयत्यवबहुकम्।
transliteration: aṃsadeśasthito vāyaḥ śoṣayitvāṃ'sabandhanam | sirāicākuñcya tatrastho janayatyavabahukam |
commentary: The vitiated vāyu situated in the shoulder region causes wasting of the shoulder joint and it also causes the contraction of veins situated therein, thus producing avabāhuka.

sanskrit_text: स्रोतो वायरावत्य तिष्‍ठति। शब्दवहं यदा शद्धः इलेष्मान्वितो वाऽपि बाधिर्य तेन जायते
transliteration: sroto vāyarāvatya tiṣṭhati | śabdavahaṃ yadā śaddhaḥ ileṣmānvito vā'pi bādhairya tena jāyate
commentary: When vāyu alone or with kapha covers and gets located in the acoustic channels, it produces deafness.

sanskrit_text: हनुसुङ्वशिरोग्रीवं यस्य भिन्दन्निवानिलः। कर्णश्लं तद्रच्यते। कर्णयोः कुरुते हालं
transliteration: hanusuṅvaśirogrīvaṃ yasya bhindannivānilaḥ | karṇaślaṃ tadracyate | karṇayoḥ kurute hālaṃ
commentary: When there is tearing sensation in the jaw, temple, head and neck and pain in both the ears due to the vitiated vāyu, it is called karṇaśūla.

sanskrit_text: आवृत्य सकर्फो वायुर्धमनीः शब्दवाहिनीः। नरान् करोत्यक्रियकान्मूकमिन्मिणगद्गदान्।
transliteration: āvṛtya sakarpho vāyurdhamanīḥ śabdavāhinīḥ | narān karotyakriyakānmūkaminmiṇagadgadān |
commentary: When the speech carrying channels get blocked up by the vitiated vāyu alongwith kapha, it disables the persons and produces aphasia, nasal twang and stammering.

sanskrit_text: अधो या वेदना याति वर्चोमूत्राहायोत्थिता। भिन्दतीव गुदोपस्थं सा तूनीत्यभिधीयते। गदोपस्थोत्थिता सैव प्रतिलोमविर्सपिणी। वेगैः पक्वाशयं याति प्रतितूनीति सा स्मृताः।
transliteration: adho yā vedanā yāti varcomūtrāhāyotthitā | bhindatīva gudopasthaṃ sā tūnītyabhidhīyate | gadopasthotthitā saiva pratilomavirspiṇī | vegaiḥ pakvāśayaṃ yāti pratitūnīti sā smṛtāḥ |
commentary: When the pain arising from the rectum and urinary bladder travels down and produces tearing sensation in the anus and the genitals that, is known as tūnī. The same (pain), when arises from the anus and the genitals and travels in the opposite direction reaching the colon forcefully, is known as pratitūnī.

sanskrit_text: साटोपमत्यग्ररुजमाध्मातमुदर भराम। आध्मानमिति जानीयाद्वोरं वातनिरोधंजम्।
transliteration: sāṭopamatyagrarujamādhmātamudara bharāma | ādhmānamiti jānīyādvoraṃ vātanirodhaṃjam |
commentary: Very severe pain accompanied by borborygmi and excessive distension of abdomen is produced due to severe obstruction of vāta and is known as ādhmāna.

sanskrit_text: तदेवामाशयोत्थितम्। विमक्तपाहर्वहदयं प्रत्याध्मानं विजानीयात् कफव्याकुलितानिलम्।
transliteration: tadevāmāśayotthitam | vimaktapāharvahadayaṃ pratyādhmānaṃ vijānīyāt kaphavyākulitānilam |
commentary: When the sides and the precordium are free and (distension) originates from the stomach due to the vitiated vāta with kapha, it is known as pratyādhmāna.

sanskrit_text: अष्ठीलावर्द्धनं ग्रन्थिमर्ध्वमायतमन्नतम्। वाताष्ठीलां विजानीयादबहिर्मार्गावरोधिनीम्।
transliteration: aṣṭhīlāvarddhanaṃ granthimardhvamāyatamannatam | vātāṣṭhīlāṃ vijānīyādabahirmārgāvarodhinīm |
commentary: The gland which is organised like round stone, which enlarges upwards and is bulging and which causes obstruction to the external passages, is known as vātaṣṭhīlā.

sanskrit_text: एनामेव रुजायक्तां वातविण्मत्ररोधिनीम। प्रत्यष्ठीलामिति वदेज्जठरे तिर्यगृत्थिताम्।
transliteration: enāmeva rujāyaktāṃ vātaviṇmatrarodhinīma | pratyaṣṭhīlāmiti vadejjaṭhare tiryagṛtthitām |
commentary: The same, when associated with pain causes obstruction to the flatus, faeces and urine, is known as pratyasthilā and it grows obliquely towards the abdomen.

sanskrit_text: अथातोऽर्शसां निदानं व्याख्यास्यामः।
transliteration: athāto' rśasāṃ nidānaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ |
commentary: Now we would expound upon 'The Diagnosis of Piles'.

sanskrit_text: यथोवाच भगवान् धन्वन्तरिः
transliteration: yathovāca bhagavān dhanvantariḥ
commentary: As was described by Lord Dhanvantari.

sanskrit_text: षडर्मांसि भवन्ति वातपित्तकफशोणितसन्निपातैः सहजानि चेति
transliteration: ṣaḍarmāṃsi bhavanti vātapittakaphaśoṇitasannipātaiḥ sahajāni ceti
commentary: Piles are of six types—due to vāta, pitta, kapha, śonita and due to all the doṣas together and the hereditary ones.

sanskrit_text: तत्रानात्मवतां यथोक्तः प्रकोपर्णविरुद्धाध्यशनस्त्रीप्रसड्ग्रेत्कट- कासनपुष्ठयानवेगविधारणादिभिविशेषःप्रकुपिता दोषा एक्शो द्विश: समस्ताः शोणितसहिता वा यथोवतं प्रसताः प्रधानधमनीरनप्रपद्याधो ग्दवलीर्मासप्ररोहाञ्जनयन्ति विशेषतो गदमागम्य प्रदुष्य गत्वा त्णकाष्ठोपललोष्ठवस्त्रादिभिः शीतोदकसंस्पर्शनाद्वा मन्दाग्नेः, तथा कन्दाः परिवुद्धिमासादयन्तिः, तान्यर्शांसीत्याचक्षते
transliteration: tatrānātmavatāṃ yathoktaḥ prakopaṇaviruddhādhy aśanastrīprasaḍgretkaṭ- kāsana puṣṭh yānavegavidhāraṇādibhiviśeṣaḥprakupitā doṣā ekśo dviśaḥ samastāḥ śoṇitasahitā vā yathovataṃ prasatāḥ pradhānadhamanīranaprapadyādho gdavalīrmāsaprarohāñjanayanti viśeṣato gadamāgamya praduṣya gatvā tṇakāṣṭhopalal oṣṭhavastrādibhiḥ śītodakasaṃsparśanādvā mandāgneḥ, tathā kandāḥ parivuddhimāsādayantiḥ, tānyarśāṃsītyācakṣate
commentary: Now, the various causes as described earlier which excite the doṣas in those who are not self-possessed and in those who take contradictory foods, eat again before the last meal has been digested, do (excessive) sexual intercourse, (in those who are accustomed to) squatting posture, ride on the back of an animal and inhibit the natural evacuatory reflexes etc., aggravate one, two or all the doṣas with or without the involvement of śoṇita. As described earlier, the doṣas spread, having entered the main artery, go down and having reached the rectum afflict its walls and produce fleshy excrescences specially in the dyspeptic. And by coming into contact with straw, wood, stone, lump (of clay) and clothings etc. or with cold water, the swellings grow in size alround; and these are known as piles.

sanskrit_text: तन्त्र स्थलान्त्रप्रतिबद्धमर्धपञ्चाङ्वलं गुदमाह्वः, तस्मिन् वलयस्ति- स्रोऽध्यर्धाङ्गलान्तरसंभूताः प्रवाहणी विंसर्जनी संवरणी चेति चतुर- ङ्गलायताः, सर्वास्तिर्यगेका ड्गलोच्छिताः।। हा, ड्रावर्तनिभाइचार्पि उपर्युपरि संस्थिताः। गजतालनिभाइचापि वर्णतः संप्रकीर्तिताः। रोमान्तेभ्यो यवाध्यर्धो ग्रदौष्ठः परिकीर्तितः। प्रथमा तु गर्दोष्ठादड्वलमात्रे
transliteration: tantra sthālāntrapratibaddhamardhapañcāṅvalaṃ gudamāhvaḥ, tasmin valayasti- sro'dhyardhāṅgalāntarasaṃbhūtāḥ pravāhaṇī viṃsarjanī saṃvaraṇī ceti catura- ṅgalāyatāḥ, sarvāstiryagekā ḍgalocchitāḥ || hā, ḍrāvartanibhāicārpi uparyupari saṃsthitāḥ | gajatālanibhāicāpi varṇataḥ saṃprakīrtitāḥ | romāntebhyo yavādhyardho gra dauṣṭhaḥ parikīrtitaḥ | prathamā tu gardoṣṭhādaḍvalamātre
commentary: Now the portion just distal to the large bowel for four and a half fingers is known as the anus. There are three sphincters at intervals of one and a half fingers each, known as pravāhinī, visarjanī, and saṃvarṇī and are four fingers in diameter. All of them project obliquely for one finger. And also they are spiral like a conch and are situated one above the other. They have also been described to be of the colour of the palate of an elephant. The anal lips have been described to be one and a half yava (barley) from the end of the hair-line. Thus the first sphincter is one finger above the anal lips.

sanskrit_text: तेषां तु भविष्यतां पूर्वरूपाणि—अन्नेऽश्रद्धा कृच्छात् पक्तिरम्लोका : परिदाहो विष्टरूभ: पिपासा सक्थिसदनसाटोप: काइयमुद्गारबाहुल्य- सक्ष्णोः इवयथरन्त्रकजन ग्रदपरिकर्तनमाहाड्रा पाण्डरोगग्रहणीदोष- शोषाणां कासइवासो बलहानिर्भ्रमस्तन्द्रा निद्रेन्द्रियदौर्बल्यं च। जातेष्वेतान्येव लक्षणानि प्रव्यक्ततराणि भवन्ति
transliteration: teṣāṃ tu bhaviṣyatāṃ pūrvarūpāṇi—anne'śraddhā kṛcchāt paktiramlokā : paridāho viṣṭarūbhaḥ pipāsā sakthisadanasāṭopa: kāiyamudgārabāhulya- sakṣṇoḥ ivayatharantrakajana gra daparikartanama hāḍrā pāṇḍarogagrahaṇīdoṣa- śoṣāṇāṃ kāsaivāso balahānirbhramastand rā nidrendriyadaurbalyaṃ ca | jāteṣvetānyeva lakṣaṇāni pravyaktatarāṇi bhavanti
commentary: These would be their prodromal features-dislike for food, difficulty in digestion, sour eructations, burning pain, fullness of abdomen, thirst, tiredness in the legs, meteorism, emaciation, excessive belching, swelling of the eyes, borborygmi, feeling of cutting pain around the anus, suspicion of anaemia, sprue and consumption, cough, asthma, loss of strength, disorientation, drowsiness, sleepiness, and diminished perception of senses. When (piles) are produced, these very symptoms become evidently manifest.

sanskrit_text: तत्र मारुतात् परिश्रष्कारुणविवर्णानि विषममध्यानि कदम्बप्रष्प- तुण्डिकेरीनाडीमुकुलसूचीमुखाकृतीनि च भवन्ति , तैरुपद्रुतः सशूल संहतमुपवेश्यते, कटीपष्ठपार्श्वमेढ्गुदनाभिप्रदशेषु चास्य वेदना भवन्ति, गुल्माष्ठीलाप्लीहोदराणि चास्य तन्निमित्तान्येव भवन्ति, कृष्णत्वङ नख- नयनदशनवदनमूत्रपुरीषइच पुरुषो भवति
transliteration: tatra mārutāt pariśraṣkāruṇavivarṇāni viṣamamadhyāni kadambapraṣpa- tuṇḍikerīnāḍīmukulasūcīmukhākṛtīni ca bhavanti , tairapadrutaḥ saśūla saṃhatamupaveśyate, kaṭīpaṣṭhapārśvameḍgudanābhipradaśeṣu cāsya vedanā bhavanti, gulmāṣṭhīlāplīhodarāṇi cāsya tannimittānyeva bhavanti, kṛṣṇatvaṅ nakha- nayanadaśanavadanamūtrapurīṣaica puruṣo bhavati
commentary: Now, the vāṭika (piles) are dry, reddish or discoloured, irregular in the centre, are like the flowers of kadamba or of the wild cotton plant, are tubular, bud like or are like the point of a needle in appearance. One afflicted by these (piles) defecates painfully and also has pain in the waist, back, sides, penis, rectum and in the umbilical region; abdominal swelling, prostatic and splenic enlargements are produced due to them and the patient's skin, nails, eyes, teeth, face, urine and stool become blackish.

sanskrit_text: पित्ताम्नीलाग्राणि तनूनि विसर्पीणि पीतावभासानि यक्वत्प्रकाशानि श्कजिह्वासंस्थानानि यवमध्यानि जलौकोवक्वसदृशानि प्रविल्मानि च भवन्ति, तैरूपद्रुतः सदाहं सरुधिरमतिसार्यते, ज्वरदाहपिपासामुच्छा- इचास्योपद्रवा भवन्ति, पीतत्वङनखनयनदशनवदनमूत्रपुरीषहच पुरुषो अवति
transliteration: pittāmnīlāgrāṇi tanūni visarpīṇi pītāvabhāsāni yakvatprakāśāni śkajihvāsaṃsthānāni yavamadhyāni jalaukōvakvasadṛśāni pravilmāni ca bhavanti, tairūpadrutaḥ sadāhaṃ sarudhiramatisāryate, jvaradāhapipāsā mucchā- icāsyopadravā bhavanti, pītatvaṅanakhanayanadaśanavadanamūtrapurīṣahaca puruṣo avati
commentary: The piles caused by (vitiated) pitta are blue in their presenting part and are slender, mobile, pale to look at and shine like liver; their shape is like that of a parrots tongue; they are barley (spindle) shaped in the middle, are similar to the mouth of a leech and are moist. One afflicted by them passes loose motions with blood accompanied with burning sensation. Fever, burning sensation, thirst, and fainting are its complications; and the patient's skin, nails, eyes, teeth, face, urine and stool become yellow.

sanskrit_text: इलेष्मजानि इवेतानि महामूलानि स्थिराणि व्रत्तानि स्निग्धानि पाण्डूनि करीरपनसास्थिगोस्तनाकाराणि, न भिद्यन्ते न स्रवन्ति कप्डूबहुलानि च भवन्ति, मांसघांवनप्रकाशमतिसार्यते, तरुप्रद्वतः सइलटमाणमनलप शोफशोतज्वरारोच्नकाविपाकशिरोगौरवाणि तन्निमित्तान्येव चास्य भवन्ति, शुक्लत्वइनखनयनदशनवदनमूत्रपुरीषइच पुरुषो भवति
transliteration: ileṣmajāni ivetāni mahāmūlāni sthirāṇi vrattāni snigdhāni pāṇḍūni karīrapanasāsthigostanākārāṇi, na bhidyante na sravanti kapḍūbahulāni ca bhavanti, māṃsaghāṃvanaprakāśamatisāryate, tarupradvataḥ sailatamāṇamanalapa śophaśotajvarārocnakavipākaśi rogauravāṇi tannimittānyeva cāsya bhavanti, śuklatvainanakhanayanadaśanavadanamūtrapurīṣaica puruṣo bhavati
commentary: The piles produced by (vitiated) śleṣma are whitish, broad based, fixed, rounded, smooth and yellowish-white; they are like karīra sprout or the kernel of a panasa fruit or are like the teat of a cow. They neither burst nor discharge but cause excessive itching. One afflicted by them passes copious mucus in their motions which are frequent and look like the washings of meat. Oedema, fever with rigor, dislike for food, indigestion and feeling of heaviness in the head occur due to these; and the patient's skin, nails, eyes, teeth, face, urine and stool become white.

sanskrit_text: न्यग्रोधप्ररोहविद्रमकाकणन्तिकाफलसदृशानि पित्त- रवंतजानि यदाऽवगाढपुरीषपीडितानि भवन्ति लक्षणानि तदाऽत्यथं चे होणिताति- चातिप्रवत्तौ दुष्टमनल्पमसूक् सहसा विसूजन्ति, तस्य योगोपद्रवा भवन्ति
transliteration: nyagrodhaprarohavidramakākaṇantikāphalasadṛśāni pitta- ravaṃtajāni yadā'vagāḍhapurīṣapīḍitāni bhavanti lakṣaṇāni tadā'tyathaṃ ce hoṇitāti- cātipravattau duṣṭamanalpamask sahasa visūjanti, tasya yogopadravā bhavanti
commentary: Raktaja piles are like the sprouts of a banyan tree or are like coral or like the fruit of kākaṇantikā and their clinical features resemble those of paittika piles. When they are pressed by the hard stools, excessively vitiated and copious amount of blood is suddenly passed; and complications pertaining to excessive bleeding set in if this continues for long.

sanskrit_text: सन्निपातजानि सर्वदोषलक्षणयक्तानि
transliteration: sannipātajāni sarvadoṣalakṣaṇayaktāni
commentary: The piles due to vitiation of all the doṣas together are associated with the clinical features of (piles produced by) all the doṣas.

sanskrit_text: तेषां द्रष्ट होणित शुक्रनिमितानि, दोषत सहजान एथ कर्तव्यं, विशेषतहचैतानि दुर्दर्दर्शनानि परुषाणि पांसनि प्रसाधन दारुणान्यन्तर्मुखानि, सिरासन्ततगात्रा- तैरुपद्रतः क्रशोऽल्पभक् sल्पप्रजः क्षीणरेताः क्षामस्वरः क्रोधनोऽल्पाग्निप्राणः परमलसइच, तथा घ्राणशिरोडक्षिनासाध्रवणरागी, सततमन्त्रकूजाटापहहदयोपलेपारो- चकप्रभंतिभिः पीडचते
transliteration: teṣāṃ draṣṭa hoṇita śukranimitāni, doṣata sahajāna etha kartavyaṃ, viśeṣatahacaitāni durdarda rśanāni paruṣāṇi pāṃsani prasādhana dāruṇānyantarmukhāni, sirāsantatagātrā- tairupadrutaḥ kraśo'lpabhak slpaprajaḥ kṣīṇaretāḥ kṣāmasvaraḥ krodhano'lpāgniprāṇaḥ paramalasaica, tathā ghrāṇaśiroḍakṣināsādhravaṇarāgī, satatamantrakūjāṭāpahahadayop alepāro- cakaprabhaṃtibhiḥ pīḍacate
commentary: The hereditary piles are due to the vitiation of sperm and ovum; they should also be treated according to the doṣa involved, Moreover, these are seen with difficulty, are rough, greyish, extremely painful and have their mouth pointing internally. One suffering from these is thin, eats less, has prominent veins over the entire body, has only a few offsprings, oligospermia, feeble voice, irritability, weak digestion and vitality and excessive lethargy; he usually suffers from olfactory diseases and diseases of the head, eyes, nose and ear. The patient always suffers from borborygmi, meteorism, feeling of heaviness in the heart and has no relish for food etc.

topic_heading: Prognosis (Based on the Extent of Piles)
sanskrit_text: भवति 'चात्र---- प्रतिकुर्य द्विद्विषग्वरः। बाह्यमध्यवलिस्थानां अन्तर्वेलिसमुत्थानां प्रत्याख्यायाचरेत् क्रियाम
transliteration: bhavati 'cātra---- pratikurya dvidviṣagvaraḥ | bāhyamadhyavalisthānāṃ antarvelisamutthānāṃ pratyākhyāyācaret kriyāma
commentary: The (following verse) has been quoted in this context: The piles situated in the regions of lower and middle sphincters should be treated by the good doctor; whereas, those situated in the region of upper sphincter should be managed after giving due warning of their bad prognosis.

topic_heading: Pile like Fleshy Excrescences at Other Parts of the Body
sanskrit_text: प्रक्रपितास्त्र दोषा मेढ़मभिप्रपन्ना सांসহােणिते प्रद्वष्य क्रणड तस्मिंग्रहच क्षते जनयन्ति, ततः दुष्टमांसजाः प्ररोहाः पिच्छिलरुधिरस्राविणो जायन्ते कूर्चकिनोऽभ्यन्त- रमपरिष्टाद्वा, ते तु योनि- शेफो विनाशयन्त्युपघनन्ति च्च पंस्त्वं, मभिप्रपन्नाः दुर्गन्धान् पिच्छिलरुधिरस्राविणइछत्राकारान् सुकुमाराज् र्ते तु योनिमुपधनत्यार्तवं च, नाभिमभिप्रपन्ना: करीराञ्जनयन्ति, करीराञ्जनयन्ति, सुकुमारान् दुर्गन्धान् पिच्छिलान् गण्डूपदमुखसद्रशान् श्रोत्राक्षिघ्राणवदनेष्वर्शास्यपनिर्वर्तयन्ति, एवोध्वमागताः तन त कर्णजेषु बाधिय शूलं पूतिकर्णता च, नेत्रजेषु वर्त्मावरोधो वेदना स्रावो घ्राणजेष् प्रतिश्यायोऽतिमात्रं क्षवथः कच्छोच्छवासता दशननाशश्च, पूतिनस्य साननासिकवाक्यत्वं शिरादुःखं च, वक्रजेष कण्ठौष्ठतालूनाम- न्यतर्मस्मिस्तैर्गद्गदवाक्यता भवन्ति रसाज्ञानं मुखरोगाइच
transliteration: prakrapitāstra doṣā meḍhamabhiprapannā sāṃsahaṇaite pradvyaṣya kraṇada tasmiṃgraha ca kṣate janayanti, tataḥ duṣṭamāṃsajāḥ prarohāḥ picchilarudhirasrāviṇo jāyante kūrcakino'bhyanta- ramapariṣṭādvā, te tu yoni- śepho vināśayantyupaghananti cca paṃstvaṃ, mabhiprapannā durgandhān picchilarudhirasrāviṇaicchatrākārān sukumārāj rte tu yonimupadhanatyārtavaṃ ca, nābhimabhiprapannā: karīrāñjanayanti, karīrāñjanayanti, sukumārān durgandhān picchilān gaṇḍūpadamukhasadrśān śrotrākṣighrāṇavadaneṣvarśās yapanirvartayanti, evodhvamāgatāḥ tana ta karṇajeṣu bādhiya śūlaṃ pūtikarṇatā ca, netrajeṣu vartmāvarodho vedanā srāvo ghrāṇajeṣ pratiśyā yo'timātraṃ kṣavathaḥ kacchocchavāsatā daśananāśaśca, pūtinasyasān anāsikavākyatvaṃ śirāduḥkhaṃ ca, vakrajeṣ kaṇṭhauṣṭhatālūnāma- nyatarmasmistairgadgadavākyatā bhavanti rasājñānaṃ mukharogāica
commentary: Now, the vitiated doṣas having reached the penis and having afflicted the muscles and blood produce itching. Then due to itching, ulcers are produced; and in those ulcers vitiated fleshy excrescences with a sero-sanguinous discharge originate; they are like a broom and are situated inside or externally. They definitely damage the penis and destroy the potency also. And the vitiated doṣas having reached the female genitals produce delicate, foul smelling,'and umbrella shaped buds with a sero-sanguinous discharge. They definitely destroy the vagina as well as the menstruation. And the vitiated doṣas having reached the umbilical region produce delicate, foul smelling, slimy buds similar to the mouth of earthworms. And those vitiated doṣas having spread upwards may produce pile like lesions in the ears, eyes, nose and mouth. Now, in the ears it produces deafness, earache, and pus discharge; in the eyes it produces inability to open the eyelids, pain, discharge and blindness; in the nose it produces cold, excessive sneezing, difficulty in breathing, pus discharge from the nose, nasal twang in the speech and headache; and in the mouth it causes diseases of the lips, palate and of other parts, indistinct speech, loss of taste and other diseases of the oral cavity.

sanskrit_text: व्यानस्तु प्रकुपितः इलेष्माणं परिगृह्य बहिः स्थिराणि कीलवद- र्मांसी निर्वतयति, तानि चर्मकीलान्यर्मांसीत्याच्वक्षते। भवन्ति चात्र—— तेष् कीलेष् निरतोदो मारुतेनोपजायते। इलेष्मणा त्र सवर्णत्वं ग्रन्थित्वं च विनिदिशेत्। पित्तशोणितजं रौक्ष्यं कृष्णत्वं इलक्ष्णता तथा। समदीर्णस्वरत्वं च चर्मकीलस्य लक्षणम्। अर्शांसि लक्षणं व्यासादुवतं सामान्यतस्तु यत्। तत्सर्व प्राग्विर्निदेष्टात्साधये
transliteration: vyānastu prakupitaḥ ileṣmāṇaṃ parigṛhya bahiḥ sthirāṇi kīlavad- rmāṃsī nirvatayati, tāni carmakīlānyarmāṃsītyācvakṣate | bhavanti cātra—— teṣ kīleṣ niratodo mārutenopajāyate | ileṣmaṇā tra savarṇatvaṃ granthitvaṃ ca vinidiśet | pittasśoṇitajaṃ raukṣyaṃ kṛṣṇatvaṃ ilakṣṇatā tathā | samadīrṇasvaratvaṃ ca carmakīlasya lakṣaṇam | arśāṃsi lakṣaṇaṃ vyāsāduvataṃ sāmānyatastu yat | tatsarva prāgvirnideṣṭātsādhaye
commentary: The vitiated vyāna vāyu in association with kapha produces firm and nail shaped piles externally; they are known as carmakīla piles (warts). The following verses have been quoted in this context: In those warts pain is produced due to the vāyu; and it is said that the colour and nodularity are due to śleṣmā. Whereas pitta and śoṇita produce dryness, blackness, glossiness and excessive roughness over the entire surface of the carmakīla. Thus, these are the clinical features of piles in general discoursed in detail. All these piles should be managed by a good doctor in the way described earlier.

sanskrit_text: अर्शःस दृश्यते रूपं यदा दोषद्वयस्य तु। संसर्ग तं विजानीयात् संसर्गः स च षड्विधः
transliteration: arśaḥsa dṛśyate rūpaṃ yadā doṣadvayasya tu | saṃsarga taṃ vijānīyāt saṃsargaḥ sa ca ṣaḍvidhaḥ
commentary: When features of two doṣas are seen together in a pile, it should be known as a samsarga pile; and those samarga piles are of six types.

topic_heading: Further Considerations on the Prognosis of Piles
sanskrit_text: त्रिदोषाण्यल्पलिङ्वानि याप्यानि तु विनिदेशेत्। यान्याश्रितानि च। द्वन्द्वजानि द्वितीयायां वलौ कूच्छसाध्यानि तान्याहः परिसंवत्सराणि च। वर्जयेत। सहजानि तु सन्निपातसमत्थानि
transliteration: tridoṣāṇyalpaliṅvāni yāpyāni tu vinideśet | yānyāśritāni ca | dvandvajāni dvitīyāyāṃ valau kūcchasādhyāni tānyāhaḥ parisaṃvatsarāṇi ca | varjayet | sahajāni tu sannipātasamatthāni
commentary: (Piles) produced by the three doṣas seperately as well as those having minor symptoms only, should be considered palliable. Those (piles) produced by a combination of two doṣas or those situated in the region of the middle sphincter and those of more than one year's duration have been said to be curable with difficulty. Those (piles) produced by all the doṣas together and the hereditary ones should be discarded (from treatment as incurable).

sanskrit_text: सर्वाः स्यर्वलयो येषां दुर्नामभिरुपद्रताः। वायरपानः सम्निवर्तते। तैस्त्र प्रतिहतो तंती व्यानेन संड्रम्य ज्योंतिमंदगंति देहिनाम्।
transliteration: sarvāḥ syarvalayo yeṣāṃ durnāmabhirapadratāḥ | vāyarapānaḥ samnivartate | taistra pratihato taṃtī vyānena saṃḍramya jyontimaṃdagaṃti dehinām |
commentary: Those in whom all the sphincters are affected by the (notorious) piles, the apāna vāyu gets obstructed and it does not come out; then, in association with vāyu (vyāna) it weakens the metabolic fire in the human being.

sanskrit_text: अथातोऽइमरीणां निदानं व्याख्यास्यामः
transliteration: athāto'imariṇāṃ nidānaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ
commentary: Now we would expound upon' The Diagnosis of Urinary Calculi'.

sanskrit_text: यथोवाच भगवान् धन्वन्तरिः
transliteration: yathovāca bhagavān dhanvantariḥ
commentary: As was described by Lord Dhanvantari.

sanskrit_text: चतस्रोऽइमर्यो भवन्ति, इलेष्माधिष्ठानाः, तद्यथा—इलेष्मणा, वातेन, पिसेन, हाक्रेण चेति
transliteration: catasro'imaryo bhavanti, ileṣmādhiṣṭhānāḥ, tadyathā—ileṣmaṇā, vātena, pisena, hākreṇa ceti
commentary: The urinary calculi are of four types. Śleṣmā is the basis of all. They are as follows : those caused by śleṣmā, vāta, pitta and śukra.

sanskrit_text: तत्रासंशोधनशीलस्यापथ्यकारिणः प्रकुपितः इलेटमा मत्र- संपक्तोनप्रविहय बस्तिमइमरीं जनयति
transliteration: tatrāsaṃśodhanaśīlasyāpathyakāriṇaḥ prakupitaḥ ileṭamā matra- saṃpaktonapravihaya bastimimarīṃ janayati
commentary: Now, in those who do not observe proper cleansing procedures and in those who are indiscrete regarding their dietary habits, the śleṣmā gets aggravated and mixed with urine enters the urinary bladder and therein it produces calculi.

sanskrit_text: तासां पूर्वरूपाण—ज्वरा बस्तिपीडारोचकौ म्त्रकृच्छं बस्ति- शिरोम्ब्क्रोफसां वेदना क्टच्छावसादा बस्तगन्धित्वं मंत्रस्येति। यथास्ववदनावण द्रष्ट सान्द्रमथाविलम्। पुर्वरूपेऽइमनः क्रच्छान्मूत्रं सृजति मानवः।
transliteration: tāsāṃ pūrvarūpāṇa—jvarā bastipīḍārocakau mtrakṛcchaṃ basti- śirombkrophasāṃ vedanā kṭacchāvasādā bastagandhitvaṃ maṃtrasyeti | yathāsvavadanāvaṇa draṣṭa sāndramathāvilam | purvarūpe'imanaḥ kracchānmūtraṃ sṛjati mānavaḥ |
commentary: The premonitary symptoms of urinary calculi are fever, pain in the bladder region, dislike for food, dysuria, pain in the region of bladder neck, scrotum and penis, exhaustion due to pain and goat like smell in the urine. During the prodromal stage of urinary calculi the patient passes urine with difficulty, which is viscid, turbid, and has characteristic pains and colours of the vitiated doṣas.

sanskrit_text: नाभिबस्तिसेवनीमेहनेष्वन्यतमस्मिन् अथ महता जातास म्त्रविकिरणं गोमेदकप्रकाश- वेदना मंत्रधारासड्वः सरुधिरम्त्रता अत्याविलं ससिकतं विसुजति, धावनलंघनप्लवनप्रष्ठयानीष्णाध्वगम- नेइचास्य वेदना भवन्ति
transliteration: nābhibastisevanīmehaneṣvanyatamasmin atha mahatā jātāsa mtravikiraṇaṃ gom edakaprakāśa- vedanā maṃtradhārāsaḍvaḥ sarudhiramtatā atyāvilaṃ sasikataṃ visujati, dhāvanalaṃghanap lavanapraṣṭhayānīṣṇādhvagama- neicāsya vedanā bhavanti
commentary: Now, when (calculi have) formed, pain during micturition occurs in any of these regions—the umbilical region, bladder, perineal raphe and penis and there is obstruction to the flow of urine, haematuria, scattering of the urinary stream, and passage of turbid, sandy urine shining like gomeda jem. Its pain is felt during running, jumping, riding and during walking in the sun and for long distances.

sanskrit_text: इलेटमाइमरी इलेष्मलमन्नमभ्यवहरतोऽत्यर्थमुपलिप्याधः तत्र परिवद्ध स्रातो निरुणद्धि, तस्य मूत्र- प्राप्य बस्तिमुखमधिष्ठाय भिद्यते प्रतिधाताहाल्यते निस्तुद्यत इव च बस्तिर्गुरु: हीतहच स्निग्धा महती कुक्कुटाण्डप्रतीकाशा अइमरी चात्र भवात, मध्कपुष्पवर्णा वा भवति, तां इलैष्मिकीमिति विद्यात्
transliteration: ileṭamāimari ileṣmalamannamabhyavaharato'tyarthamupalipyādhaḥ tatra parivaddha srāto nirṇaddhi, tasya mūtra- prāpya bastimukhamadhiṣṭhāya bhidyate pratidhātāhālyate nistudyata iva ca bastirguru: hītahaca snigdhā mahatī kukkuṭāṇḍapratīkāśā aimarī cātra bhavāta, madhkapuṣpavarṇā vā bhavati, tāṃ ilaiṣmikīmiti vidyāt
commentary: Now the śleṣmika stones are produced due to the excessive intake of śleṣma generating foods, and increase in size alround due to a further deposition of śleṣma. Being located in the bladder neck they obstruct the passage. Due to the obstruction to the flow of urine, cutting, incising or pricking pain, heaviness and sensation of cold is felt in the region. This type of stone is white, slimy and big like a hen's egg or else has the colours of madhūka flowers; these are known as śleṣmika (calculi).

topic_heading: The Paittika Stones (Uric Acid and Urate Calculi)
sanskrit_text: पित्तयुतस्त्र इलेंচमा यथोक्तां परिवद्धिं, प्राप्य संघातमपगम्य बस्तिमुखमधिष्ठाय स्रोतो निरुणद्वि, तस्य मृत्रप्रतिघातादृष्यते चृष्यते पच्यत इव बस्तिहष्णवातश्च भवति; अश्मरी चात्र सरक्ता पीतावभासा क्वब्णा भल्लातकास्थिप्रतिमा मधवर्णा वा भवति, तां पैत्तिकीमिति विद्यात्
transliteration: pittayutastra ileṃcamā yathoktāṃ parivaddhiṃ, prāpya saṃghātamapagamya bastimukhamadhiṣṭhāya sroto niruṇadvi, tasya mṛtrapratighātādṛṣyate cṛṣyate pacyata iva bastihiṣṇavātaśca bhavati; aśmarī cātra saraktā pītāvabhāsā kvabṇā bhallātakāsthipratimā madhavarṇā vā bhavati, tāṃ paittikīmiti vidyāt
commentary: The śleṣmā alongwith pitta gets solidified and increases in size alround as described earlier, and when located in the bladder neck region obstructs the passage. Due to obstruction to the flow of urine, warmth, sucking, burning or throbbing sensation is felt in the bladder region and uṣṇa vāta occurs. This type of stone is blood stained, yellowish in appearance or black, is like the kernel of bhallātaka fruit or else has the colour of honey. These are known as the paittika (calculi).

sanskrit_text: वीतयुतस्तु बस्तिमुखमधिष्ठाय स्रातो निरुणद्धि, तस्य मुत्रप्रतीघातात्तीव्रा वेदना भवति, तदाऽत्यर्थं पीडचमानो दन्तान् खादति, नाभि पीडयति, मेढ् प्रमुद्गाति, पायं स्प्शति, विशर्धते, विदहति, वातमूत्रपुरीषाणि कृच्छेण चास्य मेहतो निःसरन्ति; अश्मरी चात्र श्यावा परुषा विषमा खरा कवम्बपुष्प वत्कण्टकाचिता भवति ; तां वातिकोमिति विद्यात्
transliteration: vītayutastu bastimukhamadhiṣṭhāya srāto niruṇaddhi, tasya mutrapratīghātāttīvrā vedanā bhavati, tadā'tyarthaṃ pīḍacamāno dantān khādati, nābhi pīḍayati, meḍh pramudgāti, pāyaṃ spśati, viśardhate, vidahati, vātamūtrapurīṣāṇi kṛccheṇa cāsya mehato niḥsaranti; aśmarī cātra śyāvā paruṣā viṣamā kharā kavambapuṣpa vatkaṇṭakācitā bhavati ; tāṃ vātikomiti vidyāt
commentary: The śleṣmā alongwith vāta gets solidified and increases in size alround as described earlier and when located in the bladder neck obstructs the passage. Due to obstruction to the flow of his urine severe pain takes place; then, due to the excessive pain (the patient) gnashes his teeth, squeezes the umbilical region, rubs the penis, touches the perineum and he cries out in agony, feels a burning sensation and passes flatus, urine and stool with difficulty while straining for micturition. This type of stone is blackish, hard, irregular and rough and is full of spikes like the flowers of kadamba. These are known as the vātika (calculi).

sanskrit_text: प्रायेणीतास्तिस्रोऽइमंयों दिवास्क्प्नसमहानाध्यशनशीतस्निग्धगुरु- तेषामेवाल्पबस्तिका- मध्रराहारप्रियत्वाद्विशेषेण बालानां भवन्ति ; यत्वादनपचितमांसत्वाच्च बस्तेः सुखग्रहणाहरणा भवन्ति। महतां तु हाक्राइमरी हाक्रनिमित्ता भवति
transliteration: prāyeṇītāstisro'imayoṃ divāskpnasamahānādhyaśanaśītasnigdhaguru- teṣāmevālpabastikā- madhrarāhārapriyātvādviśeṣeṇa bālānāṃ bhavanti ; yatvādanapacitamāṃsatvācca basteḥ sukhagrahaṇāharaṇā bhavanti | mahatāṃ tu hākrāimarī hākranimittā bhavati
commentary: Often all these types of stones are formed in children specially because of their indulgence in day sleep, consumption of all sorts of food, eating before the previous meal has been digested and because of their liking for cold, bland, heavy and sweet dishes. Because of the small size of the bladder in them and because of its thin musculature (the stones) can be easily caught hold of and taken out. And in adults, the seminal concretions form due to śukra.

sanskrit_text: मैथ्नविघातादतिमैथनाद्वा श्र्कं चलितमनिर्गच्छद्विमार्गगमनादनि- लोऽभितः संगृह्य मेढव़षणयोरन्तरे संहरति, संहत्य चोपशोषयति; सा मूत्रमार्गमाव्रणोति, मृत्रकृच्छं बस्तिवेदनां वषणयोइच इवयथमा- प्रविलयमापद्यते ; तां पीडितमात्रे च तस्मिन्नेव प्रदेशे I हाक्राइमरीमिति विद्यात्
transliteration: maithnavighātād atimaiṭhanādvā śrkaṃ calitamanirgacchadvimārgagamanādani- lo'bhitaḥ saṃgṛhya meḍhavaṣaṇayorantare saṃharati, saṃhatya copaśoṣayati; sā mūtramārgamāvraṇoti, mṛtrakṛcchaṃ bastivedanāṃ vaṣaṇayoica ivayathamā- pravilayamāpadyate ; tāṃ pīḍitamātre ca tasminneva pradeśe I hākrāimarīmiti vidyāt
commentary: Due to interruption of sexual intercourse, or due to excessive sexual intercourse, the semen gets displaced but does not come out and is diverted into the wrong tract. Vāyu then gets (the displaced semen) together and deposits it between the penis and both the testes and after that it dries it up. This obstructs the urethra and dysuria, pain in the bladder and swelling in both the testes are brought about. It disappears by just a pressure in that very region. These are known as śukrāśmaris (seminal concretions).

sanskrit_text: भवन्ति चात्र—— शर्करा सिकता मेहो भस्माख्योऽइमरिवैक्रतम्। अइमर्या शर्करा ज्ञेया त्रल्यव्यञ्जनवेदना। पवनेऽनगणे सा तु निरेत्यल्पा विशेषतः। सा भिन्नर्म्तिर्वातेन हार्करेत्यभिधीयतें। हृत्पीडा सक्थिसदनं कुक्षिश्लं च वेपथः। तष्णोर्ध्वगोऽनिलः काष्ण्य दौर्बल्यं पाण्डुगात्रता। अरोचकाविपाकौ तु शर्करातें भवन्ति च
transliteration: bhavanti cātra—— śarkarā sikatā meho bhasmākhyo'im arivaikratam | aimaryā śarkarā jñeyā tralyavyañjanavedanā | pavane'nagaṇe sā tu niretyalpā viśeṣataḥ | sā bhinnarmtirvātena hārkaretyabhidhīyat eṃ | hṛtpīḍā sakthisadanaṃ kukṣiślaṃ ca vepathaḥ | taṣṇordhvag o'nilaḥ kāṣṇya daurbalyaṃ pāṇḍugātratā | arocakāvipākau tu śarkarāteṃ bhavanti ca
commentary: These verses are quoted in this context. Gravel, sand or ash like substances in the urine are the altered appearances of urinary calculi. Gravel and urinary calculi are known to have similar features alongwith pain. When the vāyu is favourable and specially when the calculi are small, they (the stones) come out. However, the same (calculi) when disrupted by the local vāyu are known as gravel. Pain in the precordium, weakness of lower limbs, pain in the flanks and shivering, thirst, upgoing vāyu, blackish discolouration, weakness, pale appearance of the body, dislike for food and indigestion : these occur in patients suffering from śarkarā (gravel) disease.

sanskrit_text: मूत्रमार्गप्रवृत्ता सा सक्ता कुर्यादुपद्रवान्। दौर्बल्यं सदनं काइयं कुक्षिश्रालमरोचकम्। पाण्डत्वमुष्णवातं च तृष्णां हृत्पीडनं वमिम्
transliteration: mūtramārgapravṛttā sā saktā kuryādupadvavān | daurbalyaṃ sadanaṃ kāiyaṃ kukṣiśrālamarocakam | pāṇḍatvamuṣṇavātaṃ ca tṛṣṇāṃ hṛtpīḍanaṃ vamim
commentary: Those (gravels) get stuck up on their passage through the urethra and produce complications such as weakness, lethargy, emaciation, pain in the flanks, dislike for food, pallor, uṣṇa-vāṭa (cysto-urethritis), thirst, pain in the precordium and vomiting.

sanskrit_text: नाभिप्ट्ठकटीमड्कगदवङक्षणशेफसाम्। एकद्वारस्तन्त्वक्कोमध्ये बस्तिरधोमुखः। बस्तिर्बस्तिशिरहचैव पौरुषं वृषणौ गुदः। एकसंबन्धिनो ह्येते गुदास्थिविवराश्रिताः। अलाब्वा इव रूपेण सिरास्नायपरिग्रहः
transliteration: nābhi pṭṭhakaṭīmaḍkagadavaṅkṣaṇaśephasām | ekadvārastantvakkomadhye bastiradhomukhaḥ | bastirbastiśirahacaiva pauruṣaṃ vṛṣaṇau gudaḥ | ekasaṃbandhino hyete gudāsthivivarāśritāḥ | alābvā iva rūpeṇa sirāsnāyaparigrahaḥ
commentary: The urinary bladder lies between the umbilicus, back, waist, testes, rectum, groin and penis, is thin walled and has a single outlet directed downwards. The bladder, as also the bladder neck, the penis, both testes and rectum are all related to each other and are situated in the space in front of the bone of the rectum (sacrum). (The bladder) is shaped like a gourd and is fixed on all sides by the veins and ligaments.

sanskrit_text: मत्राशयो मलाधारः प्राणायतनमंत्तमं। पक्वाशयगतास्तत्र नाडचो मूत्रबहास्त्र याः। तर्पयन्ति सदा मूत्रं सरितः सागरं यथा। सक्ष्मत्वान्नोपलम्यन्ते मुखान्यासां सहस्रहाः। नाडीभिरुपनीतस्य म्त्रस्यामाशयान्तरात्। जाग्रतः स्वपतइचैव स निःस्यन्देन पूर्यते। आमुखात्सलिले न्यस्तः पार्श्वेभ्यः पूर्यते नवः। घटो यथा तथा विद्धि बस्तिर्मंत्रेण पूर्यते
transliteration: matrāśayo malādhāraḥ prāṇāyatanaṃmaṃttamaṃ | pakvāśayagatāstatra nāḍaco mūtrabāhāstra yāḥ | tarpayanti sadā mūtraṃ saritaḥ sāgaraṃ yathā | sakṣmatvānnopalamyante mukhānyāsāṃ sahasrahāḥ | nāḍībhirupanītasya mtrasyāmāśayāntarāt | jāgrataḥ svapataicaiva sa niḥsyandena pūryate | āmukhātsalile nyastaḥ pārśvebhyaḥ pūryate navaḥ | ghaṭo yathā tathā viddhi bastirmaṃtreṇa pūryate
commentary: This (urinary bladder) is a site for collection of urine, a base for the mala, and is foremost amongst those organs which sustain life. The urine carrying channels originating from the pakvāśaya (intestines) always fill (the bladder) with urine in the same way as the rivers (constantly) fill the sea. Their mouths or openings are in thousands and because of their being extremely minute, are not seen. That (bladder) gets filled up with urine by percolation having been carried there by channels, from the āmāśaya (stomach) during waking as well as sleep. As a new pitcher sunk into water upto its mouth fills up from the sides, similarly bladder gets filled up by the urine.

sanskrit_text: एवमेव प्रवेशोन वातः पित्तं कफोऽपि वा। म्त्रयुक्तमुपस्नेहात् प्रविहय कुरुतेऽइमरोम्। अप्सु स्वच्छा (स्था) स्वपि यथा निषिकतासु नवे घटे। कालान्तरण पड्डु: स्यादइमरीसंभवस्तथा। संहन्त्यापो यथा दिव्या मारतोऽग्निइच वैद्युतः। तद्वब्दलासं बस्तिस्थमुद्रमा संहल्लि सानिलः। मारुते प्रगूणे बस्तौ मृत्रं सम्यक् प्रवर्तते।
transliteration: evameva praveśona vātaḥ pittaṃ kapho'pi vā | mtrayuktamupasnehāt pravihaya kurute'imarom | apsu svacchā (sthā) svapi yathā niṣikatasū nave ghaṭe | kālāntaraṇa paḍḍu: syā d aimarīsaṃbhavastathā | saṃhantyāpo yathā divyā mārato'gnica vaidyutaḥ | tadvbadalāsaṃ bastisthamudramā saṃhalli sānilaḥ | mārute pragūṇe bastau mṛtraṃ samyak pravartate |
commentary: Similarly, vāta, pitta and/or kapha enter the bladder and after mixing with urine because of their adhesiveness form the calculi. As even clean water kept in a new pitcher, gets muddy in due course of time—in a similar way calculi are formed. As air and fire of the electricity in the sky consolidate water (to form hail storms), similarly pitta located in the bladder in conjuction with vāyu consolidates kapha (to form calculi).

topic_heading: Effects of Normal and Abnormal Vāta on the Urinary Bladder
sanskrit_text: विकारा विविधाइचापि प्रतिलोमें भवन्ति हि। म्त्राघाताः प्रमेहाइच श्क्रदोषास्तथैव च। म्त्रदोषाइच ये केचिद्बस्तावेव भवन्ति हि।
transliteration: vikārā vividhāicāpi pratilomeṃ bhavanti hi | mtrāghātāḥ pramehāica śkradoṣāstathaiva ca | mtradoṣāica ye kecidbastāveva bhavanti hi |
commentary: When vāyu is functioning normally in the bladder, urine is properly discharged; on its becoming abnormal various complications such as retention of urine, urinary abnormalities and spermatic disorders, or some other urinary diseases occur in the bladder itself.

sanskrit_text: अथातो भगन्दराणां निदानं व्याख्यास्यामः।
transliteration: athāto bhagandarāṇāṃ nidānaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ |
commentary: Now we would expound upon 'The Diagnosis of Fistulae-in-ano.'

sanskrit_text: यथोवाच/ भगवान् धन्वन्तरिः
transliteration: yathovāca/ bhagavān dhanvantariḥ
commentary: As was described by Lord Dhanvantari.

sanskrit_text: वातपित्तइलेष्मसन्नियातागन्तुनिमित्ताः शतपोनकोष्ट्रग्रीवपरिस्रा- विशम्ब्रकावर्तोन्मागिणो यथासंख्यं पञ्च, अगन्दरा भवन्ति। ते तु भगगुदबस्तिप्रदेशदारणाच्च ‘भगन्दरा’ इत्युच्यन्ते। अभिन्नाः पिडकाः भिन्नास्तु भगन्दरा:
transliteration: vātapittaileṣmasanniyātāgantunimittāḥ śataponakoṣṭragrīvaparisrā- viśambrakāvartommāgiṇo yathāsaṃkhyaṃ pañca, agandarā bhavanti | te tu bhagagudabastipradeśadāraṇācca ‘bhagandarā’ ityucyante | abhinnāḥ piḍakāḥ bhinnāstu bhagandarā:
commentary: The fistulae-in-ano are of five types—śataponaka, uṣṭragrīva, parisrāvī, śambūkāvarta and unmārgī; they are caused by vāta, pitta and kapha, by a combination of the three doṣas and by trauma respectively. These are called fistulae-in-ano (bhagandara) because they break through the perineum (bhaga), anus and bladder regions. Those without an opening are called (anorectal) abscesses and those with an opening are called fistulae-in-ano.

sanskrit_text: तेषां त्र पूर्वरूपाणि—कटीकपालवेदना कण्डूर्दाहः शोफइच गुदस्य भवति
transliteration: teṣāṃ tra pūrvarūpāṇi—kaṭīkapālavedanā kaṇḍūrdāhaḥ śophaica gudasya bhavati
commentary: Their prodromal features are pain in the waist, itching, burning sensation and swelling at the anus.

sanskrit_text: तत्रापथ्यसेविनां वाय्: प्रकुपितः सन्निवृत्तः स्थिरीभूतो गु दमभि- तोऽङग्लेद्व यङग्ले वा मांसशोणिते प्रदूष्यारुणवर्णी पिडकां जनयति, वेदनाविशेषाञ्जनयति, साऽस्य तोदादीन् अप्रतिक्रियमाणा च पार्कप्रेति, म्रत्राशयाभ्यासगतत्वाच्च व्रणः प्रक्लिन्नः शतपोनकवद- ण मुखैशिछद्रै रापूर्यतै, तानि च छिद्राण्यजस्रमच्छं फेनान विद्धमधिकमास्रावं स्रवन्ति, व्रणश्व ताड्यते भिद्यते छिद्यते सूचीभिरिव निस्त्रद्यते, गद चावदीर्यते, उपेक्षिते च वातमूत्रपुरीषरेतसामप्यागमइच तैरेव छिद्रे- र्भवति; तं भगन्दरं शतपोनकमित्याचक्षते
transliteration: tatrāpathyasevināṃ vāy: prakupitaḥ sannivṛttaḥ sthirībhūto gu damabhi- to'ṅgledva yaṅgle vā māṃsaśoṇite praduṣyāruṇavarṇī piḍakāṃ janayati, vedanāviśeṣāñjanayati, sā'sya todādīn apratikriyamāṇā ca pārkpreti, mratrāśayābhyāsa gatatvācca vraṇaḥ praklinn aḥ śataponakavad- aṇa mukhaisśidrai rāpūryatai, tāni ca chidrāṇyajasramacchaṃ phenāna viddhamadhikamāsrāvaṃ sravanti, vraṇaśva tāḍyate bhidyate chidyate sūcībhiriva nistradyate, gada cāvadīryate, upekṣite ca vātamūtrapurīṣaretasāmapyāgamaica taireva chidre- rbhavati; taṃ bhagandaraṃ śataponakamityācakṣate
commentary: Now, due to indulgence in unsalutary diets and habits, the vāyu gets vitiated, condensed and then localised one to two fingers around the anus and involves the muscles and blood, gives rise to specific types of pain like pins and needles etc. and if it remains untreated, suppuration results (anorectal abscess). Due to its close proximity to the urinary bladder, the wound is always moist and is full of multiple small holes like that in a sieve; from those minute holes copious, clear or foamy discharge flows out continuously and there is whipping, tearing, biting and pricking pain in the wound and there is also splitting sensation of the anus. If neglected, flatus, urine, faeces and semen start coming out of those openings; such a fistula is called śataponaka.

sanskrit_text: पित्तं तु प्रकुपितमनिलेनाधः प्रेरितं पूर्ववदवस्थितं रवतां तन्वीमु - च्छितामुष्ट्रग्रीवाकारां पिडकां जनयति; साऽस्य चोषादोन् वेदना- विशषाञ्जनयति ; अप्रतिक्रियमाणा च पाकम्पेति ; वणइचाग्निक्षारा- म्यामिव दह्यते, दुर्गन्धमुष्णमास्रावं स्रवति, उपेक्षितइच वातमूत्रपुरोष- रेतांसि विस्जति ; तं भगन्दरमुष्ट्रग्रीवमित्याचक्षते
transliteration: pittaṃ tu prakupitam anilenādhaḥ preritaṃ pūrvavadavasthitaṃ ravatāṃ tanvīmu - cchitāmuṣṭragrīvākārāṃ piḍakāṃ janayati; sā'sya coṣādon vedanā- viśaṣāñjanayati ; apratikriyamāṇā ca pākampeti ; vaṇicāgnikṣārā- myāmiva dahyate, durgandhamuṣṇamāsrāvaṃ sravati, upekṣitaica vātamūtrapuroṣa- retāṃsi visjati ; taṃ bhagandaramuṣṭragrīvamityācakṣate
commentary: Vitiated pitta is pushed down by the vāyu and accumulates as described before around the anus and produces a red coloured, small and raised inflammed swelling of the shape of a camel's neck; it gives rise to specific burning type of pains etc. in it; and if untreated, suppuration results. The resulting wound gives rise to sensation as if burnt by alkali or fire cautery and there is foul smelling and warm discharge; if neglected, flatus, urine, faeces and semen are discharged (through it) and that fistula is called uṣṭragrīva.

sanskrit_text: इलेष्मा तु प्रकुपितः समीरणेनाधः प्रेरितः पूर्ववदवस्थितः हाुक्ला- वभासां स्थिरां कण्ड्मतों पिडकां जनयति; साऽस्य कण्ड्वादीन् वेदनाविरोषाञ्जनयति, अप्रतिक्रियमाणा च पाकमूर्पति, व्रणइच कठिनः संरम्भी क्रण्ड्रप्रायः पिच्छिलमजस्रमास्रावं स्रवति, उपेक्षितश्च वात म्त्रप्ररीषरेतांसि विस्जति ; तं भगन्दरं परिस्राविणमित्याचक्षते
transliteration: ileṣmā tu prakupitaḥ samīraṇenādhaḥ preritaḥ pūrvavadavasthitaḥ hāuklā- vabhāsāṃ sthirāṃ kaṇḍmatom piḍakāṃ janayati; sā'sya kaṇḍvādīn vedanāviroṣāñjanayati, apratikriyamāṇā ca pākamūrpati, vraṇaica kaṭhinaḥ saṃrambhī kraṇḍraprāyaḥ picchilamajasramāsrāvaṃ sravati, upekṣitaśca vāta mtraprarīṣaretāṃsi visjati ; taṃ bhagandaraṃ parisrāviṇamityācakṣate
commentary: The vitiated kapha, is pushed down by the vāyu and accumulates, as described before, around the anus and produces a white coloured, firm and itching swelling; it gives rise to specific pains like itching etc. If untreated, suppuration results and the resulting wound is indurated, angry looking and usually itching and a continuous mucoid discharge flows from it. If neglected flatus, urine, faeces and semen are discharged from it; that fistula is called as parisrāvī.

sanskrit_text: वायः प्रकुपितः प्रकुपितौ पित्तइलेष्माणौ परिगुह्याधो गत्वा पूर्ववइवस्थितः पादा ङ्गु ष्ठाग्रप्रमाणां सर्वेलिङ्गां पिडकां जनयति, साऽस्य तोददाहकण्ड्वादीन् वेदनाविशेषाञ्जनयति अप्रतिक्रियमाणा च पाकम् - पैति, व्रणश्‍च नानाविधवणैमास्रावं स्रवति, पूर्णनदीशम्बूंकावतेवच्चात्र सम्त्तिष्ठन्ति वेदनाविशेषाः ; ते अगन्दरं शम्बुकावर्तमित्यांचक्षते
transliteration: vāyaḥ prakupitaḥ prakupitau pittail eṣmāṇau pariguhyādho gatvā pūrvavaivasthitaḥ pādā ṅgu ṣṭhāgrapramāṇāṃ sarveliṅgāṃ piḍakāṃ janayati, sā'sya todadāhakaṇḍvādīn vedanāviśeṣāñjanayati apratikriyamāṇā ca pākam - paiti, vraṇaś ca nānāvidhavaṇaimāsrāvaṃ sravati, pūrṇanadīśambūkāvatevaccātra samttiṣṭhanti vedanāviśeṣāḥ ; te agandaraṃ śambukāvartamityāṃcakṣate
commentary: The vitiated vāyu, in close association with the vitiated pitta and kapha, travels down, and accumulates as described before around the anus and produces a swelling of the size of the tip of the great toe of the foot; it has the clinical features of all the doṣas and gives rise to specific pains like pricking, burning sensation and itching etc. If untreated, suppuration results and the resulting wound has a discharge of various colours; its specific pains are (deep seated and directed inwards) like whirlpools in a full river or the revolutions in a conch-shell; that fistula is called śambūkāvarta.

sanskrit_text: मूढ़ेन मांसलुब्धन प्रदस्थिशल्यप्रप्रेन सहास्यवहतं पदाऽवगाढपुरो- षोन्मिश्रमपानेनाधः प्रेरितमसम्यगागतं गुदमपक्षिणोति तदा क्षतनि- मित्तः कोथ : उपजायते, तस्मिइच क्षते पुयरुधिरावकोर्णमांसकोथे भूमाविव जलप्रक्लिन्नायां क्रिमयः संजायन्ते, ते भक्षयस्तो गुहमनेक्वधा पाइर्वतो दारयन्ति, तस्य तैर्मार्गेः क्रमिक्टर्तैर्वातमूत्रपुरोष रेतांस्यभिनिः- सरन्ति तं भगन्दरम न्मागिणमित्याचक्षते
transliteration: mūḍhena māṃsalubdhana pradastiśalyapraprena sahāsyavahataṃ padā'vagāḍhapuro- ṣonmiśramapānenādhaḥ preritamasamyagāgataṃ gudamapakṣiṇoti tadā kṣatani- mittakḥ kotha : upajāyate, tasmica kṣate puyarudhirāvakoṇamāṃsakothe bhūmāviva jalapraklin nāyāṃ krimayaḥ saṃjāyante, te bhakṣayasto guhamanekvadhā pāirvato dārayanti, tasya tairmārgeḥ kramikṭartairvātamūtrapuroṣa retāṃsyabhiniḥ- saranti taṃ bhagandaram nmāgiṇamityācakṣate
commentary: When a bony foreign body is taken with food by an unaware and meat greedy person, it is pushed down with solid stools by apāna vāyu and arrives in the anus abnormally and traumatises it; due to this injury putrefaction results. Organisms grow in the resulting wound and in the dead tissues full of pus and blood as they would grow in a soil full of stagnating water. These (organisms) while eating away the anus tear it from many sides. Then from the passages thus created by the organisms flatus urine, faeces and semen are discharged; that fistula is called unmārgī.

sanskrit_text: भवन्ति चात्र—— उत्पद्यतेऽल्पर्हक् शोफात् क्षिप्रं चाप्यपशाम्यति। पायवन्तदेशो पिडका सा ज्ञेयाऽन्या भगन्दरात्
transliteration: bhavanti cātra—— utpadyate'lparhak śophāt kṣipraṃ cāpyapaśāmyati | pāyavantadeśo piḍakā sā jñeyā'nyā bhagandarāt
commentary: The following verses are quoted in this context: A swelling in the anal region, which has mild pain and subsides quickly is known as piḍākā; and it is different from bhagandara-piḍakā.

sanskrit_text: पायोः स्याद् द्वयङ्गुले देशे गूढमूला सरुग्ज्वरा। भागन्दरीति विज्ञेया पिडकाऽतो विपर्ययात
transliteration: pāyoḥ syād dvayaṅgule deśe gūḍhamūlā sarugjvarā | bhāgandarīti vijñeyā piḍakā'to viparyayāt
commentary: A swelling occuring within two fingers around the anus, which is deep rooted and is accompanied with pain and fever is known as bhagandara-piḍakā as opposed to the piḍakā mentioned above.

sanskrit_text: कण्डरहग्दाहराफवान। यानयान्मलोत्सर्गत पर्वरूप कटय T पाय भवेद्रजः भगन्दरे
transliteration: kaṇḍarahagdāharāphavāna | yānayānmalotsargata parvarūpa kaṭaya T pāya bhavedrajaḥ bhagandare
commentary: Itching, pain, burning sensation and inflammation occuring in the anal region after riding on a vehicle and after defaecation are the prodromal features of fistula-in-ano.

sanskrit_text: घोराः साधयितुं दुःखाः सर्व एव भगन्दराः। तेष्वसाध्यस्त्रिदोषोत्थः क्षतजहच भगन्दरः
transliteration: ghorāḥ sādhayituṃ duḥkhāḥ sarva eva bhagandarāḥ | teṣvasādhyastridoṣotthaḥ kṣatajahaca bhagandaraḥ
commentary: All the fistulae are very difficult to treat; out of them the fistulae produced by a combination of the three doṣas i.e. śambūkāvarta and the traumatic ones (unmārgī) are incurable.

sanskrit_text: अथातः कुष्ठानदान व्याख्यास्यामः
transliteration: athātaḥ kuṣṭhānadāna vyākhyāsyāmaḥ
commentary: Now we would expound upon 'The Diagnosis of Skin Diseases (including Leprosy)'.

sanskrit_text: यथोवाच भगवान धन्वन्तरिः
transliteration: yathovāca bhagavān dhanvantariḥ
commentary: As was described by Lord Dhanvantari.

sanskrit_text: मिथ्याहाराचारस्थ विशेषाद्गुरुविरुद्धासात्म्याजीर्णीहिताहिनः स्नेहपीतस्य वान्तस्य वा व्यायामग्राम्यधर्मसेविनो ग्राम्यानूपौदकमांसानि वा पयसाऽभीक्ष्णमइनतो यो वा मज्जत्यप्सूष्माभितप्तः सहसा छादि वा प्रतिहन्ति, तस्य पित्तइलेष्माणौ प्रकुपितौ परिगृह्यानिलः प्रवृद्धस्तिर्यग्गाः सिराः संप्रपद्य समुद्धय बाह्यं मार्ग प्रति समन्ताद्विक्षिपति, यत्र तत्र च दोषो विक्षिप्तो निश्चरति तत्र तत्र मण्डलानि प्रादुर्भवन्ति, एवं समु- त्पन्नस्त्वचि दोषस्तत्र तत्र च परिर्वांद्व प्राप्याप्रतिक्रियमाणोऽभ्यन्तरं प्रतिपद्यते धातूनभिदूषयन्
transliteration: mithyāhārācārastha viśeṣādguruviruddhāsātmyājīrṇīhitāhinaḥ snehapītasya vāntasya vā vyāyāmagrāmyadharmasevino grāmyānūpaudakamāṃsāni vā payasā'bhīkṣṇamainato yo vā majjatyapsūṣmābhitaptaḥ sahasā chādi vā pratihanti, tasya pittail eṣmāṇau prakupitau parigṛhyānilaḥ pravṛddhastiryaggāḥ sirāḥ saṃprapadya samuddhaya bāhyaṃ mārga prati samantādvikṣipati, yatra tatra ca doṣo vikṣipto niścarati tatra tatra maṇḍalāni prādurbhavanti, evaṃ samu- tpannastvaci doṣastatra tatra ca parirvāṃdvā prāpyāpratikriyamāṇo'bhyantaraṃ pratipadyate dhātūn abhidūṣayan
commentary: Irregularity in diet or in daily routine; taking of specially heavy, contraindicated, unsuitable foods; taking meals before the previous meal has been digested or taking of unwholesome (foods); indulgence in exercise or in sexual intercourse after ingesting fatty foods or after having undergone emesis; taking of milk alongwith the meats of domestic, swamp and aquatic animals; taking of bath habitually while still feeling hot (after exposure to the sun or after physical exertion) and forcible inhibition of vomiting; all these vitiate pitta and kapha which get mixed up with vāyu, and getting aggravated traverse the oblique veins, involve the external passages and flare up alround.
