Patches become manifest at those very places wherever the flared up doṣas reach; the doṣas thus afflicting the skin increase at these very places, if left untreated; and when they reach internally they vitiate the dhātus.

sanskrit_text: तस्य पूर्वरूपाण— त्वकृपारुष्यमकस्माद्रोमहर्षः कण्डः स्वेदबाहल्य- मस्वेदनं वाऽङ्गप्रदेशानां स्वापः क्षतविसर्पणमसृजः कृष्णता चेति
transliteration: tasya pūrvarūpāṇa— tvakṛpāruṣyamakasmādromaharṣaḥ kaṇḍaḥ svedabāhalya- masvedanaṃ vā'ṅgapradeśānāṃ svāpaḥ kṣatavisarpaṇamasṛjaḥ kṛṣṇatā ceti
commentary: Their prodromal features are roughness of skin, sudden horripilation, itching, excessive sweating or absence of sweating, loss of sensation in the limbs, increase in the size of wounds (inspite of treatment) and blackish discolouration of the blood.

sanskrit_text: त्रत्र सप्त महाकुष्ठानि, एकादश क्ष्प्रकुष्ठान, एकमण्दादरा कुष्ठानि भवन्ति। तत्र महाकुष्ठान्यरुणोदुम्बरर्ष्य (र्क्ष) जिहवकपाल- काकणकपुण्डरोकदबुकुष्ठानोति। क्षुद्रकुष्ठान्यपि स्थलारुष्कं महाकुष्ठ- चर्मदलं विसर्पः परिसर्पः सिध्मं विर्चाचका किटिभं (मं) मंकक्ठ पामा रकसा चेति
transliteration: tratra sapta mahākuṣṭhāni, ekādaśa kṣprakuṣṭhāna, ekamaṇdādarā kuṣṭhāni bhavanti | tatra mahākuṣṭhānyaruṇodumbararṣya (rkṣa) jihavakapāla- kākaṇakapuṇḍarokadabukuṣṭhānōti | kṣudrakuṣṭhānyapi sthalāruṣkaṃ mahākuṣṭha- carmadalaṃ visarpaḥ parisarpaḥ sidhmaṃ vircācakā kiṭibhaṃ (maṃ) maṃkakṭha pāmā rakasā ceti
commentary: There are seven major kuṣṭhas and eleven minor kuṣṭhas; thus there are eighteen kuṣṭhas in all. The major kuṣṭhas are aruṇa, audumbara, ṛṣyajihva, kapāla, kākaṇaka, puṇḍarīka and dadru. The minor kuṣṭhas are sthūlāruṣka, mahākuṣṭha, ekakuṣṭha, carmadala, visarpa, parisarpa, sidhma, vicarcikā, kitibha, pāmā and rakasā.

topic_heading: Doṣa as the Basis of Nomenclature and Prognosis of Major Kuṣṭha
sanskrit_text: सक्रिमोणि सर्वाणि कुष्ठानि सवातानि सपित्तानि सइलेष्माणि च भवन्ति, उत्सन्नतस्तु दोषग्रहणमभिभवात्। तत्र वातेनारुणं, पित्तेनोदुम्बरर्ष्य (क्ष्) जिह्वकपालकाकणकानि, इलेष्मणा पुण्डरीकं दद्रकुष्ठं चेति। तेषां महत्त्वं क्रियागुर्त्वमुत्तरोत्तरं घात्वनुप्रवेशादसाध्यत्वं चेति
transliteration: sakrimoṇi sarvāṇi kuṣṭhāni savātāni sapittāni sail eṣmāṇi ca bhavanti, utsannatastu doṣagrahaṇamabhibhavāt | tatra vātenāruṇaṃ, pittenōdumbararṣya (kṣ) jihvakapālakākaṇakāni, ileṣmaṇā puṇḍarīkaṃ dadrakuṣṭhaṃ ceti | teṣāṃ mahattvaṃ kriyāgurtvamuttarottaraṃ ghātvanupraveśād asādhyatvaṃ ceti
commentary: All the kuṣṭhas are due to the vitiation of vāta, pitta, and kapha and due to organisms. The nomenclature is done according to the predominance of the doṣas concerned. Out of them aruṇa is due to vāta; audumbara, ṛṣyajihva, kapāla and kākaṇaka are due to pitta and puṇḍarīka and dadru are due to kapha. The significance of this order is because of the increasing difficulty in their management, their ability to involve the dhātus successively and their increasing incurability.

sanskrit_text: तत्र वातेनारुणाभानि तन्नि विसर्पोणि तोदभेदस्वापयुक्तान्य- हणानि। पिलेन पक्वोदुम्बरफलाकृतिवर्णन्यौदुम्बराणि, ऋष्य(क्ष)- जिह्वाप्रकाशानि खराणि ऋष्य (क्ष) जिव्हानि, कृष्णकपालिकाप्रका- हानि कपालकुड्ठानि, काकणान्तिकाफलसदृशान्यतीव रक्तकृष्णानि काकणकानि; तेषां चतुर्णमप्योषचोषपरिदाहघूमायनानि क्षिप्रोत्थान- प्रपाकभेदित्वानि क्रिमिजन्म च सामान्यानि लिङ्कानि। इलेष्मणा पुण्डरीकपत्रप्रकाशानि पौण्डरीकाणि, अतसीपुष्पवर्णानि ताम्पाणि वा विसर्पीणि पिडकावन्ति च दद्रुकुष्ठानि; तयोर्द्वयोरप्युत्सन्नता परिमण्ड- लता कण्ड़शिचरोत्थानत्वं चेति सामान्यानि रूपाणि
transliteration: tatra vātenāruṇābhāni tanni visarpoṇi todabhedasvāpayuktānya- haṇāni | pilena pakvodumbaraphalākṛtivarṇanyaudumbarāṇi, ṛṣya(kṣa)- jihvāprakāśāni kharāṇi ṛṣya (kṣa) jivhāni, kṛṣṇakapālikāprakā- hāni kapālakuḍṭhāni, kākaṇāntikāphalasadṛśānyatīva raktakṛṣṇāni kākaṇakāni; teṣāṃ catu rṇamapyoṣacoṣaparidāhaghūmāyanāni kṣiprotthāna- prapākabheditvāni krimijanma ca sāmānyāni liṅkāni | ileṣmaṇā puṇḍarīkapatraprakāśāni pauṇḍarīkāṇi, atasīpuṣpavarṇāni tāmpāṇi vā visarpīṇi piḍakāvanti ca dadrukuṣṭhāni; tayordvayorapyutsannatā parimaṇḍa- latā kaṇḍaśicarotthānatvaṃ ceti sāmānyāni rūpāṇi
commentary: Vātika Mahākuṣṭha (1) Aruṇa—Out of these, the aruṇa kuṣṭha caused by vāta, is reddish in appearance, thin and has a tendency to spread and is associated with pricking and tearing pains and with loss of sensations. Paittika Mahākuṣṭhas (2) Audumbara—The audumbara mahākuṣṭhas caused by pitta are of similar colour and sizes as the ripe audumbara fruits. (3) Ṛṣyajihva—The ṛṣyajihva kuṣṭhas are similar in appearance and roughness to that of the tongue of ṛṣya deers. (4) Kapālakuṣṭha—The kapālakuṣṭhas are like black clay pot in appearance. (5) Kākaṇaka—The kākaṇaka kuṣṭhas are extremely black and red in colour like the fruits of kākaṇāntikā. The general features of all these four are warmth, sucking and burning sensations, smoky sensation, quick appearance, suppuration, bursting and growth of organisms in them. Slesmika-Kusthas (6) The puṇḍarīka kuṣṭha—The puṇḍarīka kuṣṭhas caused by śleṣma are like the leaves of white lotus. (7) Dadru kuṣṭha—The dadru kuṣṭhas have the colouration of the flowers of linseed, or are copper coloured, and are serpigenous and full of eruptions. The general features of both these are elevated, spherical, itching and slowly growing patches.

sanskrit_text: क्ष्मद्रकुष्ठान्यत ऊर्घ्व वक्ष्यामः—— स्थूलानि सन्धिष्वतिदारुणानि स्थूलारुषि स्यः कठिनान्यरूंषि। त्वक्कोचर्भदस्वपना ङ्गसादाः कुष्ठे महत्पूर्वयुते भवन्ति
transliteration: kṣmadrakuṣṭhānyata ūrghva vakṣyāmaḥ—— sthūlāni sandhiṣvatidāruṇāni sthūlāruṣi syaḥ kaṭhinānyarūṃṣi | tvak kocarbhadasvapanā ṅgasādāḥ kuṣṭhe mahatpūrvayute bhavanti
commentary: Now we would describe the minor kuṣṭhas. (1) Sthūlāruṣka: There are hard and thick ulcers in the joints and are difficult to treat in cases of sthūlāruṣka kuṣṭhas. (2) Mahākuṣṭha: Appearance of wrinkles, cracks and anaesthesia in the skin and lethargy occur in mahākuṣṭha.

sanskrit_text: कष्णाहणं येन भवेच्छरीरं तदेककुष्ठं प्रवदन्ति कुष्ठम्। कण्ड्व्यथनौषचोषास्तलेष् तच्चर्मदलं वदन्ति
transliteration: kaṣṇāhaṇaṃ yena bhaveccharīraṃ tadekakuṣṭhaṃ pravadanti kuṣṭham | kaṇḍvyathanauṣacoṣāstaleṣ tac carmatalaṃ vadanti
commentary: (3) Ekakuṣṭha: That kuṣṭha in which the body becomes blackish-red is known as ekakuṣṭha. (4) Carmadala: That kuṣṭha in which there is itching, pain, warmth and sucking sensation in the palms and soles is called carmadala.

sanskrit_text: विसर्पवतः सर्पति सर्वतो यस्त्वग्रक्तमांसान्यभिभ्य शीघ्रम्। मूर्च्छाविदाहारतितोदपाकान् कृत्वा विसर्पः स भवेद्विकारः
transliteration: visarpavataḥ sarpati sarvato yastvagraktamāṃsānyabhibhya śīghram | mūrcchāvidāhāratitodapākān kṛtvā visarpaḥ sa bhavedvikāraḥ
commentary: (5) Visarpa Kuṣṭha: That kuṣṭha is visarpa which having afflicted the skin, blood, and muscles quickly spreads all over like erysipelas and which produces unconsciousness, burning, restlessness, pricking pain and suppuration.

sanskrit_text: हानैः शरीरे पिडकाः स्रवन्त्यः सर्पन्ति यास्तं परिसर्पमाहुः। कण्डवन्वितं इवेतमपायि सिध्म विद्यात्तन् प्रायश ऊर्ध्वकाये
transliteration: hānaiḥ śarīre piḍakāḥ sravantyaḥ sarpanti yāstaṃ parisarpamāhuḥ | kaṇḍavanvitaṃ ive tamapāyi sidhma vidyāttan prāyaśa ūrdhvakāye
commentary: (6) Parisarpa Kuṣṭha: That is called parisarpa in which discharging boils gradually spread over the body. (7) Sidhma Kuṣṭha: That should be known as sidhma kuṣṭha which has itching, is whitish, painless and thin and usually occurs in the upper half of the body.

sanskrit_text: राज्योऽतिकण्ड्वर्तिरुजः सरूक्षा भवन्ति गात्रेष् विर्चाचकायाम्। कण्ड्मती दाहरुजोपपन्ना विपादिका पादगतेयमेव
transliteration: rājyo'tikaṇḍvartirujaḥ sarūkṣā bhavanti gātreṣ vircācakāyām | kaṇḍmatī dāharujopapannā vipādikā pādagateyameva
commentary: (8) Vicarcikā Kuṣṭha: Cracks, excessive itching, severe pain alongwith roughness in the body are present in vicarcikā kuṣṭha. The same occuring in the foot only with itching, burning and pain is called vipādikā.

sanskrit_text: यत् स्रावि वृत्तं घनमुप्रकण्डु तत् स्निग्धकृष्णं किटिभं (मं) वदन्ति। सास्रावकण्ड्रपरिदाहकाभिः पामाऽण्काभिः पिडकाभिरूह्या
transliteration: yat srāvi vṛttaṃ ghanamuprakaṇḍu tat snigdhakṛṣṇaṃ kiṭibhaṃ (maṃ) vadanti | sāsrāvakaṇḍraparidāhakābhiḥ pāmā'ṇkābhiḥ piḍakābhirūhyā
commentary: (9) Kitibha Kuṣṭha: That is known as kitibha kuṣṭha in which the patches are discharging, circular, dense, severely itching, slimy and blackish. (10) Pāmā Kuṣṭha: Pāmā kuṣṭha is associated with discharge, itching and burning, and with the appearance of tiny boils.

sanskrit_text: स्फोटैः सदाहैरति सैव कच्छूः स्फिक्पाणिपादप्रभर्वनिरूप्या। कण्ड्वन्विता या पिडका शरीरे संस्रावहीना रकसोच्यते सा
transliteration: sphoṭaiḥ sadāhairati saiva kacchūḥ sphikpāṇipādaprabharvanirūpyā | kaṇḍvanvitā yā piḍakā śarīre saṃsrāvahīnā rakasocyate sā
commentary: Kacchu Kuṣṭha: And that (pāmā) in which blisters with burning pain are produced in the buttocks, hands and feet is called kacchū kuṣṭha. (11) Rakasā Kuṣṭha: That is called rakasā kuṣṭha in which there is itching in the body and boils are present without any discharge.

topic_heading: Doṣas as the Aetiological Basis of Minor Kuṣṭhas
sanskrit_text: अरुः ससिध्मं रकसा महच्च यच्चैककुष्ठं कफजान्यमनि। वायोः प्रकोपात् परिसर्पमेकं शेषाणि पित्तप्रभवाणि विद्यात्
transliteration: aruḥ sasidhmaṃ rakasā mahacca yaccaikakuṣṭhaṃ kaphajānyamani | vāyoḥ prakōpāt parisarpamekaṃ śeṣāṇi pittaprabhavāṇi vidyāt
commentary: Sthūlāruṣka, sidhma, rakasā, mahākuṣṭha, and ekakuṣṭha are produced by kapha. Parisarpa is the only one produced by the vitiation of vāyu; the rest are known to be due to vitiation of the pitta.

sanskrit_text: तन्त्रिविधं—वातेन, पित्तेन, किलासमपि कूष्ठविकल्प एव; इलेष्मणा चेति। कुष्ठकिलासयोरन्तरं—त्वग्गतमेव किलासमपरिस्रावि च। तद्वातेन मण्डलमरुणं परुषं परिध्वंसि च, पित्तेन पद्मपत्रप्रतीकाशं हवेतं स्निग्धं सपरिदाहं च, इलेष्मणा बहल कण्डमच्च। तंष संबद्धमण्डलमन्तेजातं रक्तरोम चासाध्यमग्निदग्धं च
transliteration: tantrividhaṃ—vātena, pittena, kilāsamapi kūṣṭhavikalpa eva; ileṣmaṇā ceti | kuṣṭhakilāsayorantaraṃ—tvaggatameva kilāsamaparisrāvi ca | tad vātena maṇḍalamaruṇaṃ paruṣaṃ paridhvaṃsi ca, pittena padmapatrapratīkāśaṃ havetaṃ snigdhaṃ saparidāhaṃ ca, ileṣmaṇā bahala kaṇḍamacca | taṃṣa saṃbaddhamaṇḍalamantejātaṃ raktaroma cāsādhyamagnidagdhaṃ ca
commentary: Leucoderma is also a kind of dermatoses; they are of three types—that due to vāta, pitta and kapha. Differentiating Features from Leprosy: The difference between leprosy and leucoderma is that the later is limited to the skin only and has no discharge. Clinical Features: Leucoderma Caused By The Vāta: That leucoderma which is caused by vāta is circular, red, indurated, and gives out dusty particles on rubbing. Leucoderma caused by Pitta: That leucoderma which is caused by pitta is like a lotus leaf, reddish, smooth and is associated with burning sensation. Leucoderma caused by Kapha: That caused by kapha, is white, oily, extensive and is associated with itching. These leucodermas in which the patches overlap each other and in which the hairs are red at the terminal parts of the body are incurable, as are also those which develop after burns.

sanskrit_text: त्वकसंकोचस्वापस्वेदशोफभेदकौण्यस्वरोपघाता वातेन, कुष्ठष् त् पित्तेन, पाकावदरणाङग्लिपतनकर्णनासाभड्वाक्षिरागसत्त्वोत्पत्तयः | कण्ड्रवर्णभेदशोफास्रावगौरवाणि इलेष्मणा
transliteration: tvakasaṃkocasvāpasvedaśophabhedakauṇyasvaropaghātā vātena, kuṣṭhaṣ t pitten a, pākāvadaraṇāṅglipatanakarṇanāsābhaḍvākṣirāgasattvotpattayaḥ | kaṇḍravarṇabhedaśophāsrāvagaura vāṇi ileṣmaṇā
commentary: In leprosy contraction of skin, loss of sensation, excessive perspiration, oedema, tearing sensation, deformity and speech disturbances are due to vitiated vāta; suppuration, bursting, dropping off of fingers, breaking off of the ears and nose, congestion of eyes, and production of organisms are due to vitiated pitta; and itching, discolouration, oedema, discharge, and heaviness are due to śleṣma.

sanskrit_text: तत्रादिबलप्रव्त्तं पौण्डरीकं काकणं चासाध्यम्
transliteration: tatrādibalapravttaṃ pauṇḍarīkaṃ kākaṇaṃ cāsādhyam
commentary: Out of them, the paunḍarīka and kākaṇaka, which are due to defect in the germ cells, are incurable.

sanskrit_text: भवन्ति चात्र—— यथा वनस्पतिजातः प्राप्य कालप्रकर्षणम्। अन्तर्भूमि विगाहेत मलैर्वष्टिविवर्धितैः। एव कुष्ठ समुत्पन्नं त्वचि कालप्रकर्षतः । ऋमेण धात्न् व्याप्नोति नरस्याप्रतिकारिणः
transliteration: bhavanti cātra—— yathā vanaspatijātaḥ prāpya kālaprakarṣaṇam | antarbhūmi vigāheta malairvaṣṭivivardhitaiḥ | eva kuṣṭha samutpannaṃ tvaci kālaprakarṣataḥ | ṛmeṇa dhātn vyāpnoti narasyāpratikāriṇaḥ
commentary: These verses have been quoted in this context. As a growing plant in due course of time spreads inside the earth by its roots and further proliferates with rains, similarly leprosy appearing in the skin, in due course of time spreads in the dhātus sequentially in those patients who remain untreated.

sanskrit_text: स्पर्शहानिः स्वेदनत्वमीषत्कण्डूइच जायते। वैवर्ण्य रूक्षभावहच कुष्ठे त्वचि समाश्रिते
transliteration: sparśahāniḥ svedanatvamīṣatkaṇḍūica jāyate | vaivarṇya rūkṣabhāvahaca kuṣṭhe tvaci samāśrite
commentary: Loss of tactile sensation, excessive perspiration, slight itching, discolouration and feeling of dryness are produced in leprosy located within the skin.

topic_heading: Clinical Features of Leprosy Involving Śoṇita
sanskrit_text: त्वक्स्वापो रोमहर्षइच स्वेदस्याभिप्रवर्तनम्। कर्ण्डूविपुयकइचेव कुष्ठे शोणितसंश्रिते
transliteration: tvak svāpo romaharṣica svedasyābhipravartanam | karṇḍūvipuyakaiceva kuṣṭhe śoṇitasaṃśrite
commentary: Loss of tactile sensation, horripilation, excessive perspiration, itching and suppuration are produced in leprosy located in the rakta.

topic_heading: Clinical Features of Leprosy Involving Māṁsa
sanskrit_text: बाहुल्यं वऋशोषइच कार्कइयं पिडकोद्गमः। तोदः स्फोटः स्थिरत्वं च कुष्ठे मांससमाश्रिते
transliteration: bāhulyaṃ vaṛśoṣica kārkaiyaṃ piḍakodgamaḥ | todaḥ sphoṭaḥ sthiratvaṃ ca kuṣṭhe māṃsasamāśrite
commentary: Big patches, dryness of the mouth, roughness, production of multiple boils, pricking pain, blisters and induration are produced in leprosy located in the māṁsa.

topic_heading: Clinical Features of Leprosy Involving Meda
sanskrit_text: दौर्गन्ध्यमपदेहहच पूयोऽथ क्रिमयस्तथा। गात्राणां भेदनं चापि कुष्ठे मेद:समाश्रिते
transliteration: daurgandhyamapadeha haca pūyo'tha krimayastathā | gātrāṇāṃ bhedanaṃ cāpi kuṣṭhe meda:samāśrite
commentary: Bad smell, soddening, pus formation, production of organisms and tearing sensation in the limbs are produced in leprosy located in the meda.

topic_heading: Clinical Features of Leprosy Involving Asthi and Majjā
sanskrit_text: नासाभड्मोऽक्षिरागइच क्षते च क्रिमिसंभवः। भवेत् स्वरोपघातइच हचस्थिमज्जसमाश्रिते
transliteration: nāsābhaḍmo'kṣirāgica kṣate ca krimisaṃbhavaḥ | bhavet svaropaghātica hac asthimajjasamāśrite
commentary: Falling off of the nose, congestion of the eyes, production of organisms in the lesion, and speech disorders are produced in leprosy located in the asthi and majjā.

topic_heading: Clinical Features of Leprosy Involving the Śukra
sanskrit_text: कौण्यं गतिक्षयोऽङ्गनां संभेदः क्षतसर्पणम्। शुक्रस्थानगते लिङ्गं प्रागुक्तानि तथैव च
transliteration: kauṇyaṃ gatikṣayo'ṅganāṃ saṃbhedaḥ kṣatasarpaṇam | śukrasthānagate liṅgaṃ prāguktāni tathaiva ca
commentary: Paralysis of the hands, loss of movements of the limbs, tearing sensation of the limbs and spreading of the lesions are produced when it (leprosy) reaches the site of śukra; as also all those features mentioned above are produced.

sanskrit_text: स्त्रीपुंसयोः कुष्ठदोषादुदुष्टइहो'णितहाक्रयोः। यदपत्यं तयोर्जातं ज़ेयं तदपि कुष्ठितम्
transliteration: strīpuṃsayoḥ kuṣṭhadoṣāduduṣṭaiho'ṇitahākrayoḥ | yadapatyaṃ tayorjātaṃ ze yaṃ tadapi kuṣṭhitam
commentary: The child born of a woman and a man with vitiated ovum and sperm due to leprosy should be regarded as leprotic.

sanskrit_text: कुष्ठमात्मवतः साध्यं त्वग्रक्तपिशिताश्रितम्। मेदोगतं भवेद्याप्यमसाध्यमत उत्तरम्
transliteration: kuṣṭhamātmavataḥ sādhyaṃ tvagraktapiśitāśritam | medogataṃ bhavedyāpyamasādhyamata uttaram
commentary: Leprosy is curable in the prudent if it is located within tvak, rakta and māṁsa ; it is relievable if it involves meda whereas it is incurable if it is located in the rest of the dhātus.

topic_heading: Effects of Good and Bad Deeds on Leprosy
sanskrit_text: ब्रह्मस्त्रीसज्जनवधपरस्वहरणादिभिः। कर्मभिः पापरोगस्य प्राहुः कुष्ठस्य संभवम्। म्पियते यदि कुष्ठेल पुनर्जातेऽपि गच्छति। नातः कष्टतरो रोगो यथा कुष्ठं प्रकीतितम्। आहाराचारयोः प्रोक्तामास्थाय महतीं क्रियाम्। औषधीनां विशिष्टानां तपसइच निषेवणात् । यस्तेन मुच्यते जन्तुः स पुण्यां गतिमाप्नयात
transliteration: brahmastrīsajjanavadhaparasvaharaṇādibhiḥ | karmabhiḥ pāparogasya prāhuḥ kuṣṭhasya saṃbhavam | mpiyate yadi kuṣṭhela punarjāte'pi gacchati | nātaḥ kaṣṭataro rogo yathā kuṣṭhaṃ prakītitam | āhārācārayoḥ proktāmāsthāya mahatīṃ kriyām | auṣadhīnāṃ viśiṣṭānāṃ tapasaica niṣevaṇāt | yastena mucyate jantuḥ sa puṇyāṃ gatimāpnayāt
commentary: It has been said that the evil acts of killing of brāhmins, women, and noble persons and taking of others riches etc., produce leprosy as a disease of sin. If one dies due to leprosy, he gets the same disease when he is reborn; therefore there is none more distressing disease known than leprosy. One who, having faith in the diet and daily rituals mentioned (elsewhere) carries out the same great deeds and the person who gets rid of this (leprosy) disease due to the use of special medicines and religious austerities obtains healthy body.

topic_heading: Modes of Spread of Contagious Diseases
sanskrit_text: प्रसङ्गाद्गात्रसंस्पर्शान्निश्वासात् सहभोजनात्। सहशय्यासनाच्चापि वस्त्रमाल्यानुलेपनात्। कुष्ठं ज्वरइच शोषइच नेत्राभिष्यन्द एव च। औपसर्गिकरोगाइच संक्रामन्ति नरान्नरम्
transliteration: prasaṅgādgātrasaṃsparśānniśvāsāt sahabhojanāt | sahaśayyāsanāccāpi vastramālyānulepanāt | kuṣṭhaṃ jvaraca śoṣaca netrābhiṣyanda eva ca | aupasargikarogāica saṃkrāmanti narānnaram
commentary: Kuṣṭha, fever, consumption, conjunctivitis and infectious diseases spread from human beings to human beings due to sexual intercourse, touching of the body, due to breath, eating together, and even sharing the same bed and by clothings, garlands and cosmetics.

sanskrit_text: अथातः प्रमेहनिदार्न व्याख्यास्यामः
transliteration: athātaḥ pramehanidārna vyākhyāsyāmaḥ
commentary: Now we would expound upon the chapter entitled 'Diagnosis of Urinary Abnormalities'.

sanskrit_text: यथोवाच भगवान धन्वन्तरिः
transliteration: yathovāca bhagavān dhanvantariḥ
commentary: As was described by Lord Dhanvantari.

sanskrit_text: दिवास्वप्नाव्यायामालस्यप्रसक्तं सेविनं पुरुषं जानीयात् प्रमेही भविष्यतीति
transliteration: divāsvapnāvyāyāmālasyaprasaktaṃ sevinaṃ puruṣaṃ jānīyāt pramehī bhaviṣyatīti
commentary: The person who indulges in day sleeping, abstains from physical exercise, is lazy and takes cold, slimy, sweet and fatty foods or drinks should be known as one who would develop urinary abnormalities.

sanskrit_text: वातपित्तइलेंष्माणो यदा एव तस्य चवप्रवृत्तस्यापरिपक्वा मूत्रवाहिस्रोतांस्यनुसृत्याधो गत्वा बस्तेर्मुखमा- मेदसा सहैकत्वभुपेत्य श्रित्य निभिद्यन्ते तदा प्रमेहाञ्जनयन्ति
transliteration: vātapittailenṣmāṇo yadā eva tasya cavapravṛttasyāparipakvā mūtravāhisrotāṃsy anusṛtyādho gatvā bastermukhamā- medasā sahaikatvabhu petya śritya nibhidyante tadā pramehāñjanayanti
commentary: In such a person, when the immature vāta, pitta and kapha combine with meda and get unified they go downwards following the urine conducting channels and getting located at the neck of the bladder are excreted and thus produce urinary abnormalities.

sanskrit_text: स्निग्धपिच्छिलगुरुता तेषां पूर्वरूपाणि——हस्तपादतलदाहः त्रा गात्राणा मधुरशुक्लमूत्रता तन्द्रा सादः पिपासा दुर्गन्धइच श्वासस्ताल- मलोत्पन्निर्जठिलीसाचः गलजिह्वादन्तषु केशानां वद्धिहच नखानाम्
transliteration: snigdhapicchilagurutā teṣāṃ pūrvarūpāṇi——hastapādataladāhaḥ trā gātrāṇā madhuraśuklamūtratā tandrā sādaḥ pipāsā durgandhica śvāsastāla- malotpannirjaṭhilīsācaḥ galajihvādantaṣu keśānāṃ vaddhihaca nakhānām
commentary: Their prodromal features are : Burning sensation in the palms and soles; oiliness, sliminess and heaviness in the limbs; sweetness and whitishness in the urine; drowsiness; lethargy; thirst; bad smell in the breath; production of deposits in the palate, throat, tongue and teeth; matting together of hairs; and increased growth of nails.

sanskrit_text: तत्राविलप्रभूतमंत्रलक्षणाः सर्वैं एव प्रमेंहा भवन्ति
transliteration: tatrāvilaprabhūtamaṃtralakṣaṇāḥ sarvaiṃ eva prameṃhā bhavanti
commentary: Turbidity and excessive urination are the symptoms present in all types of urinary abnormalities.

sanskrit_text: सर्व एव सर्वदोषसमृत्थाः सह पिडकाभिः
transliteration: sarva eva sarvadoṣasamṛtthāḥ saha piḍakābhiḥ
commentary: All (urinary abnormalities) are due to vitiation of all the doṣas together (vāta, pitta and kapha) as also are the associated furuncles.

topic_heading: Doṣawise Classification and Prognosis of Urinary Abnormalities
sanskrit_text: कफादुदकेक्षुवालिकासुरासिकताशनैर्लवणपिष्टसान्द्रशक्रफेन- तत्र, समक्रियत्वात; पित्तान्नीलहरिद्रा- मेहा दश साध्याः दोषदूष्याणां म्लक्षारमञ्जिष्ठाशोणितमेहाः षड् विषम- दोषदूष्याणी याप्याः, क्रियत्वात; र्सापर्वसाक्षौद्रहस्तिमेहाइचत्वारोऽसाध्यतमाः, वातात् महात्यायकत्वात
transliteration: kaphādudakekṣuvālikāsurāsikātaśanairlavaṇapiṣṭasāndraśakraphēna- tatra, samakriyatvāt; pittānnīlaharidrā- mehā daśa sādhyāḥ doṣadūṣyāṇāṃ mlakṣāramañjiṣṭhāśoṇitamehāḥ ṣaḍ viṣama- doṣadūṣyāṇī yāpyāḥ, kriyatvāt; rsāparvasākṣaudrahastimehāicatvāro'sādhyatamāḥ, vātāt mahātyāyakatvāt
commentary: Urinary Abnormalites due to Kapha : Udakameha, ikṣuvālikāmeha, surāmeha, sikatāmeha, śanairmeha, lavanameha, piṣṭameha, sāndrameha, śukrameha, and phenameha; these ten (urinary abnormalities) are due to (vitiated) kapha and they are curable because of the identical remedial measures which have to be employed both for the correction of (vitiated) doṣas as for the vitiated tissues (dūṣya). Urinary Abnormalities due to Pitta : Nīlameha, haridrāmeha, amlameha, kṣārameha, mañjiṣṭhāmeha, and raktameha; these six (urinary abnormalities) are due to (vitiated) pitta and they are relievable only because of the remedial measures being dissimilar which have to be employed for the correction of (vitiated) doṣas and the tissues. Urinary Abnormalities due to vāta : Sarpirmeha, vasāmeha, kṣaudrameha, and hastimeha; these four (urinary abnormalities) are due to (vitiated) vāta and they are incurable because of their being extremely serious.

topic_heading: The Doṣas in Relation to Urinary Abnormalities
sanskrit_text: वातपित्तमेदोभिरन्वितः हलेडमा इलेष्मप्रमेहाञ्जनयति, तत्र वातकफशोणितमेदोभिरन्वितं पित्तं पित्तप्रमेहान्, कफपित्तवसामज्जमेदो भिरन्वितो वायुर्वातप्रमेहान्
transliteration: vātapittamedobhiranvitaḥ haleḍamā ileṣmapramehāñjanayati, tatra vātakaphaśoṇitamedobhiranvitaṃ pittaṃ pittapramehān, kaphapittavasāmajjamedo bhiranvito vāyurvātapramehān
commentary: Now, kapha in combination with vāta, pitta and meda produces the urinary abnormalities of kaphaja origin. Pitta, in combination with vāta, kapha, śoṇita and meda produces the urinary abnormalities of pitta origin. Vāyu, in combination with kapha, pitta, vasā, majjā and meda produces urinary abnormalities of vāta origin.

topic_heading: Clinical Features of Urinary Abnormalities due to Kapha
sanskrit_text: इवे तमवेदनमदकसदृशमदकमेही मेहति ; इक्षुरसतुल्यमि- तंत, सरामेही ; क्षवालिकामेही ; सिकतानविद्धं सर्हज सरात्रल्य हानैर्मेही; विहादं लवणत्रल्य लवणमेही; हष्टरोम: पिष्टरसतुल्यं पिष्टमेही; आविलं सान्द्रं सान्द्रमही; शुक्रतुल्यं शुक्रमही; स्तोकं स्तोकं सफेनमच्छं फेनमेही मेहति
transliteration: ive tamavedanamadakasadṛśamadakamēhī mēhati ; ikṣurasatulyami- tanta, sarāmēhī ; kṣavālikāmēhī ; sikatānaviddhaṃ sarhaja sarātrālya hānairmēhī; vihādaṃ lavaṇatralya lavaṇamēhī; haṣṭarōma: piṣṭarasatulyaṃ piṣṭamēhī; āvilaṃ sāndraṃ sāndramahī; śukratulyaṃ śukramahī; stōkaṃ stōkaṃ saphenamacchaṃ phenamēhī mēhati
commentary: One suffering from udakameha micturates whitish, watery (urine) without pain. One suffering from ikṣuvālikāmeha (micturates urine) like sugarcane juice. One suffering from surāmeha (micturates urine) like wine. One suffering from sikatāmeha (micturates urine) with pain, mixed with gravel. One suffering from śanairmeha slowly (micturates) mucoid muddy (urine). One suffering from lavanameha (micturates) clear (urine) like saline water. One suffering from piṣṭameha has horripilation and (micturates urine) like water mixed with ground flour. One suffering from sāndrameha passes turbid and concentrated (urine). One suffering from śukrameha passes (urine) similar to semen. One suffering from phenameha micturates clear and foamy urine in small quantities repeatedly.

topic_heading: Clinical Features of Urinary Abnormalities due to Pitta
sanskrit_text: अत ऊर्ध्वं पित्तनिमित्तान वक्ष्याम:—सफेनमच्छं नीलं नीलमेही मेहति ; सदाहं हरिद्राभं हरिद्रामेही ; अम्लरसगन्धमम्लमेही ; स्रतक्षारप्रतिमं क्षारमेही; मञ्जिष्ठोदकप्रकाशं मडिजष्ठामेही ; शोणितप्रकाशं शोणितमेही मेहति
transliteration: ata ūrdhvaṃ pittanimittāna vakṣyāma:—saphenamacchaṃ nīlaṃ nīlamehī mehati ; sadāhaṃ haridrābhaṃ haridrāmehī ; amlarasagandhamamlamehī ; sratakṣārapratimaṃ kṣāramehī; mañjiṣṭhodakaprakāśaṃ maḍijaṣṭhāmehī ; śoṇitaprakāśaṃ śoṇitamehī mehati
commentary: Now we would hereafter describe the (urinary abnormalities) caused by (vitiated) pitta. One suffering from nīlameha micturates foamy, clear and bluish (urine). One suffering from haridrāmeha (passes urine) of turmeric colour alongwith burning pain. One suffering from amlameha (passes urine) of sour taste and odour. One suffering from kṣārameha (passes urine) like solution of alkalies. One suffering from mañjiṣṭhāmeha (passes urine) like mañjiṣṭhā water. One suffering from śoṇitameha passes urine like blood.

topic_heading: Clinical Features of Urinary Abnormalities due to Vāta
sanskrit_text: सपिमेंहो अत ऊर्ध्वं वातनिमित्तान् वक्ष्याम:—सर्पिःप्रकाशं मेहति; वसाप्रकाशं वसामेही; क्षौद्ररसवर्णं क्षौद्रमेही; मत्तमातड्य- वदनुप्रबन्धं हस्तिमेही मेहति
transliteration: sapimeṃho ata ūrdhvaṃ vātanimittān vakṣyāma:—sarpiḥprakāśaṃ mehati; vasāprakāśaṃ vasāmehī; kṣaudrarasavarṇaṃ kṣaudramehī; mattamātaḍya- vadanuprabandhaṃ hastimehī mehati
commentary: Now we would hereafter describe the (urinary abnormalities) caused by (vitiated) vāta. One suffering from sarpirmeha micturates urine like ghee. One suffering from vasāmeha (passes urine) like fat. One suffering from kṣaudrameha (passes urine) of the colour of honey. One suffering from hastimeha (passes urine) unrestrained like an intoxicated elephant.

topic_heading: Doṣawise Complications of the Urinary Abnormalities
sanskrit_text: हौथि- प्रतिइयायः मक्षिकोपसर्पणमालस्यं मांसोपचयः इलेटम- ल्यारोचकाविपाकाः कफप्रसेकच्छर्दिनिद्राकासइवासाइचेति मेढतोदो हदि बस्तिभेदो वषणयोरवदरणं जानामपद्रवा: ; इालमम्लीकाज्वरातीसारारोचका वमथः परिधपनं दाहो मुर्च्छा पिपासा निद्रानाशः पाण्डरोगः पीतविण्मत्रनेत्रत्वं चेति पैत्तिकानां; हृद्ग्रहो लौल्यमनिद्रा स्तम्भः कम्पः शूलं बद्धपुरीषत्वं चेति वातजानाम् एवमेते विंशति प्रमेहाः सोपद्रवा व्याख्याताः
transliteration: hauthi- prati iyāyaḥ makṣikopasarpaṇamālasyaṃ māṃsopacayaḥ ileṭama- lyārocakāvipākāḥ kaphaprasekacchardinidrākāsaivāsāiceti meḍhatodo hadi bastibhedo vaṣaṇayoravadaraṇaṃ jānām apadravā: ; iālamamlīkājvarātīsārārocakā vamathaḥ paridhapanaṃ dāho murcchā pipāsā nidrānāśaḥ pāṇḍarogaḥ pītaviṇmatranetratvaṃ ceti paittikānāṃ; hṛdgraho laulyamanidrā stambhaḥ kampaḥ śūlaṃ baddhapurīṣatvaṃ ceti vātajānām evamete viṃśati pramehāḥ sopadravā vyākhyātāḥ
commentary: The complications of urinary abnormalities, of kapha origin are : sitting of the flies, lassitude, muscular hypertrophy, corrhyza, lethargy, distaste for food, indigestion, mucous discharge, vomitting, (excessive) sleep, cough and breathlessness. The complications of urinary abnormalities of pitta origin are : tearing sensation in both the testes, tearing sensation of urinary bladder, pricking pain in penis, precordial pain, sour eructations, fever, diarrhoea, distaste for food, vomiting, feeling of emission of fumes alround, burning sensation, unconciousness, thirst, insomnia, anaemia and yellowish discolouration of stool, urine and eyes. The complications of urinary abnormalities of vāta origin are : constricting sensation in the precordium, craving for varying tastes, insomnia, rigidity, tremor, colics and constipation. Thus these twenty urinary abnormalities alongwith their complications have been described.

topic_heading: Pathogenesis and Types of Associated Boils
sanskrit_text: त्रिभिर्दीषैहचान्गतधातोः वसामेदोभ्यामभिपन्नशरीरस्य तत्र प्रमेहिणा सर्षपिका, दश पिडका जायन्ते । तद्यथी——शराविका, कच्छपिका, जालिनी, विनता, पुत्रिणी, मसूरिका, अलजी, विदारिका, विद्रधिका चेति
transliteration: tribhirdīṣaihacān gatadhātoḥ vasāmedobhyāmabhipannaśarīrasya tatra pramehiṇā sarṣapikā, daśa piḍakā jāyante | tadyathī——śarāvikā, kacchapikā, jālinī, vinatā, putriṇī, masūrikā, alajī, vidārikā, vidradhikā ceti
commentary: Now the three vitiated doṣas, after spreading in the tissues with excessive fat and fatty tissues in patients suffering from urinary abnormalities, produce ten types of boils (piḍakās). They are : śarāvikā, sarṣapikā, kacchapikā, jālinī, vinatā, putriṇī, masūrikā, alajī, vidārikā, and vidradhikā.

topic_heading: Clinical Features of Boils (Śarāvikā and Sarṣapikā)
sanskrit_text: शरावमात्रा तद्रपा निम्नमध्या शराविका। गौरसर्षपसंस्थाना तत्प्रमाणा च सार्षपी
transliteration: śarāvamātrā tadrapā nimnamadhyā śarāvikā | gaurasarṣapasaṃsthānā tatpramāṇā ca sārṣapī
commentary: Śarāvikā is of the appearance and size of an earthen saucer with depression in the centre. And sarṣapikā is of the shape and size of white mustard.

topic_heading: Clinical Features of Boils (Kacchapikā and Jālinī)
sanskrit_text: सदाहा क्र्मसंस्थाना ज्ञेया कच्छपिका बुधै : । जालिनी तींव्रदाहा त्र मांसजालसमावृता
transliteration: sadāhā krmasaṃsthānā jñeyā kacchapikā budhai : | jālinī tīṃvradāhā tra māṃsajālasamāvṛtā
commentary: The kacchapikā should be known by the wise to be associated with burning sensation and to be of the shape of a tortoise. Jālinī, on the other hand, has severe burning pain and is surrounded by a network of fleshy mass.

topic_heading: Clinical Features of Boils (Vinatā and Putriṇī)
sanskrit_text: महती पिडका नीला पिडका विनता स्मृता। महत्यल्पाचिता ज्ञेया पिडका सा तु पुत्रिणी
transliteration: mahatī piḍakā nīlā piḍakā vinatā smṛtā | mahatyalpācitā jñeyā piḍakā sā tu putriṇī
commentary: The vinatā boil is known to be the big and blue boil. That boil which is big in size surrounded by multiple small boils should be known as putriṇī.

topic_heading: Clinical Features of Boils (Masūrikā and Alajī)
sanskrit_text: मसरसमसंस्थाना ज्ञेया सा तु मसूरिका। रक्ता सिता स्फोटवती दारुणो त्वलजी भवेत्
transliteration: masarasamasaṃsthānā jñeyā sā tu masūrikā | raktā sitā sphoṭavatī dāruṇo tvalajī bhavet
commentary: A (boil) similar to lentils should be known as masūrikā (boil). And alaji, on the other hand, is reddish-white alongwith blisters and induration.

topic_heading: Clinical Features of Boils (Vidārikā and Vidradhikā)
sanskrit_text: विदारीकन्दवहत्ता कठिना च विदारिका। विद्रधेर्लक्षणैर्य क्ता ज्ञेया विद्रधिका बुधैः
transliteration: vidārīkandavahattā kaṭhinā ca vidārikā | vidradherlakṣaṇairyaktā jñeyā vidradhikā budhaiḥ
commentary: Vidārikā is round and hard like a gourd. The boil which is associated with the features of an abscess should be known by the wise as vidradhikā.

sanskrit_text: ये यन्मयाः स्मृता मेहास्तेषामेतास्त्र तत्कृताः। गुदे हृदि शिरस्यंसे पृष्ठे मर्मणि चोत्थिताः। सोपद्रवा दूर्बलाग्नेः पिडकाः परिवर्जयेत्
transliteration: ye yanmayāḥ smṛtā mehāsteṣāmetāstra tatkṛtāḥ | gude hṛdi śirasyamse pṛṣṭhe marmaṇi cotthitāḥ | sopadravā dūrbalāgneḥ piḍakāḥ parivarjayet
commentary: The aetiological factors which are responsible for the urinary abnormalities are also the causes of these (boils). The boils arising in the rectum, precordial region, head, shoulders, back and on the vital spots associated with complications in a person with weak digestive power should be discarded (from treatment, because of their incurability).

topic_heading: The Incurability of Boils of Vāta Origin
sanskrit_text: कृत्स्नं शरीरं निष्पीडच मेदोमज्जवसायुतः। अधः प्रक्रमते वायु स्तेनासाध्यास्त्र वातजाः
transliteration: kṛtsnaṃ śarīraṃ niṣpīḍaca medomajjavasāyutaḥ | adhaḥ prakramate vāyu stenāsādhyāstra vātajāḥ
commentary: The vāyu alongwith meda, majjā, and vasā, having gripped the body all over comes down; hence the boils of vāta origin are definitely incurable.

sanskrit_text: प्रमेहपूर्वरूपाणामाकृतिर्यत्र दृश्यते। किच्चाप्यधिकं मुत्रं त प्रमेहिणमादिशेत्। कृत्स्नान्यर्धानि वा यस्मिन् पूर्वरूपाणि मानवे। प्रवृत्तमूत्रमत्यर्थं तं प्रमेहिणमादिशेत
transliteration: pramehapūrvarūpāṇāmākṛtiryatra dṛśyate | kiccāpyadhikaṃ mutraṃ ta pramehiṇamādiśet | kṛtsnānyardhāni vā yasmin pūrvarūpāṇi mānave | pravṛttamūtramatyarthaṃ taṃ pramehiṇamādiśeta
commentary: In whomsoever the prodromal features of urinary abnormalities are seen and even if there is a slight increase in urine, he should be considered to be a pramehī (one suffering from urinary abnormalities). In whomsoever person the prodromal features are present fully or partially and who has an excessive urination should be considered to be a pramehī.

sanskrit_text: पिडकापाडित गाढमपसब्टमपद्रवः। मध्मेहिनमाचष्टे स चासाध्यः प्रकीतितः। स चापि गमनात् स्थानं स्थानादासनमिच्छति। आसनाद्वृणुते शय्यां शयनात् स्वप्नमिच्छति
transliteration: piḍakāpāḍita gāḍhamapasabṭamapadravaḥ | madhmehinamācaṣṭe sa cāsādhyaḥ prakītitaḥ | sa cāpi gamanāt sthānaṃ sthānādāsanamicchati | āsanādvṛṇute śayyāṃ śayanāt svapnamicchati
commentary: One who is suffering from boils and has severe complications is called madhumehī and that is considered incurable. And he prefers to stand rather than move from place to place, prefers sitting to standing, lying down to sitting, and desires to sleep rather than lie down in bed.

topic_heading: Further Considerations on the Pathogenesis of Prameha and Madhumeha
sanskrit_text: संयोगविहोषेण यथा हि वर्णानां पञ्चानामत्कर्षापकर्षकृतेन शबलबभ्रुकपिलकपोतमेचकादीनां वर्णानामनेकेषामत्पत्तिर्भवति,एवमेव दोषधात्रमलाहारविशेषेणोत्कर्षापकर्षक्रतेन 'संयोगविहोषण प्रमेहाणी नानाकरणं भवति। भवति चात्र—— सर्व एव प्रमेहास्तु कालेनाप्रतिकुर्वतः। मधुर्मेहत्वमायान्ति तदाऽसाध्या भवन्ति हि
transliteration: saṃyogavihoṣeṇa yathā hi varṇānāṃ pañcānāmatkarṣāpakarṣakṛtena śabalababhrukapilakapotamecakādīnāṃ varṇānāmanekeṣāmatpattirbhavati, evameva doṣadhātramalāhāraviśeṣeṇotkarṣāpakarṣakr tena 'saṃyogavihoṣaṇa pramehāṇī nānākaraṇaṃ bhavati | bhavati cātra—— sarva eva pramehāstu kālenāpratikurvataḥ | madhurmehatvamāyānti tadā'sādhyā bhavanti hi
commentary: Just as by an increase or decrease of and by specific combinations of the five colours various other colours like śabala, babhru, kapila, kapota, mecaka etc. are produced, similarly by specific increase or decrease of and by the specific combination of the doṣas, dhātus, malas and foods, various types of urinary abnormalities are produced. The (following verse) has been quoted in this context : All types of urinary abnormalities, if not treated in time develop madhumeha and then become incurable.

sanskrit_text: अथात उदराणां निदानं व्याख्यास्यामः
transliteration: athāta udarāṇāṃ nidānaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ
commentary: Now we would expound upon 'The Diagnosis of Abdominal Enlargements'.

sanskrit_text: यथोवाच भगवान् धन्वन्तरिः
transliteration: yathovāca bhagavān dhanvantariḥ
commentary: As was described by Lord Dhanvantari.

sanskrit_text: धन्वन्तरिर्धर्मभुतां वरिष्ठो राजर्षिरिन्वप्रतिमोऽभवद्यः। ब्रह्म्र्षिपुत्रं विनयोपपन्नं शिष्यं शुभं सुथ्रुतमन्वशात् सः
transliteration: dhanvantarirdharmabhutāṃ variṣṭho rājarṣirinvapratimo'bhavadyaḥ | brahmrṣiputraṃ vinayopapannaṃ śiṣyaṃ śubhaṃ sut hrutamanvaśāt saḥ
commentary: Dhanvantari, greatest amongst the religious, sage amongst the kings and who was equal (in glory) to Indra, thus discoursed to the noble and modest student Suśruta, son of Brahmarsi.

topic_heading: The Eight Types of Abdominal Enlargements
sanskrit_text: प्थक् समस्तैरपि चेह दोषैः प्लीहोदरं बद्धगुदं तथैव। आगन्तुकं सप्तममष्टमं च दकोदरं चेति वदन्ति तानि
transliteration: pthak samastairapi ceha doṣaiḥ plīhodaraṃ baddhagudaṃ tathaiva | āgantukaṃ saptamamaṣṭamaṃ ca dakodaraṃ ceti vadanti tāni
commentary: There are eight types of abdominal enlargements : those due to the three doṣas seperately (vātodara, pittodara, kaphodara), that due to all the vitiated doṣas together, plīhodara, and baddhaguda; āgantuka is the seventh and dakodara is the eighth one.

sanskrit_text: स दूर्बलाग्नेरहिताशनस्य संशुष्कप्वत्यन्ननिषेवणाद्वा। स्नेहादिमिथ्याचरणाच्च जन्तोर्व द्धि गताः कोष्ठमभिप्रपन्नाः। गुल्माकृतिव्यञ्जितलक्षणानि कुर्वन्ति घोराण्यदराणि दोषाः। कोष्ठाद्रपस्नेहवदन्नसारो निःसृत्य द्रष्टोऽनिलवेगन्नः। त्वचः समुन्नम्य शनैः समन्ताद्विवर्धमानो जठरं करोति।
transliteration: sa dūrbalāgnerahitāśanasya saṃśuṣkapvatyannaniṣevaṇādvā | snehādimithyācaraṇācca jantorva d dhi gatāḥ koṣṭhamabhiprapannāḥ | gulmākṛtivyañjitalakṣaṇāni kurvanti ghorāṇyadarāṇi doṣāḥ | koṣṭhādrapasnehavadannasāro niḥsṛtya draṣṭo'nilavegannaḥ | tvacaḥ samunnamya śanaiḥ samantādvivardhamāno jaṭharaṃ karoti |
commentary: Due to partaking of non-beneficial diets and due to the use of dry and putrified foods by persons of extremely weak digestion and due to the faulty use of oleation etc., the doṣas get loacted in the abdomen, and having increased therein manifest symptoms of a rounded abdominal swelling and cause severe abdominal diseases. Aetiology of Distension of Abdomen in Abdominal Diseases: As oil percolates out of a new earthen pot, similarly the extract of digested food comes out of the abdominal organs due to the pressure of vāta, becomes vitiated and goes on increasing, and thus gradually increasing raises the skin all over and produces abdominal enlargement.

sanskrit_text: तत्पुर्वरूपं बलवर्णकाङ क्षावलीविनाशो जठरे हि राज्यः। जीर्णापरिज्ञानविदाहवत्यो बस्तौ रुजः पादगतश्च शोफः।
transliteration: tatpurvarūpaṃ balavarṇakāṅ kṣāvalīvināśo jaṭhare hi rājyaḥ | jīrṇāparijñānavidāhavatyo bastau rujaḥ pādagataśca śophaḥ |
commentary: Their prodromal features are a diminution of strength and of complexion, loss of appetite, obliteration of abdominal folds, appearance of striae on the abdominal wall, inability to know when digestion is complete, burning sensation, pain in urinary bladder region and oedema over the feet.

sanskrit_text: संग्रह्य पार्र्वोदरप्रष्ठनाभीर्यद्वर्धते कृष्णसिरावनद्वम्। सशूलमानाहवदुग्रशब्दं सतोदभेदं पवनात्मकं तत्।
transliteration: saṃgrahya pārrvodarapraṣṭhanābhīryadvardhate kṛṣṇasirāvanadvam | saśūlamānāhavadugraśabdaṃ satodabhedaṃ pavanātmakaṃ tat |
commentary: When vāta increases after having got located in the sides, abdomen, back and umbilical region, prominence of bluish veins occurs and it produces loud noise with pain, as in meteorism alongwith pricking and tearing sensation, that (abdominal enlargement) is due to vāta.

sanskrit_text: यच्चोषतृष्णाज्वरदाहयुक्तं पीतं सिरा भान्ति च यत्र पीताः। पीताक्षिविण्म्त्रनखाननस्य पित्तोदरं तत्त्वचिराभिवृद्धि।
transliteration: yaccoṣatṛṣṇājvaradāhayuktaṃ pītaṃ sirā bhānti ca yatra pītāḥ | pītākṣiviṇmtranakhānanasya pittodaraṃ tattvacirābhivṛddhi |
commentary: When there is sucking pain, thirst, fever, burning sensation and yellow colouration, and when veins and complexion alongwith eyes, stool, urine, nail and face become yellow, it should be known as pittodara and it increases rapidly.

sanskrit_text: यच्छीतलं श्क्लसिरावनद्धं गुरु स्थिरं शुक्लनखाननस्य। स्निग्धं महच्छोफयुतं ससादं कफोदरं तत्तु चिराभिवृद्धि।
transliteration: yacchītalaṃ śklasirāvanaddhaṃ guru sthiraṃ śuklanakhānanasya | snigdhaṃ mahacchophayutaṃ sasādaṃ kaphodaraṃ tattu cirābhivṛddhi |
commentary: When there is a feeling of coldness, prominence of white veins, feeling of heaviness, stasis, whiteness of the nails and face, sliminess, marked oedema and lassitude, it should be known as kaphodara and it increases slowly.

sanskrit_text: स्त्रियोऽन्नपानं नखरोममूत्रविडार्तवैर्यंक्तमसाधुवृत्ताः। यस्मै प्रयच्छन्त्यरयो गरांशच दुष्टाम्बदूषीविषसेवनाद्वा। तेनाशु रक्तं कुपिताइच दोषाः कुर्वन्ति घोरं जठरं त्रिलिड्मम्। तच्छीतवाताभासमुद्भवेषु विशेषतः कुप्यति दहचते च। स चातुरो मूर्च्छति संप्रसक्तं पाण्डुः कृशः शुष्यति तृष्णया च। प्रकीर्तितं दृष्युदरंतु घोरं प्लीहोदरं कीर्तयतो निबोध।
transliteration: striyo'nnapānaṃ nakharomamūtraviḍārtavairyaṃktamasādhuvṛttāḥ | yasmai prayacchantyarayo garāṃśaca duṣṭāmbadūṣīviṣasevanādvā | tenāśu raktaṃ kupitāica doṣāḥ kurvanti ghoraṃ jaṭharaṃ triliḍmam | tacchītavātābhāsamudbhaveṣu viśeṣataḥ kupyati dahacate ca | sa cāturo mūrcchati saṃprasaktaṃ pāṇḍuḥ kṛśaḥ śuṣyati tṛṣṇayā ca | prakīrtitaṃ dṛṣyudaraṃtu ghoraṃ plīhodaraṃ kīrtayato nibodha |
commentary: The blood and doṣas get vitiated soon and produce severe abdominal disorders (sannipātodara) with the symptoms of all the three doṣas in persons to whom women with unrighteous behaviour offer food and drinks mixed with nails, hairs, urine, faeces and menstrual fluid, and to whom enemies give 'gara' poison or who use contaminated water or 'dūṣī' poison. That (disease) is aggravated and produces burning sensation specially during the cold, windy and cloudy weather. And that patient faints repeatedly, becomes anaemic, emaciated and dehydrated due to thirst. This is the description of severe dūṣyudara. Now please listen to the description of plīhodara.

sanskrit_text: विदाह्यभिष्यन्दिरतस्य जन्तोः प्रद्रष्टमत्यर्थमसुक् कफइच। प्लीहाभिवृद्धिं सततं करोति प्लीहोदरं तत् प्रवदन्ति तज्ज्ञाः। वामे च पार्श्वे परिवृद्धिमेति विशेषतः सीदति चातुरोऽत्र। मन्दज्वराग्निः कफप्तिलिड्नैरुपद्रुतः क्षीणबलोऽतिपाण्डुः। सब्येतरस्मिन् यक्रृति प्रदुष्टे ज्ञेयं यक्रद्दाल्युदर्र तर्देव।
transliteration: vidāhyabhiṣyandiratasya jantoḥ pradraṣṭamatyarthamasuk kaphaica | plīhābhivṛddhiṃ satataṃ karoti plīhodaraṃ tat pravadanti tajjñāḥ | vāme ca pārśve parivṛddhim eti viśeṣataḥ sīdati cāturo'tra | mandajvarāgniḥ kaphtiliḍnairupadrutaḥ kṣīṇabalo'tipāṇḍuḥ | sabyetarasmin yakṛti praduṣṭe jñeyaṃ yakṛddālyudarra tardaiva |
commentary: The blood and kapha get excessively vitiated in that person who takes hot and abhisyandī food, which then enlarges the spleen and that is said to be plīhodara by the learned. It (spleen) increases on the left side (of the abdomen) and the patient in this disease gets fatigued particularly. Mild fever and weak digestion with the symptoms of kapha and pitta and loss of strength and severe anaemia occur. If same features appear on the right side (of the abdomen) and the liver is involved, it should be known as yakṛddālyudara.

sanskrit_text: यस्यान्त्रमन्नैरुपलेपिभिर्वा बालाइमभिर्वा सहितैः प्रथग्वा। संचीयते तत्र मलः सदोषः ऋमण नाड्यामिव संकरो हि। निरुध्यते चास्य गुदें पुरीषं निरेति कृच्छ ादपि चाल्पमल्पम्। हन्नाभिमध्ये परिवद्धिमेति त (य)च्चोदरं विद्समगन्धिकं च। प्रच्छर्दयन् बद्धगुदी विभाव्यः, ततः परिस्राव्युदरं निबोध।
transliteration: yasyāntramannairupalepibhirvā bālāim abhirvā sahitaiḥ prathagvā | saṃcīyate tatra malaḥ sadoṣaḥ ṛmaṇa nāḍyāmiva saṃkaro hi | nirudhyate cāsya gudeṃ purīṣaṃ nireti kṛcchād api cālpamalpam | hannābhimadhye parivaddhim eti ta (ya)ccodaraṃ vidsamagandhikaṃ ca | pracchardayan baddhagudī vibhāvyaḥ, tataḥ parisrāvyudaraṃ nibodha |
commentary: When food or slimy substances, hair or small stones gather collectively or separately in the intestines of the patient, the faeces alongwith the doṣas gradually accumulate in him like that in a drain. The faeces then get obstructed in his rectum and even when it comes out, it is in very small amounts and with difficulty. It distends his abdomen between the precordium and umbilicus and faecal smell is present in the vomitus; this condition should be known as baddhagudodara. Now please listen to the description of parisrāvyudara.

topic_heading: Parisrāvyudara (Āgantuka or Foreign Bodies causing perforation)
sanskrit_text: शल्यं यदन्नोपहितं तदन्त्रं भिनत्ति यस्यागतमन्यथा वा। तस्मात स्रतोऽन्त्रात सलिलप्रकाशः स्रावः स्रवेद्व गदतस्त्र भयः। नाभेरधइचोदरमेति वृद्धिं निस्तुद्यतेऽतीव विदह्यते च। कीर्तयतो निबोध । दकोदरं परिस्राव्यदरं प्रदिष्टं एतत्
transliteration: śalyaṃ yadannopahitaṃ tadantraṃ bhinatti yasyāgatamanyathā vā | tasmāt srato'ntrāt salilaprakāśaḥ srāvaḥ sravedva gadatastra bhayaḥ | nābheradhaicodarameti vṛddhiṃ nistudyate'tīva vidahyate ca | kīrtayato nibodha | dakodaraṃ parisrāvyadaraṃ pradiṣṭaṃ etat
commentary: When a foreign body taken alongwith food or otherwise lies abnormally it pierces the intestines. An exudation, like water, comes out of the patient's intestines and also a similar exudation is discharged from his rectum. This distends the abdomen below the umbilicus and causes severe pricking and burning sensation. This is called parisrāvyudara. Now please listen to the description of dakodara.

sanskrit_text: यः।स्नेहपीतोऽप्यनवासितो वा वान्तो विरिक्तोऽप्यथवा निरूढः। पिबेज्जलं शीतलमाशु तस्य स्रोतांसि दुष्यन्ति हि तद्वहानि। स्नेहोपलिप्तेष्वथवाऽपि तेषु दकादरं पूर्ववदभ्युपैति। स्निग्धं महत संपरिवत्तनाभि भूशीन्नतं पूर्णमिवाम्बुना च। यथा दृतिः क्षुभ्यति कम्पते च शब्दायते चापि दकोदरं तत्।
transliteration: yaḥ | snehapīto'pyanavāsito vā vānto virikto'pyathavā nirūḍhaḥ | pibejjalaṃ śītalamāśu tasya srotāṃsi duṣyanti hi tadvahāni | snehopalip teṣvathavā'pi teṣu dakādaraṃ pūrvavadabhyupaiti | snigdhaṃ mahata saṃparivattanābhi bhūśīnnataṃ pūrṇamivāmbunā ca | yathā dṛtiḥ kṣubhyati kampate ca śabdāyate cāpi dakodaraṃ tat |
commentary: The water carrying channels of the person, who drinks cold water soon after oleation, oily enemas, emesis, purgation or after taking enemas of medicated decoctions, get vitiated. And even if those (channels) are lined by oily substance, dakodara occurs as in the preceeding one (parisrāvyudara). The abdomen becomes very smooth, distends alround and the umbilicus gets definitely everted as if full of water. Just as a leather bag full of water and air shakes, fluctuates and makes sounds, similar features are produced in dakodara.

sanskrit_text: आध्मानं गमनेऽशक्तिदौर्बल्यं दुर्बलाग्निता। शोफः सदनमङ्गनां सङ्गो वातपुरीषयोः। दाहस्तुष्णा च सर्वेंष् जठरेष भवन्ति हि।
transliteration: ādhmānaṃ gamane'śaktidaurbalyaṃ durbalāgnitā | śophaḥ sadanamaṅganāṃ saṅgo vātapurīṣayoḥ | dāhastuṣṇā ca sarveṃṣ jaṭhareṣa bhavanti hi |
commentary: Tympanitis, inability to walk, weakness, weak digestion, oedema, lassitude in the limbs, obstruction to the passage of flatus and faeces, burning and thirst occur in all types of abdominal diseases.

sanskrit_text: अन्ते सलिलभावं हि भजन्ते जठराणि त्र। सर्वाण्येव परीपाकात्तदा तानि विवर्जयेत्
transliteration: ante salilabhāvaṃ hi bhajante jaṭharāṇi tra | sarvāṇyeva parīpākāttadā tāni vivarjayet
commentary: Water collects ultimately in all abdominal enlargements in due course of time and then the same should be discarded (from treatment).

sanskrit_text: अथातो मुढगर्भनिदानं व्याख्यास्यामः
transliteration: athāto muḍhagarbhanidānaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ
commentary: Now we would expound upon 'The Diagnosis of Abnormal Foetal Presentations'.

sanskrit_text: यथोवाच भगवान धन्वतरिः
transliteration: yathovāca bhagavān dhanvatariḥ
commentary: As was described by Lord Dhanvantari.

sanskrit_text: ग्राम्यधर्मयानवाहनाध्वगमनप्रस्खलनप्रपतनप्रपीडनधावनाभिघात- विषमशयनासनोपवासवेगाभिघातातिरूक्षकट्तिक्तभो जलशोकातिक्षार- सेवनातिसारवमनविरेचनप्रेड्वोलनाजीर्णगर्भइातनप्रभूतिभिविशेषर्बन्ध- गर्भः, फलमिव नान्मच्यते स विमुक्तबन्धनो गर्भाशयमतिऋभ्य यकृत्प्लीहान्त्रविवरैरवस्रंसमानः कोष्ठसंक्षोभमापादयति, तस्या जठरसंक्षोभाद्वायुरपानो मूढः पार्श्व- बस्तिशीर्षोदरयोनिशूलानाहमूत्रसङ्गनामन्यतममापाद्ध गर्भं च्यावयति तरुणं शोणितस्रावेण ; तर्मेव क्रदाचिद्विवृद्धमसम्यगागतमपत्यपथमनु- है प्राप्तमनिरस्यमानं विगुणावानसंमोहितं गर्भ मूढगर्भभित्याचक्षते
transliteration: grāmyadharmayānavāhanādhvagamanaprasakhalanaprapatanaprapīḍanadhāvanābhighāta- viṣamaśayanāsanopavāsavegābhighātātirūkṣakaṭtiktabho jalaśokātikṣāra- sevanātisāravamanavirecanapreḍvolanājīrṇagarbhaātana prabhūtibhiviśeṣarbandha- garbhaḥ, phalamiva nānmacyate sa vimuktabandhano garbhāśayamatirbhya yakṛtplīhāntravivarairavastraṃsamānaḥ koṣṭhasaṃkṣobhamāpādayati, tasyā jaṭharasaṃkṣobhādvāyurapāno mūḍhaḥ pārśva- bastiśīrṣodayayoniśūlānāhamūtrasaṅganāmanyatamamāpāddha garbhaṃ cyāvayati taruṇaṃ śoṇitasrāveṇa ; tarmeva kradācidvivṛddhamasamyagāgatamapatyapathamanu- hai prāptamanirasyamānaṃ viguṇāvānasaṃmohitaṃ garbha mūḍhagarbhabhityācakṣate
commentary: Sexual intercourse, use of a vehicle, riding, walking on foot, slipping, falling, compression, running, trauma, use of an uneven bed or seat, fasting, suppression of nature's calls, excessively dry, acrid and bitter diet, grief, excessive use of alkalies, diarrhoea, vomiting, purgatives, swinging, indigestion, use of abortifacients etc; these causes specially release the foetus from its supports just as a fruit gets specifically severed off from its stalk by a blow. The (foetus), having been released from its supports, leaves the uterus and getting through the space between the liver, spleen and the intestines, produces agitation in the abdomen. In her, (the mother), due to agitation in the abdomen, the apāna vāyu becomes abnormal and having produced any one of these symptoms, such as pain in the sides, bladder region, abdomen or vagina and severe constipation or retention of urine, causes abortion of the young foetus alongwith discharge of blood. If the same (foetus) sometimes increases in size, travels to the foetal passage abnormally and does not come out, as well as gets stupified, because of vitiation of apāna vāyu, then that foetus is called a mūḍhagarbha.

sanskrit_text: ततः कीलः प्रतिख़ुरो बीजंकः परिघ इति । तत्र, ऊर्ध्वबाहुशि- र:पादो यो योनिमुखं निरुणद्धि कोल इव स कोलः; नि:सृतहस्तपाद- शिराः कायसड्झी प्रतिख़रः; यो निर्गच्छत्येकशिरोभ़जः स बीजकः; यस्तु परिघ इव योनिमुखमावृत्य तिष्ठति स परिघः; इति चतुर्विधो भवतीत्येके भाषन्ते । तत्त न सम्यक् ; कस्मात् ? स यदा विगुणानिल- प्रपीडितोऽपत्यपथमनेक्वा प्रपद्यते तदा संखचा हीयते
transliteration: tataḥ kīlaḥ pratikhu ro bījaṃkaḥ parigha iti | tatra, ūrdhvabāhuśi- ra:pādo yo yonimukhaṃ niruṇaddhi kola iva sa kolaḥ; niḥsṛtahastapāda- śirāḥ kāyasaḍjhī pratikha raḥ; yo nirgacchatyekaśirobha jaḥ sa bījakaḥ; yastu parigha iva yonimukhamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati sa parighaḥ; iti caturvidho bhavatītyeke bhāṣante | tatta na samyak ; kasmāt ? sa yadā viguṇānila- prapīḍito'patyapathamanekvā prapadyate tadā saṃkhacā hīyate
commentary: Kīla, pratikhura, bījaka and parigha are the types of mūḍhagarbhas (described by some). That foetus is kīla in which the upper extremeties and the head and feet point upwards and which obstructs the mouth of vagina like a peg. When the hands, feet and head come out and the body remains inside—that is called pratikhura. Bījaka is that in which the head and one limb are out. That in which the foetus is situated at the mouth of vagina having covered it like an iron bar used for closing the door is called parigha. Thus some describe four types of mūḍhagarbhas. That is not correct. Why so ? Because, the (foetus) gets compressed by the opposite acting vāyu and presents in the foetal passage in numerous ways and thus the numerical figure (of four) is quite insufficient.

sanskrit_text: तत्र, कहिचद्वाभ्यां सक्थिभ्यां योनिमुखं प्रतिपद्यते ; कहिचदा- भुग्नकसक्थिरकेन ; कश्चिदाभुग्नसक्थिशरीरः स्फिग्देशोन तिर्यगागतः ; कडिचद्रर:पार्श्वप्रष्ठानामन्यतमेन योनिद्वारं पिधायावतिष्ठते ; अन्तः पार्श्वापवत्तशिरा: कश्चिदेकेन बाह्वना ; कश्चिदाभुग्नशिरा बाह्वद्वयेन ; कडिचदाभुग्नमध्यो हस्तपादशिरोभिः; कडिचदेकेन सकथ्ना योनिम खं प्रतिपद्यतेऽपरेण पायुम् ; इत्यष्टविधा मूढगर्भगतिरुद्दिष्टा समासेन
transliteration: tatra, kahicadvābhyāṃ sakthibhyāṃ yonimukhaṃ pratipadyate ; kahicadā- bhugnakasakthirakena ; kaścidābhugnasakthiśarīraḥ sphigdeśona tiryagāgataḥ ; kaḍicadrara:pārśvapraṣṭhānāmanyatamena yonidvāraṃ pidhāyāvatiṣṭhate ; antaḥ pārśvāpavattaśirā: kaścidekena bāhvanā ; kaścidābhugnaśirā bāhvadvayena ; kaḍicadābhugnamadhyo hastapādaśirobhiḥ; kaḍicadekena sakathnā yonima khaṃ pratipadyate'pareṇa pāyum ; ityaṣṭavidhā mūḍhagarbhagatiruddiṣṭā samāsena
commentary: Out of them some present at the vaginal opening by the two lower limbs; some by one lower limb, the other one being flexed; some come out with both the lower limbs flexed over the body and the buttocks presenting obliquely; and some present by either chest, sides or back covering the vaginal exit. Some present by an arm only with the head flexed and turned to the sides; some present by both arms with the head bent; some present by the hands, feet and head with the trunk flexed; and some present at the opening of vagina by one lower limb and the other pointing towards (the mother's) anus. Thus the eight modes of presentations of mūḍhagarbhas have been described briefly.

sanskrit_text: तत्र द्वावन्त्यावसाध्यौ मुढगभौं, शेषानपि विपरीतेन्द्रियार्थाक्षेप- क्योनिभ्रंशसंवरणमक्कल्लइवासकासध्रमनिपीडितान् परिहरेत्
transliteration: tatra dvāvantyāvasādhyau muḍhagabha uṃ, śeṣānapi viparītendriyārthākṣepa- kyonibhraṃśasaṃvaraṇamakkkallaivāsakāsadhramanipīḍitān pariharet
commentary: Out of them, the last two types of mūḍhagarbhas are incurable. The rest also should be discarded (from treatment) if the mother has abnormal sensory perceptions, is troubled by convulsions, vaginal prolapse or retraction, or has puerperal sepsis, asthma, cough or mental confusion.

sanskrit_text: मेवान्त चान्त्र—— कालस्य' परिणामेन मुक्तं वुन्ताद्यथा फलम्। प्रपद्यते स्वभावेन नान्यथा पतितुं ध्रुवम्। एवं कालप्रकर्षेण मुक्तो नाडीनिबन्धनात् । गर्भांशयस्थो यो गर्भो जननाय प्रपद्यते
transliteration: mevānta cāntra—— kālasya' pariṇāmena muktaṃ vuntādyathā phalam | prapadyate svabhāvena nānyathā patituṃ dhruvam | evaṃ kālaprakarṣeṇa mukto nāḍīnibandhanāt | garbhāṃśayastho yo garbho jananāya prapadyate
commentary: The following verses have been quoted here: As by nature a fruit falls from its stalk upon maturation and certainly does not drop in any other way, similarly in due course of time the foetus, having been released from the supports of the cord, starts to come out for delivery from its location within the uterus.

sanskrit_text: कृमिवाताभिघातैस्तु तदेवोपद्रुतं फलम्। पतत्यकालेऽपि यथा तथा स्याद्गर्भविच्यतिः। आचतुर्थात्ततो मासात् प्रस्रवेद्गर्भविच्यतिः। ततः स्थिरइारीरस्य पातः पञ्चमषष्ठयोंः
transliteration: kṛmivātābhighātaistu tadevopadrutaṃ phalam | patatyakāle'pi yathā tathā syādgarbhavicyatiḥ | ācaturthāttato māsāt prasravedgarbhavicyatiḥ | tataḥ sthiraiārīrasya pātaḥ pañcamaṣaṣṭhayom̐ḥ
commentary: As a fruit affected by organisms, wind or trauma falls untimely, similarly a foetus can also be expelled (untimely). Upto the fourth month (of pregnancy) the foetus is aborted; thereafter in the fifth and sixth months the well formed body is miscarried.

sanskrit_text: प्रविध्यति शिरो या तु शीताङ्गी निरपत्रपा। नीलोद्वतसिरा हन्ति सा गर्भे स च तां तथा
transliteration: pravidhyati śiro yā tu śītāṅgī nira patrapā | nīlodvatasirā hanti sā garbhe sa ca tāṃ tathā
commentary: The (mother) who is constantly shaking her head and whose body feels cold or that woman who is shameless or has prominent bluish veins kills the foetus; so also the foetus kills her.

sanskrit_text: गर्भास्पन्दनमावीनां प्रणाशः इयावपाण्डता। भवत्युच्छ्वासपूतित्वं शूलं वान्तर्मृते शिशौ
transliteration: garbhāspandanamāvīnāṃ praṇāśaḥ iyāvapāṇḍatā | bhavatyucchvāsapūtitvaṃ śūlaṃ vāntarmṛte śiśau
commentary: Stoppage of foetal heart and labour pains, occurence of cyanosis or palor, foetid odour in the breath and pain occur after the death of the foetus.

sanskrit_text: मानसागन्तुभिर्मातुरुपतापैः प्रपीडितः। गर्भो व्यापद्यते कुक्षौ व्याधिभिइच प्रपीडितः
transliteration: mānasāgantubhirmāturupatāpaiḥ prapīḍitaḥ | garbho vyāpadyate kukṣau vyādhibhica prapīḍitaḥ
commentary: If the mother is suffering from mental or traumatic diseases or from other diseases the foetus dies within the womb.

sanskrit_text: वस्तमारविपन्नायाः कुक्षिः प्रस्पन्दते यदि। तत्क्षणाज्जन्मकाले तं पाटयित्वोद्धरें, द्विषक्
transliteration: vastamāravipannāyāḥ kukṣiḥ praspandate yadi | tatkṣaṇājjanmakāle taṃ pāṭayitvod'dhareṃ, dviṣak
commentary: If the beatings are still there in the womb (of the mother) in labour suffering as a dying goat, the physician should deliver out the foetus immediately, after opening the abdomen.

sanskrit_text: अथातो विद्रधीनां निदानं व्याख्यास्यामः
transliteration: athāto vidradhīnāṃ nidānaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ
commentary: Now we would expound upon 'The Diagnosis of Abscesses.'

sanskrit_text: यथोवाच भगवान् धन्वन्तरिः
transliteration: yathovāca bhagavān dhanvantariḥ
commentary: As was described by Lord Dhanvantari.

sanskrit_text: सर्वामरगुरः श्रीमान्निमित्तान्तरभूमिपः। शिष्यायोवाच निखिलमिदं विद्रधिलक्षणम्
transliteration: sarvāmaraguraḥ śrīmānnimittāntarabhūmipaḥ | śiṣyāyovāca nikhilamidaṃ vidradhilakṣaṇam
commentary: The revered amongst all the Gods, the most respected Lord Dhanvantari who had come on earth as a king with a specific purpose (to discourse on (Ayurveda) spoke to his disciple (Suśruta) all the following clinical features of an abscess.

sanskrit_text: त्वग्रक्तमांसमेदांसि प्रदूष्यास्थिसमाश्रिताः। दोषा: हाोफं हानैर्घोरं जनयन्त्यच्छिता भुशम्। महामुलं रुजावन्तं वृत्तं चाप्यथवाऽऽयतम्। तमार्हावर्द्रधि धीरा, विज्ञेयः स 'व षड्विधः। प्थग्दाषै: समस्तैइ'व क्षतेनाप्यस्जा तथा। षण्णामपि हि तेषां तु लक्षणं संप्रवक्ष्यते
transliteration: tvagraktamāṃsamedāṃsi praduṣyāsthisamāśritāḥ | doṣā: hāophaṃ hānairghoraṃ janayantyacchitā bhuśam | mahāmulaṃ rujāvantaṃ vṛttaṃ cāpyathavā''yatam | tamārhāvardradhi dhīrā, vijñeyaḥ sa 'va ṣaḍvidhaḥ | pthagdāṣai: samastaii'va kṣatenāpyasjā tathā | ṣaṇṇāmapi hi teṣāṃ tu lakṣaṇaṃ saṃpravakṣyate
commentary: The vitiated doṣas located in the bones afflict the skin, blood, muscles and fat and gradually produce excessively severe inflammatory swelling. The swelling (described above) which is broad based, painful and round or else elongated is known by the wise physician as an abscess and it is known to be of six types. The six types are those due to individual doṣas (vāta, pitta and kapha), and all together (all the doṣas mixed together), that due to trauma and that due to śoṇita. Clinical features of all these six types are now described.

sanskrit_text: क्टणोऽरुणो वा परुषो भु इामत्यर्थवेदनः। वित्रोत्थानप्रपाक्रहच विद्रधिर्वातसंभवः
transliteration: kṭaṇo'ruṇo vā paruṣo bhu iāmatyarthavedanaḥ | vitrotthānaprapākrahaca vidradhirvātasaṃbhavaḥ
commentary: The vātika abscess is black, red or rough and produces excessively severe pain. There are a variety of ways in which it can begin and suppurate.

sanskrit_text: पक्वोदुम्बरसङ्काहाः हयावो वा ज्वरदाहवान। क्षिप्रोत्थानप्रपाकइच विद्रधिः पित्तसंभवः
transliteration: pakvodumbarasaṅkāhāḥ hayāvo vā jvaradāhavāna | kṣiprotthānapapākaica vidradhiḥ pittasaṃbhavaḥ
commentary: The pitta abscess is like the ripe fruit of udumbara, is blackish, produces fever and burning sensation, has a sudden onset and suppurates quickly.

sanskrit_text: हारावसद् चिरोत्थानप्रपाक्रच सकण्ड्रइच कफोत्थितः
transliteration: hārāvasad cirotthānapapākraca sakaṇḍraica kaphotthitaḥ
commentary: Abscess produced due to kapha arises and suppurates late, is associated with itching, appears like an earthen saucer, is whitish, cold, indurated and has mild pain.

sanskrit_text: तनपीतसिताइचैषामास्रावाः ऋमशः स्मृताः
transliteration: tanapītasi tāicaiṣāmāsrāvāḥ ṛmaśaḥ smṛtāḥ
commentary: The discharges of these three are known to be thin, yellowish and whitish respectively.

topic_heading: Abscess due to Combination of the Doṣas
sanskrit_text: नानावर्णरुजास्त्रावो घाटालो विषमो महान्। चापि विद्रधिः सान्निपातिकः । विषमं पच्यते
transliteration: nānāvarṇarujāstrāvo ghāṭālo viṣamo mahān | cāpi vidradhiḥ sānnipātikaḥ | viṣamaṃ pacyate
commentary: And the abscess due to a combination of the doṣas suppurates irregularly, has multiple colours, pain and discharge, is raised, irregular and extensive.

sanskrit_text: तेस्तैभवैरभिहते क्षते वाऽपथ्यसेविनः। क्षतोष्मा वायु विसृतो सरवतं पित्तमीरयेत्। ज्वरस्तृtणा च दाहरच जायते तस्य देहिन:। एष विद्रधिरागन्तुः पित्तविद्रधिल्क्षणः।
transliteration: testaibhavairabhihate kṣate vā'pathyasevinaḥ | kṣatoṣmā vāyu visṛto saravataṃ pittamīrayet | jvarastṛtṇā ca dāharaca jāyate tasya dehina: | eṣa vidradhirāgantuḥ pittavidradhil kṣaṇaḥ |
commentary: Those who indulge in unsalutary diets and habits, if get a (closed) injury or an open wound caused by their respective agents, in them vāyu induces heat of the injury to vitiate pitta alongwith śoṇita. Fever, thirst, and burning are produced in his body. This is an abscess due to trauma and has the clinical features of a paittika abscess.

sanskrit_text: क्ष्णस्फोटावृत्तः इयावस्तीव्रदा हहजाज्वरः। पित्तविद्रधिलिङ्गस्तु रक्तविद्रधिरुच्यते।
transliteration: kṣṇasphoṭāvṛttaḥ iyāvastīvradā hahajājvaraḥ | pittavidradhiliṅgastu raktavidradhirucyate |
commentary: That is called a raktaja abscess which is covered by black blisters, is blackish, has severe burning, pain and fever and has the features of a pittaja abscess also.

sanskrit_text: उक्ता विद्रधयो ह्येते तेष्वसाध्यस्तु सर्वजः
transliteration: uktā vidradhayo hyete teṣvasādhyastu sarvajaḥ
commentary: Out of the abscesses mentioned above, the one caused by combination of the doṣas is incurable; (rest are curable).

sanskrit_text: आभ्यन्तरानतस्तुध्वं विद्रधीन परिचक्षते। ग्र्वसात्म्यविरुद्धान्नहाष्कसंस्प्टभोजनात्। अतिव्यवायव्यायामवेगाघातविदाहिभिः। प्रथक् संभूय वा दोषा: कुपिता गुल्मरूपिणम्। वल्मीकवत्समुन्नद्धमन्तः कुर्वन्ति विद्रधिम ।
transliteration: ābhyantarānatastudhvaṃ vidradhīna paricakṣate | grvasātmyaviruddhānnahāṣkasaṃspṭabhojanāt | ativyavāyavyāyāmavegāghātavidāhibhiḥ | prathak saṃbhūya vā doṣā: kupitā gulmarūpiṇam | valmīkavatsamunnaddhamantaḥ kurvanti vidradhim |
commentary: Hereafter, the internal abscesses are described. Due to taking of heavy, unsuitable, incompatible, dry, and contaminated foods, due to excessive indulgence in sexual intercourse and exercise, due to suppression of nature's calls, and due to the use of hot substances, the doṣas get vitiated singly or in combination and produce internal abscess of the shape of a (bush like) tumour elevated like an anthill.

topic_heading: Sites and Clinical Features of Internal Abscesses
sanskrit_text: गदे बस्तिमुखे नाभ्यां कुक्षौ वङ् क्षणयोस्तथा। वक्कयोर्यक्रति प्लीह्नि हृदये वलोम्नि वा तथा। तेषां लिङ्वानि जानीयाद्वाह्यविद्रधिलक्षणीः। आमपक्वैषणीयाच्च पक्वापववं विनिदिशेत्।
transliteration: gade bastimukhe nābhyāṃ kukṣau vaṅ kṣaṇayostathā | vakkayoryakrati plīhni hṛdaye valomni vā tathā | teṣāṃ liṅvāni jānīyādvāhyavidradhilakṣaṇīḥ | āmapakvaiṣaṇīyācca pakvāpavavaṃ vinidiśet |
commentary: They occur in the rectum, mouth of the bladder, umbilicus, both flanks, groins and kidneys, liver, spleen, heart and the kloma. Their features should be known as those of external abscesses. The (distinguishing) features between a ripe and an unripe abscess should be known according to the description of (the chapter on) 'The Unripe and Ripe Abscess'.

topic_heading: Specific Features of Abscesses According to the Site of Lesion
sanskrit_text: अधिष्ठानविशेषेण लिड्ड़ं श्रृण् विशेषतः। गदे वातनिरोधस्त्र बस्तौ कृच्छाल्पमूत्रता। नाभ्यां हिक्का तथाऽऽटोपः कुक्षौ मारुतकोपनम्। कटीपृष्ठग्रहस्तीव्रो वङ्क्षणोत्थे तु विद्रधौ। वृक्कयोः पाइर्वसड्कोचः प्लीह्नचुछ्वासावरोधनम्। सर्वाड्वप्रग्रहस्तीब्रो हदि शूलश्व दारुणः। इवासो यक्रति तृष्णा च पिपासा क्लोमजेऽधिका।
transliteration: adhiṣṭhānaviśeṣeṇa liḍḍaṃ śrṛṇ viśeṣataḥ | gade vātanirodhastra bastau kṛcchāl pamūtratā | nābhyāṃ hikkā tathā''ṭopaḥ kukṣau mārutakopanam | kaṭīpṛṣṭhagrahastīvro vaṅkṣaṇotthe tu vidradhau | vṛkkayoḥ pāirvasaḍkocaḥ plīhnacuchvāsāvarodhanam | sarvāḍvapragrahastībro hadi śūlaśva dāruṇaḥ | ivāso yakrati tṛṣṇā ca pipāsā klomaje'dhikā |
commentary: Now please listen to their special features according to the sites involved. If (the internal abscess is situated) in the rectum obstruction to flatus occurs; if in the bladder dysuria and oliguria occur; if in the umbilical region hiccough and borborygmi occur; if (the abscess is) in the flanks the vāta gets vitiated. If the abscess is in the groins severe catch in the waist and back occurs; if in the kidneys contraction of the sides and if the abscess is in spleen, obstruction to the breath occurs. If (the abscess occurs in) the heart, excessive pain and feeling of severe rigidity occurs all over the body; if in liver breathlessness and thirst occur; whereas if (the abscess is) in the kloma thirst is more in evidence.

sanskrit_text: आमो वा यदि वा पक्वो महान् वा यदि वेतरः। सर्वो मर्मोत्थितइचापि विद्रधिः कष्ट उच्यते। नाभेहपरिजाः पक्वा यान्त्यध्वंमितरे त्वधः। जीवत्यधो निःस्रतेष स्रतेष्ध्वं न जीवति। हन्नाभिबस्तिवर्ज्या ये तेष् भिन्नेष् बाह्यतः। जीवेत् कदाचित् पुरुषो नेतरेष् कदाचन।
transliteration: āmo vā yadi vā pakvo mahān vā yadi vetaraḥ | sarvo marmotthitaicāpi vidradhiḥ kaṣṭa ucyate | nābhehaparijāḥ pakvā yāntyadhvaṃmitare tvadhaḥ | jīvatyadho niḥsrateṣa srateṣdhvaṃ na jīvati | hannābhibastivarjyā ye teṣ bhinneṣ bāhyataḥ | jīvet kadācit puruṣo netareṣ kadācana |
commentary: All the abscesses arising from the vital parts are difficult to treat irrespective of their being unripe or ripe and big or small. The abscesses situated above the level of umbilicus on suppuration spread upwards, and the others situated below the umbilicus spread downwards; if they burst downwards the patient lives, whereas if they burst upwards, he does not live. The patients, except those with abscesses in the heart, umbilicus and bladder may sometimes live if the abscesses burst outwards but never otherwise.

sanskrit_text: स्त्रीणामपप्रजातानां प्रजातानां तथाऽहितैः। दाहज्वरकरो घोरो जायते रवतविद्रधिः। अपि सम्यक्प्रजातानामसंक् कायादनिःसतम्। रक्तजं विद्रर्धि कुर्यात् कुक्षौ मक्कल्लसंज्ञितम्।
transliteration: strīṇāmapaprajātānāṃ prajātānāṃ tathā'hitaiḥ | dāhajvarakaro ghoro jāyate ravatavidradhiḥ | api samyakprajātānāmasaṃk kāyādaniḥsatam | raktajaṃ vidrardhi kuryāt kukṣau makkallasaṃjñitam |
commentary: Women who have had abortions or full-term normal delivery and who indulge in unsalutary diets and habits get a dangerous type of abscess of blood origin accompanied with burning sensation and fever. Even if the delivery is normal but if the blood does not come out of the body, it causes abscess of blood origin in the flanks and is called makkalla.

sanskrit_text: सप्ताहान्नीपशान्तश्चेत्ततोऽसौ संप्रपच्यते
transliteration: saptāhānnīpaśāntaścettato'sau saṃprapacyate
commentary: If this does not subside in a week's time, it suppurates.

sanskrit_text: विशेषमय वक्ष्यामि स्पष्ट विद्रधिग्ल्मयोः। गल्मदोष समृत्थानाद्विद्रधेर्गुल्मकस्य च। कस्मान्न पच्यते ग़ल्मो विद्रधिः पाकर्मेति च। न निबन्धोऽस्ति गुल्मानां विद्रधिः सनिबन्धनः। ग ल्माकाराः स्वयं दोषा विद्रधिर्मांसशोणिते। विवरातुचरो ग्रन्थिरव्सु बुद्रु दको यथा। एवं प्रकारो गुल्मस्तु तस्मात पाक न गच्छति। मांसशोणितबाहुल्यात् पार्क गच्छति विद्रधिः। मांसशोणितहीनत्वादगल्मः पार्क न गच्छति। गल्मस्तिब्ठति दोषे स्वे विद्रधिमांसहोणिते । विद्रधिः पच्चते तस्माद्गुल्मइचापि न पच्यते।
transliteration: viśeṣamaya vakṣyāmi spaṣṭa vidradhiglmayoḥ | galmadoṣa samṛtthānādvidradhergulmakasya ca | kasmānna pacyate ga lmo vidradhiḥ pākarmeti ca | na nibandho'sti gulmānāṃ vidradhiḥ sanibandhanaḥ | ga lmākārāḥ svayaṃ doṣā vidradhirmāṃsaśoṇite | vivarātucaro granthiravsu budru dako yathā | evaṃ prakāro gulmastu tasmāt pāka na gacchati | māṃsaśoṇitabāhulyāt pārka gacchati vidradhiḥ | māṃsaśoṇitahīnatvād agalmaḥ pārka na gacchati | galmastibṭhati doṣe sve vidradhimāṃsahoṇite | vidradhiḥ paccate tasmādgulmaicāpi na pacyate |
commentary: Now I would discourse on differentiation between gulma (a gaseous swelling of the abdomen) and an abscess for clarity. As both gulma and the abscess occur because of aggravation of similar doṣas and similar etiology why is it that gulma does not suppurate whereas an abscess does so? The gulmas are without any base whereas the abscesses are with it; the vitiated doṣas themselves form into the shape of a gulma whereas the abscesses are confined to muscles and blood. A gulma is just like a knobbly swelling of water bubble moving within the (abdominal) cavity, hence it does not undergo suppuration. The abscess proceeds to suppuration because of preponderance of muscles and blood. The gulma does not proceed to suppuration due to lack of muscles and blood. The gulma is situated within its own doṣas whereas the abscess is in the muscles and blood; therefore the abscess suppurates and the gulma does not suppurate.

sanskrit_text: हस्नाभिबंस्तिजः*पवंवो वर्ज्यो ‘यइच’ त्रिदीषजः
transliteration: hasnābhibaṃstijaḥ*pavaṃvo varjyo ‘yaica’ tridīṣajaḥ
commentary: Suppurations occuring in the heart, umbilicus and urinary bladder and also those due to a combination of the three doṣas should be discarded (from treatment).

sanskrit_text: अथ मज्जपरीपाकी घोरः सम्पजायते। सोऽस्थिमांसनिरोधेन द्वारं न लभते यदा। ततः स ञ्याधिना तेन ज्वलनेनेव दह्यते। अस्थिमज्जोष्मणा तेन शीर्यते दह्यमानवत्। विकार: इाल्यभूतोऽयं क्लेइायेदातुरं चिरम्। अथास्य कर्मणा व्याधिद्वांरं लु लभते यदा। ततो मेदःप्रभं स्निग्धं हाक्लं हीतमथो गरु। भिन्नेऽस्थिन निःस्रवेत् पूयमेतदरिथगतं विद्वः। विद्वर्धि शास्त्रकुशलाः संवंदोषरुजावहम्।
transliteration: atha majjaparīpākī ghoraḥ sampajāyate | so'sthimāṃsanirodhena dvāraṃ na labhate yadā | tataḥ sa ñyādhinā tena jvalaneneva dahyate | asthimajjoṣmaṇā tena śīryate dahyamānavat | vikāra: iālyabhūto'yaṃ kleiāyedāturaṃ ciram | athāsya karmaṇā vyādhidvāṃraṃ lu labhate yadā | tato medaḥprabhaṃ snigdhaṃ hāklaṃ hītamatho garu | bhinne'sthinā niḥsravet pūyametadarithagataṃ vidvaḥ | vidvardhi śāstrakuśalāḥ saṃvaṃdoṣarujāvaham |
commentary: Now (sometimes) the bone marrow gets suppurated severely. When it (the suppuration) does not gain an exit due to obstruction of bone and muscles in this disease the patient feels burning sensation like (being burnt in) a fire. He withers as if being burnt due to the heat of the bone and bone marrow. This (sequestrum) disease like a foreign body troubles the patient for a long time. Now when this disease gets an outlet by the indicated management, a slimy, white, cold and heavy pus which is fat like is discharged. This is known as bone abscess by the experts in this science and is due to vitiation of all the doṣas and is painful.

topic_heading: Introduction: Cellulitis, Sinuses and Breast Diseases
sanskrit_text: अथातो विसर्पनाडीस्तनरोगनिदानं व्यार यास्यामः
transliteration: athāto visarpanāḍīstanaroganidānaṃ vyāra yāsyāmaḥ
commentary: Now we would expound upon 'The Diagnosis of Spreading Cellulitis, Sinuses and Breast Diseases'.

sanskrit_text: यथोवाच्च भगवान् धन्वन्तरिः
transliteration: yathovācca bhagavān dhanvantariḥ
commentary: As was described by Lord Dhanvantari.

sanskrit_text: त्वङ् मांसशोणितगताः कुपितास्तु दोषाः र्वाड्मसारिणमिहास्थितमात्मलिड्मम्। कुर्वन्ति विस्ततमन्नतमाहा शोफं तं सर्वतो विसरणाच्च विसर्पमाहः
transliteration: tvaṅ māṃsaśoṇitagatāḥ kupitāstu doṣāḥ rvāḍmasāriṇamihāsthitamātmal iḍmam | kurvanti vistatamannatamāhā śophaṃ taṃ sarvato visaraṇācca visarpamāhaḥ
commentary: The doṣas located in the skin, muscles and blood getting vitiated, spread into all parts of the body without getting localised and produce characteristic symptoms. They quickly produce widespread and unelevated inflammation. Because of its (inflammation) spreading nature all over it is called visarpa (spreading cellulitis).

sanskrit_text: वातात्मकोऽसितमुदुः परुषोऽङ्मर्द- संभेदतोदपवनज्वरलिङ्गयुवतः। ग्र्डर्यदा तु विषमैरतिदृषितत्वा- द्यवतः स एव कथितः खल् वर्जनीयः
transliteration: vātātmako'sitamuduḥ paruṣo'ṅmarda- saṃbhedatodapavanajvaraliṅgayuvataḥ | grḍaryadā tu viṣamairatidṛṣitatvā- dyavataḥ sa eva kathitaḥ khal varjanīyaḥ
commentary: The (cellulitis) of vāta origin is black and soft or rough, is accompanied with bodyache, tearing sensation, pricking sensation and with the features of vāta fever. It is said that when the doṣas get excessively vitiated blisters of varied characteristics develop and that should then be discarded (from treatment).

sanskrit_text: पित्तात्मको द्रतगतिर्ज्वरदाहपाक- स्फोटप्रभेदबहलः क्षतजप्रकाहाः । दोषप्रवुद्धिहतमांससिरो यदा स्यात् स्रोतोजकर्दमनिभो न तदा स सिध्येत्
transliteration: pittātmako dratagatirjvaradāhapāka- sphoṭaprabhedabahalaḥ kṣatajaprakāhāḥ | doṣapravuddhihata māṃsasiro yadā syāt srotojakardamanibho na tadā sa sidhyet
commentary: (Cellulitis) of pitta origin progresses rapidly, has fever, burning sensation, suppuration, tearing sensation, numerous blisters and is reddish like blood. When the muscles and vessels get destroyed by the aggravated doṣa and the colour becomes muddy, like collyrium, that cellulitis becomes incurable.

topic_heading: Cellulitis due to Combined Doṣas and Kapha
sanskrit_text: हलेटमात्मकः सरति मन्दमशीघ्रपाकः स्निग्धः सितहवयथुरल्परुगुग्रकण्डुः। सर्वात्मकस्त्रिविधवर्णरुजोऽवगाढः पक्वो न सिध्यति च मांससिराप्रशातात्
transliteration: haleṭamātmakaḥ sarati mandamaśīghrapākaḥ snigdhaḥ sitahavayathuralparugugrakaṇḍuḥ | sarvātmakastrividhavarṇarujo'vagāḍhaḥ pakvo na sidhyati ca māṃsasirāpraśātāt
commentary: (Cellulitis) of kapha origin spreads slowly, suppurates late, is smooth and whitish, is associated with oedema, mild pain and severe itching. Cellulitis due to vitiation of all (the three) doṣas together has the colour and characteristic pains of the three together, is based internally and is incurable upon suppuration; it is also incurable when the muscles and vessels have been destroyed.

sanskrit_text: सद्यः क्षतव्रणमुपेत्य नरस्य पित्तं रवतं 'च दोषबहलस्य' करोति शोफम् । श्यावं सलोहितमतिज्वरवाहपाकं स्फोटैः कुलत्थसद्दीरसितैइच कीर्णम
transliteration: sadyaḥ kṣatavraṇamupetya narasya pittaṃ ravataṃ 'ca doṣabahal asya' karoti śopham | śyāvaṃ salohitamatijvaravāhapākaṃ sphoṭaiḥ kulatthasaddīrasitaiica kīrṇama
commentary: The pitta and rakta afflicting a traumatic ulcer of recent origin in a person having excess of the (vitiated) doṣas produce inflammation. This is black, reddish, is associated with high fever, burning sensation, suppuration, and has blisters all over which are blackish like the lentils of kulattha.

sanskrit_text: सिध्यन्ति वातकफपित्तकृता विसर्पाः सवत्मकः क्षतकृतश्व न सिद्धिमेति। पैत्तानिलावपि च दर्शशतपूर्वलिड्मौ सर्वे च मर्मस भवन्ति हि कृच्छुसाध्याः
transliteration: sidhyanti vātakaphapittakṛtā visarpāḥ savatmakaḥ kṣatakṛtaśva na siddhim eti | paittānilāvapi ca darśaśatapūrvaliḍmau sarve ca marmasa bhavanti hi kṛcchusādhyāḥ
commentary: Cellulitis due to vāta, kapha, or pitta is curable, whereas those due to all of them together and the traumatic ones are incurable. The (cellulitis) due to pitta and also that due to vāta with the features mentioned before and all those which occur over the vital parts are curable with difficulty.

sanskrit_text: शोफं न पक्वमिति पक्वमुपेक्षते यो यो वा वर्ण प्रचुरप्तयमसाधुवृत्तः। अम्यन्तरं प्रविशति प्रविदार्य तस्य स्थानानि पूर्वविहितानि ततः स पूर्यः। तस्यातिमात्रगमनाद्गतिरित्यतंतच नाडीव यद्वहति तेन मता तु नाडी। दोषैस्त्रिभिर्भवति सा पृथगेकहाइच संमूच्छतैरपि च शल्यनिमित्ततोऽन्या
transliteration: śophaṃ na pakvamiti pakvamupekṣate yo yo vā varṇa pracu raptayamasādhuvṛttaḥ | amyantaraṃ praviśati pravidārya tasya sthānāni pūrvavihitāni tataḥ sa pūryaḥ | tasyātimātragamanādgatirityataṃtaca nāḍīva yadvahati tena matā tu nāḍī | doṣaistribhirbhavati sā pṛthagekahāica saṃmūcchatairapi ca śalyanimittato'nyā
commentary: The irresponsible person who mistakes a suppurated inflammation for an unripe one (deliberately), ignores a suppurated one, or when he allows a lot of pus to accumulate in an ulcer, then that pus having entered into his aforesaid tissues, penetrates inside. Because of its copious flow, it is known as gati (track) and as it flows like a drain, it is opined as nāḍī (sinus). That is caused by a combined action of the three doṣas or due to each one of them seperately, and also due to two together only. The others are due to foreign bodies.

topic_heading: Sinuses due to Vāta and Pitta
sanskrit_text: तत्रानिलात परुषस्क्ममली सहाला फेनानविद्धमधिकं स्त्रवति क्षपायाम्। तृट्तापतोदसदनज्वरभेदहेत्रः पीतं स्रवत्यधिकमष्णमहःसु पित्तात्
transliteration: tatrānilāta paruṣaskmamalī sahālā phenānaviddhamadhikaṃ sravati kṣapāyām | tṛṭtāpatodasadanajvarabhedahetraḥ pītaṃ sravatyadhikamaṣṇamahaḥsu pittāt
commentary: The (sinuses) due to vāta are rough, have a narrow opening and are associated with pain and excessive foam mixed discharge which occurs more at night. The (sinuses) due to pitta are associated with thirst, burning, pricking sensation, lethargy, fever, and tearing sensation; their discharge is yellow, excessive, hot and occurs during the day.

topic_heading: Sinuses due to Kapha and Combined Doṣas
sanskrit_text: ज्ञेया कफाद्वह्वनार्जुनपिच्छिलास्रा रात्रिस्रतिः स्तिमितरुक्कठिना संकण्डू: । दोषद्वयाभिहितलक्षणदर्शनेन तिस्रो गतीर्व्यतिकरप्रभवास्तु विद्यात्
transliteration: jñeyā kaphādvahvanārjunapicchilāsrā rātrisratiḥ stimitarukkaṭhinā saṃkaṇḍū: | doṣadvayābhihitalakṣaṇadarśanena tisro gatīrvyatikaraprabhavāstu vidyāt
commentary: Sinuses due to kapha should be known by a very thick, whitish and slimy discharge occuring at nights; these are associated with mild pain and severe itching. Three types of sinuses due to a combination of two (doṣas) should be known by the characteristic features of two doṣas concerned.

topic_heading: Sinuses due to Combination of the three Vitiated Doṣas
sanskrit_text: दाहज्वरइवसनमूर्च्छनवक्त्रहोषा यस्यां भवन्त्यभिहितानि च लक्षणानि। तामादिशेत् पवनपित्तकफप्रकोपा- द्धोरामसुक्षयकरीमिव कालरात्रिम्
transliteration: dāhajvaraivasana mūrcchanavaktrahoṣā yasyāṃ bhavantyabhihitāni ca lakṣaṇāni | tāmādiśet pavanapittakaphaprakopā- ddhorāmasukṣayakarīmiva kālarātrim |
commentary: (The patient) in whom the features of burning, fever, breathlessness, fainting and dryness of the mouth occur should be known to be suffering from vitiation of vāta, pitta and kapha together; it is fatal like the night of death itself.

sanskrit_text: नष्टं कथंचिदनुमार्गमुदीरितेषु स्थानेष् शल्यमंविरेण गांत करोति। सा फेनिलं मथितमच्छमसंग्विमिश्र- मष्णं स्रवेत सहसा सरुजा 'व नित्यम्
transliteration: naṣṭaṃ kathaṃcidanumārgamudīriteṣu sthāneṣ śalyamaṃvireṇa gāṃta karoti | sā phenilaṃ mathitamacchamasaṃgvimiśra- maṣṇaṃ sraveta sahasā sarujā 'va nityam
commentary: In case, the foreign body gets lost at the sites mentioned earlier it quickly produces a sinus locally. Its discharge comes out suddenly along with foam as if churned, is serosanguinous and hot, and is associated with a continuous pain.

topic_heading: Aetiology and Types of Breast Diseases
sanskrit_text: यावत्यो गतयो यैइच कारणैः संभवन्ति हि। तावन्तः स्तनरोगाः स्यः स्त्रीणां तैरेव हेतुभिः। धमन्यः संवृतद्वारा कन्यानां स्तनसंश्रिताः। दोषाविसरणात्तासां न भवन्ति स्तनामयाः। तासामेव प्रजातानां गर्भिणीनां च ताः प्रनः। स्वभावादेव विवृता जायन्ते संभवन्त्यतः
transliteration: yāvatyo gatayo yaica kāraṇaiḥ saṃbhavanti hi | tāvantaḥ stanarogāḥ syaḥ strīṇāṃ taireva hetubhiḥ | dhamanyaḥ saṃvṛtadvārā kanyānāṃ stanasaṃśritāḥ | doṣāvisaraṇāttāsāṃ na bhavanti stanāmayāḥ | tāsāmeva prajātānāṃ garbhiṇīnāṃ ca tāḥ pranaḥ | svabhāvādeva vivṛtā jāyante saṃbhavantyataḥ
commentary: Whatever are the types and the causes of gati (track, sinuses), the same are the types and causes of breast diseases in women. The exits (openings) of the ducts located in the breasts of girls are closed; thus the doṣas cannot spread and hence breast diseases do not occur in them. The (breast diseases) are possible only in those women who have delivered and in the pregnant, as the same (ducts) open out physiologically (in them).

sanskrit_text: रसप्रसादो मधुरः पक्वाहारनिमित्तजः । कृत्सनदेहात् स्तनौ प्राप्तः स्तन्यमित्यभिधीयते। विशस्तेष्वपि गात्रेष्ठ यथा शक्रं न दृहयते। सर्वदेहाश्रितत्वाच्च शुक्रलक्षणमुच्यतः। तदेव चेष्टय वतेर्दर्शनात् स्मरणादपि। शब्दसंश्रवणात् स्पर्शात् संहर्षाच्च प्रवर्तते। सप्रसन्नं मनस्तत्र हर्षणे हेतुरुच्यते। आहाररसयोनित्वादेवं स्तन्यमपि स्त्रियाः। तदेवापत्यसंस्पर्शाद्दर्शनात् स्मरणादपि। प्रहणाच्च शरीरस्य शक्रवत संप्रवर्तते। स्नेहो निरन्तरस्तत्र प्रस्रवे हेतुरुच्यते
