transliteration: rasaprasādo madhuraḥ pakvāhāranimittajaḥ | kṛtsanadehāt stanau prāptaḥ stanyamityabhidhīyate | viśasteṣvapi gātreṣṭha yathā śakraṃ na dṛhayate | sarvadehāśritatvācca śukralakṣaṇamucyataḥ | tadeva ceṣṭaya vaterdarśanāt smaraṇādapi | śabdasaṃśravaṇāt sparśāt saṃharṣācca pravartate | saprasannaṃ manastatra harṣaṇe heturucyate | āhārarasayonitvādevaṃ stanyamapi striyāḥ | tadevāpatyasaṃsparśāddarśanāt smaraṇādapi | prahaṇācca śarīrasya śakravata saṃpravartate | sneho nirantarastatra prasrave heturucyate
commentary: The sweet part of the essence of the well digested food getting into the breast from all over the body is called milk. As śukra (semen) cannot be visualized even when all parts of body are dissected, (similarly) because of its being spread, all over the body (milk) is known to have the characteristics similar to śukra. The same (śukra) is induced by seeing, remembering, hearing the voice of, touching and necking with the desired woman. There, the seminal emission is considered to be caused by fully satisfied mind. Milk is produced in women similar to that of śukra (in men), originating from the food extracts and induced due to touching, seeing, remembering or taking the child into laps. Here constant affection has been mentioned to be the cause of (milk) discharge.

topic_heading: Features of Milk Produced due to Vitiated Doṣas
sanskrit_text: तत् कषायं भवेद्वातात् क्षिप्तं च प्लवतेऽम्भसि। पित्तादम्लं सकटकं राज्योऽम्भस्नि च पीतिक्काः। कफाद्धनं पिच्छिलं च जले चाप्यवसीदति। सर्वेदृष्टैः सर्वलिड्डमभिघाताच्च दुष्यति
transliteration: tat kaṣāyaṃ bhavedvātāt kṣiptaṃ ca plavate'mbhasi | pittādamlaṃ sakaṭakaṃ rājyo'mbhasni ca pītikkāḥ | kaphāddhanaṃ picchilaṃ ca jale cāpyavasīdati | sarvedṛṣṭaiḥ sarvaliḍḍamabhighātācca duṣyati
commentary: When vitiated by vāta, it (the milk) becomes astringent and floats when thrown in water; when vitiated by pitta, it becomes acidic and bitter and yellowish lines are produced (when thrown) in water; when vitiated by kapha, it becomes thick and slimy and sinks in water; and when vitiated by all the doṣas or by trauma, features of all the doṣas are produced.

sanskrit_text: यत् क्षीरमुदके क्षिप्तमेकीभवति पाण्डुरम्। मधरं चाविवर्णं च प्रसन्नं तद्विनिर्दिशेत्
transliteration: yat kṣīramudake kṣiptamekībhavati pāṇḍuram | madharaṃ cāvivarṇaṃ ca prasannaṃ taddinirdiśet
commentary: The milk which when thrown in water becomes one with it, which is white, sweet, and without any discolouration is to be regarded as normal.

topic_heading: Pathogenesis and Clinical Features of Breast Abscess
sanskrit_text: सक्षीरौ वाऽप्यदुग्धौ वा प्राप्य दोषः स्तनौ स्त्रियाः। रक्तं मांसं च सन्दूष्य स्तनरोगाय कल्पते। एञ्चानामपि तेषां तु हित्वा शोणितविद्रधिम्। लक्षणानि समानानि बाह्यविद्रधिलक्षणैः
transliteration: sakṣīrau vā'pyadugdhau vā prāpya doṣaḥ stanau striyāḥ | raktaṃ māṃsaṃ ca sandūṣya stanarogāya kalpate | eñcānāmapi teṣāṃ tu hitvā śoṇitavidradhim | lakṣaṇāni samānāni bāhyavidradhilakṣaṇaiḥ
commentary: The doṣas having reached the breasts of women, whether lactating or non-lactating, and then having vitiated the blood and muscles produce diseases of breast. Except for the śoṇita abscess, the clinical features of all these five (breast diseases) are like the manifestations of external abscesses.

topic_heading: Introduction: Glandular Swellings, Tumours and Goitres
sanskrit_text: अथातो ग्रन्थपच्यर्बुदगलगण्डानां निदानं व्याख्यास्यामः
transliteration: athāto granthapacyarbudagalagaṇḍānāṃ nidānaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ
commentary: Now we would expound upon 'The Diagnosis of Glandular Swellings, Cervical Lymphadenopathy, Tumours and Goitres'.

sanskrit_text: यथोवाच भेगवान् धन्वन्तरिः
transliteration: yathovāca bhegavān dhanvantariḥ
commentary: As was described by Lord Dhanvantari.

topic_heading: Pathogenesis of Granthi (Glandular Swelling, Cyst etc.)
sanskrit_text: वातादयो मांसमसृक् च दुष्टाः संदूष्य मेदइच कफानुविद्धम् । वृत्तोन्नतं विग्रथितं तु शोफं कुर्वन्त्यतो ग्रन्थिरिति प्रदिष्टः
transliteration: vātādayo māṃsamask ca duṣṭāḥ saṃdūṣya medaica kaphānuviddham | vṛttonnataṃ vigrathitaṃ tu śophaṃ kurvantyato granthiriti pradiṣṭaḥ
commentary: When the deranged vāta etc. vitiate the māṁsa, śoṇita and meda mixed up with kapha they produce circular, raised and knotted inflammatory swellings called granthi.

sanskrit_text: मं आयम्यते व्यथ्यत एति तोदं प्रत्यस्यते कृत्यत एति भेदम्। कृब्णोऽमुदुर्बस्तिरिवाततइच भिन्नः स्रवेच्चानिलजोऽस्रमच्छम्
transliteration: maṃ āyamyate vyathyate ati todaṃ pratyasyate kṛtyate ati bhedam | kṛbṇo'mudurbastirivātataica bhinnaḥ sraveccānilajo'sramaccham |
commentary: The granthi of vāṭa origin produces a feeling of stretching, pain, pricking and (falling) as if being thrown and also cutting and tearing pains. It is black and hard and is like a bladder distended with air and when burst, discharges sero-sanguinous fluid.

sanskrit_text: ध्य्यति चृष्यते च पापच्यते प्रज्वलतीव चापि। दन्दह यत रक्तः सपीतोप्यथवाऽपि पित्ताद्भन्नः स्रवेदुष्णमतीव चास्रम्
transliteration: dhyyati cṛṣyate ca pāpacyate prajvalatīva cāpi | dandaha yata raktaḥ sapītopyathavā'pi pittādbhannaḥ sraveduṣṇamatīva cāsram |
commentary: And the granthi due to pitta produces a sensation of severe burning, fuming, sucking, throbbing and as if being burnt to ashes. It is red and/or yellow and when burst, discharges hot and excessive amount of blood.

sanskrit_text: शीतोऽविवर्णोऽल्परुजोऽतिकण्डूः पाषाणवत् संहननौपपन्नः । चिराभिवृद्धिश्च कफप्रकोपाद्धिन्नः स्रवेच्छुक्लघनं च पूयम्
transliteration: śīto'vivarṇo'lparujo'tikaṇḍūḥ pāṣāṇavat saṃhananaupapannaḥ | cirābhivṛddhiśca kaphaprakopāddhinnaḥ sravecchuklaghanaṃ ca pūyam |
commentary: The (granthi) due to vitiation of kapha produces a cold swelling without any discolouration associated with mild pain and excessive itching having the consistency of a stone. It increases slowly and when burst, white and thick pus is discharged.

sanskrit_text: शरीरवुद्धिक्षयवद्धिहानिः स्निग्धो महानल्परुजोतिकण्ड्:। मेद:क्रतो गच्छति चात्र भिन्ने पिण्याकर्सापः प्रतिमं तु मेदः
transliteration: śarīravuddhikṣayavaddhihāniḥ snigdho mahānalparujotikaṇḍ: | meda:krato gacchati cātra bhinne piṇyākarsāpaḥ pratimaṃ tu medaḥ
commentary: The (granthi) due to medas increases or decreases according to the increase or decrease of (fat) in the body; it is smooth, big in size and is associated with mild pain and excessive itching; and when burst it discharges fat which is similar to oil-cake and ghee.

sanskrit_text: व्यायामजातरबलस्य तैस्तैराक्षिप्य वार्याह सिराप्रतानम्। संपीड्य सड्डोच्य विशोष्य चापि ग्रन्थिं करोत्युन्नतमाशु वृत्तम्। ग्रन्थिः सिराजः स तु कृच्छसाध्यो भवेद्यदि स्यात सरुजहचलहच। अरुक् स एवाप्यचलो महांशच मर्मोत्थितश्चापि विवर्जनीयः
transliteration: vyāyāmajātarabalasya taistairākṣipya vāryāha sirāpratānam | saṃpīḍya saḍḍocya viśoṣya cāpi granthiṃ karotyunnatamāśu vṛttam | granthiḥ sirājaḥ sa tu kṛcchasādhyo bhavedyadi syāt sarujahacalahaca | aruk sa evāpyacalo mahāṃśaca marmotthitaścāpi vivarjanīyaḥ
commentary: A weak person who undertakes excessive exercise gets his network of veins affected due to vāyu which in turn compresses, squeezes and dries it up and produces granthi quickly which is raised and circular. The granthi, originating in the veins becomes curable with difficulty, if it is associated with pain and is mobile. If it is painless, and also fixed, big in size and situated over the vital spots, it should be discarded (from treatment).

sanskrit_text: हन्वस्थिकक्षाक्षकबाहसन्धिमन्यागलेषपचितं तु मेदः। ग्रन्थिं स्थिरं व्तमथायतं वा स्निग्धं कफइचाल्परुजं करोति। तं ग्रन्थिभिस्त्वामलकास्थिमात्रेर्मत्स्याण्डजालप्रतिर्मस्तथाऽन्यैः। अनन्यवर्णैहपचीयमानं चयप्रकर्षादपचों वदन्ति। कण्ड्रयुतास्तेऽल्परुजः प्रभिन्नाः स्रवन्ति नइयन्ति भवन्ति चान्ये। मेदः कफाभ्यां खलु रोग एष सुदुस्तरो वर्षगणानुबन्धी
transliteration: hanvasthikakṣākṣakabāhasandhimanyāgaleṣapacitaṃ tu medaḥ | granthiṃ sthiraṃ vtamathāyataṃ vā snigdhaṃ kaphaicālparujaṃ karoti | taṃ granthibhistvāmalakāsthimātrermatsyāṇḍajālapratirmastathā'nyaiḥ | ananyavarṇaihapacīyamānaṃ cayaprakarṣād apacom̐ vadanti | kaṇḍrayutāste'lparujaḥ prabhinnāḥ sravanti naiyanti bhavanti cānye | medaḥ kaphaṃ bhyāṃ khalu roga eṣa sudustaro varṣagaṇānubandhī
commentary: The medas and kapha collected in the regions of mandible, axilla, clavicle, shoulder joint, posterior and anterior cervical regions produce granthis which are fixed, extensive, circular in shape, smooth and associated with mild pain. Some of these swellings are of the size of kernel of āmalaka while others are like the spawn of fish in shape. They are of the same colour (as skin) and are progressively increasing and because of the continuous growth they are called apaci. They are associated with itching and mild pain ; when burst they discharge, and disappear while others appear. This disease caused by medas and kapha is difficult to treat and lasts for several years.

sanskrit_text: गात्रप्रदेशो क्वविदेव दोषाः संर्मूच्छता मांसमभिप्रदूष्य। वत्तं स्थिरं मन्दरुजं महान्तमनल्पमूलं प्विरवृद्ध्यपाकम्। कुर्वन्ति मांसोप'वयं तु शोफं तमर्बुदं शास्रविदो वदन्ति। वातेन पित्तेन कफेन चापि रक्तेन मांसेन व मेदसा च। तज्जायते तस्य 'व लक्षणानि ग्रन्थेः समानानि सदा भवन्ति।
transliteration: gātrapradeśo kvavideva doṣāḥ saṃrmūcchatā māṃsamabhipraduṣya | vattaṃ sthiraṃ mandarujaṃ mahāntamanalpamūlaṃ pviravṛddhyapākam | kurvanti māṃsopa'vayaṃ tu śophaṃ tamarbudaṃ śāstravido vadanti | vātena pittena kaphena cāpi raktena māṃsena va medasā ca | tajjāyate tasya 'va lakṣaṇāni granthēḥ samānāni sadā bhavanti |
commentary: The doṣas having got vitiated in any part of the body and afflicting the māṁsa produce swelling in the latter. This (lesion) is circular, fixed, slightly painful, big in size, broad based, slowly growing and it does not suppurate; the same is called arbuda by the experts of this science. This is produced by (vitiated) vāṭa, pitta and kapha and by rakta and māṁsa and also by medas. Its clinical features are always like that of granthi.

sanskrit_text: दोषः प्रद्रष्टो रुधिरं सिरास्तु संपीडच्च सड्कोच्य गतस्त्वपाकम्। सास्रावमुन्नह्यति मांसपिण्डं मांसा ड्रू रेराचितमाशुवृद्धिम्। स्रवत्यजस्रं रुधिरं प्रदुष्टमसाध्यमेतद्रधिरात्मकं स्यात्। सोऽर्बुदपीडितस्त्र। रक्तक्षयोपद्रवपीडितत्वात् पाण्डर्भवेत्
transliteration: doṣaḥ pradraṣṭo rudhiraṃ sirāstu saṃpīḍacca saḍkocyagatastvapākam | sāsrāvamunnahyati māṃsapiṇḍaṃ māṃsā ḍrū rerācitamāśuvṛddhim | sravatyajasraṃ rudhiraṃ praduṣṭamasādhyametadradhirātmakaṃ syāt | so'rbudapīḍitastra | raktakṣayopadravapīḍitatvāt pāṇḍarbhavet |
commentary: The vitiated doṣas compressing and contracting the śoṇita and vessels without undergoing suppuration and alongwith the discharge make the muscular lumps prominent. This is studded with fleshy buds and increases rapidly. This continuously discharges vitiated blood and is incurable and is known as raktārbuda. Because of the complication of haemorrhage the patient with this tumour becomes anaemic.

sanskrit_text: मुष्टिप्रहारादिभिरदितेऽङ्मे मांसं प्रदुष्टं प्रकरोति शोफम्। अवेदनं स्निग्धमनन्यवर्णमपाकमइमोपममप्र वाल्यम्। प्रदुष्टमांसस्य नरस्य बाढमेत द्रवेन्मांसपरायणस्य। मांसार्बुदं त्वेतदसाध्यमुक्तं साध्येष्वपीमानि विवर्जयेत्त। संप्रस्रतं मर्मणि यच्च जातं स्रोतःसु वा यच्च भवेदचाल्यम्
transliteration: muṣṭiprahārādibhiradite'ṅme māṃsaṃ praduṣṭaṃ prakaroti śopham | avedanaṃ snigdhamananyavarṇamapākamaimopamamapra vālyam | praduṣṭamāṃsasya narasya bāḍhameta dravenmāṃsaparāyaṇasya | māṃsārbudaṃ tvetadasādhyamuktaṃ sādhyeṣvapīmāni vivarjayetta | saṃprasrataṃ marmaṇi yacca jātaṃ srotaḥsu vā yacca bhavedacālyam |
commentary: Due to fist blows etc. the muscles of injured parts get vitiated and swollen. This is painless and smooth, is of the same colour (as skin), is non-suppurating, is like a stone and is fixed. This vitiated muscle increases much more in the non-vegetarian. This is maṁsārbuda and is said to be incurable. Even out of those which are curable, those which discharge, those situated over the vital parts or over the srotasas and those which become fixed, should be discarded from treatment.

sanskrit_text: यज्जायतेऽन्यत् खल्ट पूर्वजाते ज्ञेयं तदध्यर्बदमर्बदज्ञः । यद्वन्द्वजातं युगपत ऋमाद्वा द्विरर्बुदं तच्च भवेदसाध्यम
transliteration: yajjāyate'nyat khalṭa pūrvajāte jñeyaṃ tadadhyarbadamarbadajñaḥ | yadvandvajātaṃ yugapata ṛmādvā dvirarbudaṃ tacca bhavedasādhyama
commentary: When another tumour grows over the pre-existing one, that is known as adhyarbuda by the oncologist. When two tumours grow simultaneously or one after the other, that is called dvirarbuda, and both these are incurable.

sanskrit_text: न पाकमायान्ति कफाधिकत्वान्मेदोबहत्वाच्च विशेषतस्तु। दोषस्थिरत्वाद ग्रथनाच्च तेषां सर्वार्बदान्येव निसर्गतस्तु
transliteration: na pākamāyānti kaphādhikatvānmedobahatvācca viśeṣatastu | doṣasthiratvāda grathanācca teṣāṃ sarvārbadānyeva nisargatastu
commentary: All tumours by nature do not undergo suppuration because of preponderance of kapha in them and specially because of the preponderance of medas and also because of the immobilization and knotting of the doṣas in them.

sanskrit_text: वातः कफइचैव गले प्रवृद्धौ मन्ये तु संसृत्य तथैव मेदः। कुर्वेन्ति गण्डं ऋमशः स्वलिङ्वेः समन्वितं तं गलगण्डमाहः
transliteration: vātaḥ kaphaicaiva gale pravṛddhau manye tu saṃsṛtya tathaiva medaḥ | kurventi gaṇḍaṃ ṛmaśaḥ svaliṅveḥ samanvitaṃ taṃ galagaṇḍamāhaḥ |
commentary: Vāta and kapha having aggravated in the neck and having accumulated in manyā and alongwith medas produce glandular enlargements with their characteristic symptoms. It is known as goitre (galagaṇḍa).

sanskrit_text: तोदान्वितः कृष्णसिरावनद्धः कृष्णोऽरुणो वा पवनात्मकस्तु। काला द्ववेदतिस्निग्धतरोऽरुजहच। मेदान्वितइचोपचितइच पाहष्ययुक्तहिचरवद्धपाको यदृच्छया पाकमियात् कदाचित् । जन्तोर्भवेतथा तालुगलप्रशोषः। वेरस्यमास्यस्य च तस्य
transliteration: todānvitaḥ kṛṣṇasirāvanaddhaḥ kṛṣṇo'ruṇo vā pavanātmakastu | kālā dvavedatisnig dhataro'rujahaca | medānvitaicopacitaica pāhaṣyayuktahicaravaddhapāko yadṛcchayā pākamiyāt kadācit | jantorbhavetathā tālugalapraśoṣaḥ | verasyamāsyasya ca tasya
commentary: The goitre originating due to (vitiated) vāta is black or red, is associated with pricking pain and is full of blackish veins. And when medas combines with it or collects there in due course of time, the same (goitre) becomes very smooth and painless. It is hard, increases gradually in size and does not suppurate; however, it rarely suppurates for unknown reasons. Loss of taste in the mouth and dryness of palate and throat occur in that person.

sanskrit_text: स्थिर: सवर्णोऽल्परुग्रकण्डू: शीता महांशचापि कफात्मकस्तु । चिराभिर्वृद्धि कुरुते चिराच्च प्रपच्यते मन्दरजः कदाचित्। माधुर्यमास्यस्य च तस्य जन्तोर्भवेत्तथा ताल्गलप्रलेपः।
transliteration: sthira: savarṇo'lparugrakaṇḍū: śītā mahāṃśacāpi kaphātmakastu | cirābhirvṛddhi kurute cirācca prapacyate mandarajaḥ kadācit | mādhuryamāsyasya ca tasya jantorbhavettathā tālgalapralepaḥ |
commentary: The goitre due to (vitiated) kapha is fixed, is of the same colour as skin, has mild pain and excessive itching. It is cold and big in size, increases slowly and after a long time, rarely suppurates and has mild pain. Taste of the mouth becomes sweet in that person and the palate and throat feel as if pasted.

sanskrit_text: स्निग्घो मुदुः पाण्डुरनिष्टगन्धो मेदःकृतो नीरंगथातिकण्डू:। प्रलम्बतेऽलाबवदल्पमलो देहानुरूपक्षयवद्धियुक्तः। स्निग्धास्यता तस्य भवेच्च जन्तोर्गलेऽनुशब्दं कुरुते च नित्यम्
transliteration: sniggho muduḥ pāṇḍuraniṣṭagandho medaḥkṛto nīraṃgathātikaṇḍū: | pralambate'lāvavadalpamalo dehānurūpakṣayavaddhiyuktaḥ | snigdhāsyatā tasya bhavecca jantorgale'nuśabdaṃ kurute ca nityam
commentary: The goitre due to meda is smooth, soft, pale, has an offensive odour, is painless and has excessive itching. It hangs down like a gourd, with a narrow base, and its increase or decrease in size occurs corresponding to that of the body (in general). Stickiness of the mouth occurs in that person and a continuous sound is produced from his throat.

sanskrit_text: क्टच्छाच्छ्वसन्तं मृदुसर्वगात्रं संवत्सरातीतमरोचकार्तम्। क्षीणं व वैद्यो गलगण्डिनं तु भिन्नस्वरं चेव विवर्जयेत्तु
transliteration: kṭacchācchvasantaṃ mṛdusarvagātraṃ saṃvatsarātītamarocakārtam | kṣīṇaṃ va vaidyo galagaṇḍinaṃ tu bhinnasvaraṃ ceva vivarjayettu |
commentary: The patient of goitre who breathes with difficulty, whose whole body has become flaccid, whose disease has lasted more than a year, who has anorexia, is emaciated and has hoarseness of voice should be discarded from treatment by the clinician.

sanskrit_text: निबद्धः श्वयथर्यस्य मष्कवल्लम्बते गले। महान् वा यदि वा ह्रस्वो गलगण्डं तमादिशोत्
transliteration: nibaddhaḥ śvayatharyasya maṣkavallambate gale | mahān vā yadi vā hrasvo galagaṇḍaṃ tamādiśot |
commentary: Goitre has been defined as the swelling, big or small, which hangs like scrotum in the neck.

topic_heading: Introduction: Scrotal Swellings, Venereal Diseases and Elephantiasis
sanskrit_text: अथातो वुद्धच्युपदंशश्लीपदानां निदानं व्याख्यास्यामः
transliteration: athāto vuddhacyupadaṃśaślīpadānāṃ nidānaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ
commentary: Now we would expound upon 'The Diagnosis of Scrotal Swellings, Venereal Diseases and Elephantiasis'.

sanskrit_text: यथोवाच भगवान् धन्वन्तरिः
transliteration: yathovāca bhagavān dhanvantariḥ
commentary: As was described by Lord Dhanvantari.

sanskrit_text: वातपित्तइलेष्मशोणितमेदोम्त्रान्त्रतिंमित्ताः सप्तवृद्धयो भवन्ति । तासां मृत्रान्त्रनिमित्ते वुद्धी वातसमृत्थे, कैवलमृत्पत्तिहेत्रन्यतमः। अधः प्रक्रपितोऽन्यतमो हि दोषः फलकोशवाहिनीरभिप्रपद्य धमनीः फलकोषयोर्व द्धि जनयति, तां वद्धिमित्याचक्षते
transliteration: vātapittaileṣmaśoṇitamedomtrāntratimittāḥ saptavṛddhayō bhavanti | tāsāṃ mṛtrāntranimitte vuddhī vātasamṛtthe, kaivalamṛtpattihetranyatamaḥ | adhaḥ prakrapito'nyatamo hi doṣaḥ phalakōśavāhinīrabhiprapadya dhamanīḥ phalakōṣayorva d dhi janayati, tāṃ vaddhimityācakṣate
commentary: The seven types of scrotal swellings (vṛddhi) are due to vāta, pitta, kapha, śoṇita, meda, mūtra and āntra. Out of them, the scrotal swellings due to mūtra (urine) and āntra (intestines) are also associated with increased vāta, the only difference being in their immediate aetiological factors. Any one of the doṣas having got vitiated in the lower portion, enters the channels of scrotum and produces its swelling: the same is called vṛddhi.

sanskrit_text: पूर्वरूपाणि—बस्तिकटीमष्कमेढे प् वेदना भविष्यतीनां तासी मारुतनिग्रहः फलकोशशोफइचेति
transliteration: pūrvarūpāṇi—bastikaṭīmaṣkameḍhe p vedanā bhaviṣyatīnāṃ tāsī mārut anigrahaḥ phalakōśaśōphaiceti
commentary: Their prodromal features would be: pain in the bladder, waist, testes and penis, obstruction to passage of flatus and swelling of scrotum.

sanskrit_text: परुष्पामनिमित्तानिलरुज्ञां बस्त्रिमिवाततां तत्रानिलपरिपूर्णां ज्वरदाह्वोष्मवतीं च्चाशुस- वातवद्विमाचक्षते ; पववोदुम्बरसङ्काशां मुत्थानपाकां पित्तवृद्धि; कठिनामल्पवेदनां शीतां कण्डमतीं इलेष्मवृद्धि'; मृदुर्सैनग्धां कण्ड्मती- पितवृद्धिलिङ्वां रक्तवृद्धि, कृष्णस्फोटावतां मचर्चंधारणहीस्रस्य सालफाक्कपद्मावां मल्पवेदनां मूचबुद्धि भेवति, सा गन्छतोऽम्पूर्णा दृतिरिव क्षुथ्यति मूचकुरद्धवेदनां व्षफयो: स्वयंथुं कोस्पोरेचायात्रपति, तां मूत्रवृद्धि विद्वात्। भारहरण- प्रकु, पिलेडच व स्ट्राहिप्पू क्षाट्रमत नाविभिरायास विज्ञेबेर्वाच् रभिप्पू का स्थलान्त्रस्येतरस्य चैक्रदेशं विग्णमाबायाधो गरवा वङक्षणसाधिमुपरय स्थित्वाऽप्रतिक्रियमाणे च कालान्तरेण फलकोशं प्रविशय ग्रन्थि रूपेण ब्रस्तिरिवाततः प्रदीर्घः स शोफो मंडक्शोफ़मापादयति, आध्यात्रो संशब्दमकपीडितहचोर्ध्वस्प्रेति, विस्कृतहस पुनराध्मायत, भवाल, लामन्त्रत्रद्विमसाध्यामित्याचक्षते
transliteration: paruṣpāmanimittānilarujñāṃ bastrimivātatāṃ tatrānilaparipūrṇāṃ jvaradāhvoṣmavatīṃ ccāśu- savātavadvimācakṣate ; pavavodumbarasaṅkāśāṃ mutthānapākāṃ pittavṛddhi; kaṭhināmalpavedanāṃ śītāṃ kaṇḍamatīṃ ileṣmavṛddhi'; mṛdu rsainagdhāṃ kaṇḍmatī- pitavṛddhiliṅvāṃ raktavṛddhi, kṛṣṇasphoṭāvatāṃ macarcaṃdhāraṇahīsrasya sālaphākkapadmāvāṃ malpavedanāṃ mūcabuddhi bhevati, sā ganchato'mpūrṇā dṛtiriva kṣuthyati mūcakuraddhavedanāṃ vṣaphayo: svayaṃthuṃ kosporecāyā trapati, tāṃ mūtravṛddhi vidvāt | bhāraharaṇa- praku, pileḍaca va strāhippū kṣāṭramata nāvibhirāyāsa vijñebervāc rabhippū ka sthālāntrasyetaryasya caikradeśaṃ vighṇamābāyādho garavā vaṅkṣaṇasādhimuparaya sthitvā'pratikriyamāṇe ca kālāntareṇa phalakōśaṃ praviśaya granthi rūpeṇa brastirivātataḥ pradīrghaḥ sa śopho maṃḍakśopha māpādayati, ādhyātro saṃśabdamakapīḍitahacordhvaspreti, viskṛtahasa punarādhmāyata, bhavāla, lāmantratradvimasādhyā mityācakṣate
commentary: (i) That (swelling) which is distended like a bladder full of air, is hard and which produces vāṭaja pains without any reason is the scrotal swelling of vāta origin. (ii) That which is coloured like a ripe udumbara fruit, is associated with fever, burning, hot sensation and which appears and gets inflamed quickly is the scrotal swelling of pitta origin. (iii) - That which is hard, has mild pain, is cold and is itching is the scrotal swelling of śleṣma origin. (iv) That which is soft, glossy and itching with mild pain, and which shines like palm fruit is the scrotal swelling of meda origin. (v) That which is covered with blackish blisters and is associated with the features of pittaja vṛddhi is the scrotal swelling of rakta origin. (vi) Mūtraja scrotal swelling occurs in them who habitually withhold urine; it swings like a water drum while walking and dysuria, pain in both the testes and oedema in the scrotum are produced; that is known as the scrotal swelling due to mūtra. (VII) Due to carrying heavy weights, fighting with stronger opponent, fall from a tree etc. and other special strains, the vāta gets vitiated and aggravated and having afflicted a part of the large bowel or of the other one (small bowel) goes down and reaches the hip joint regions; then remaining there like a glandular swelling it enters the scrotum like a distended bladder. On squeezing it goes up (reduces) with a gurgling noise and on releasing, it again swells (reappears). This is called hernia (āntravṛddhi) and is incurable.

sanskrit_text: तत्रातिर्मथुनादृतिब्रह्मच्रर्याद्वा तथाऽतिब्रह्मच्रारिणों च्निरोत्सृष्दां रज़स्वलां रीर्घरोमां कर्कशरोमां सड्डीर्णरोमां निग्रह्नरोमामद्वपद्वपरां महाद्वारामप्रियामकामामचौक्षसलिलप्रक्षालितयोनिमप्रक्षालितयोनिं योनिरोगोपस़ष्टां स्वभावतो वा दुष्टयोनि वियोनि वा नारीमत्यर्थ- करजदहानविषहाकनिपातनाद्वन्धनाद्वस्ताभि- तथा अपसवमानस्य घाताच्चतुष्पदीगमनादचौक्षसलिलप्रक्षालनादवपीडनाच्छक्कवेगविधारणा- प न्मैथनान्ते वाऽप्रक्षालनादिभिर्मेढमागम्य प्रकुपिता दोषाः क्षतेऽक्षते वा इवयथमुपजनयन्ति, तमुपदशमित्याचक्षत
transliteration: tatrātirmathunādṛtibrah macraryādvā tathā'tibrah macrāriṇom̐ cnirōtsṛṣdāṃ razasvalāṃ rīrgharōmāṃ karkaśarōmāṃ saḍḍīrṇarōmāṃ nigrahnarōmā madvapadvaparāṃ mahādvārāmapriyāmakāmām acaukṣasalilaprakṣālitayonim aprakṣālitayoniṃ yonirōgōpasaṣṭāṃ svabhāvatō vā duṣṭayoni viyoni vā nārīmatyartha- karajadahānaviṣahākanipātanādvandhanādvastābhi- tathā apasavamānasya ghātāccatuṣpadīgamanādacaukṣasalilaprakṣālanādavapīḍanācchakkavegavidhāraṇā- p nmaithanānte vā'prakṣālanādibhirmēḍhamāgamya prakupitā doṣāḥ kṣate'kṣate vā ivayathamupajanayanti, tamupadaśamityācakṣata
commentary: Due to excessive sexual intercourse, or due to prolonged celibacy, intercourse with a woman observing excessive abstinence or with one who has been discarded (by her folks) for a long time, or with a woman who is menstruating, who has long hairs, rough hairs, dense hairs· or who has hairs in the internal parts, or with one whose vaginal orifice is too small or too large, or with one who is not loved or who does not like sex, or one who has washed the genitals with dirty water or one who has not washed the genitals, or the one having genital diseases and intercourse with the one usually having distorted and infected genitals and in those men who enjoy such women excessively and because of the injury due to nails, teeth, poison or śūka, due to tying (of the penis), due to injury during masturbation, intercourse with female quadrupeds, due to washing the penis with dirty water, squeezing it, due to suppressing the discharge at the end of the intercourse or not washing the penis (at the end of intercourse), vitiated doṣas reaching the penis produce oedema with or without an ulcer; that is known as upadamśa.

sanskrit_text: स पञ्चविधस्त्रिभिर्दोषीः पृथक् समस्तेरसूजा चेति
transliteration: sa pañcavidhastribhir doṣīḥ pṛthak samasterasūjā ceti
commentary: That (upadamśa) is of five types; due to the three vitiated doṣas seperately, all combined together and that due to (vitiated) blood.

sanskrit_text: तत्र वातिके पारुष्यं त्वक्परिप्टनं स्तब्घमेढ़ता परुषशोफ़ता विविधाइच वातवेदनाः; पंत्तिके ज्वरः इवयथः पववोदुम्बरसड्कनशस्ती- व्रदाहः क्षिप्रपाकः पित्तवेदनाइच; इलैष्मिके इवयथः कप्डुमान् कठिनः स्निग्धः इलेष्मवेदनाइचः रक्तजे कृष्णस्फोटप्रादुर्भावोऽत्यर्थमसक्प्रवृत्तिः पित्तलिङ्कान्यत्यर्थ ज्वरदाहौ होषइच; याप्यइचैव कदाचित; सर्वजे सर्वलिड्नदर्शनमवदरणं च शेफसः क्टमिप्राद्रर्भावो मरणं चेति
transliteration: tatra vātike pāruṣyaṃ tvakpari pṭanaṃ stabghameḍhatā paruṣaśophatā vividhāica vātavedanāḥ; paṃttike jvaraḥ ivayathaḥ pavavodumbarasaḍkanśastī- vradāhaḥ kṣiprapākaḥ pittavedanāica; ilaiṣmike ivayathaḥ kapḍumān kaṭhinaḥ snigdhaḥ ileṣmavedanāicaḥ raktaje kṛṣṇasphoṭaprādurbhāvo'tyarthamasakpravṛttiḥ pittaliṅkānyat yartha jvaradāhavau hoṣaica; yāpyaicaiva kadācit; sarveje sarvaliḍnadarśanamavadaraṇaṃ ca śephasaḥ kṭamiprādrarbhāvo maraṇaṃ ceti
commentary: Now, in upadamśa caused by (vitiated) vāta, roughness, cracks in the skin, rigidity in the penis, induration, and different types of vātika pains occur. In upadamśa, caused by pitta, fever, oedema, redness like that of ripe udumbara, excessive burning, early suppuration and paittika pains occur. In upadamśa caused by kapha, oedema, itching, hardness and glossiness and śleṣmika pains occur. In upadamśa caused by rakta, appearance of black blisters, tendency for excessive bleeding, paittika features, excessive fever, burning and dryness occur; this is sometimes relievable. In upadamśa caused by all the doṣas (together), features of all the doṣas are seen, tearing of penis occurs, growth of organisms takes place and death results.

sanskrit_text: वातपित्तइलैंमाणीsघःप्रपत्नी वैंड्रेक्षेणोंहजानु- दीवी कुपितास्त्र जेडेवीस्ववंतिष्ठमानोः कॉलिम्तरेण पॉर्दमाश्रित्य हानेः शौर्फ जनयन्ति, तं इलीपदमित्यों वक्षते । त्त्रिविधं— वातपित्तकफनिमित्तमिति
transliteration: vātapittailaiṃmāṇīsghaḥprapatnī vaiṃḍrekṣeṇom̐hajānu- dīvī kupitāstra jeḍevīsvavaṃtiṣṭhamānoḥ kālimtareṇa pōrdamāśritya hāneḥ śaurpha janayanti, taṃ ilīpadamityom̐ vakṣate | ttrividhaṃ— vātapittakaphanimittamiti
commentary: The vitiated doṣas, vāta, pitta and kapha having gone down and having got into the waist, thighs, knees, and legs and in due course of time having got located into the feet slowly, produce swelling; that is called as ślīpada (elephant's feet). That is of three types – due to vāta, pitta and kapha.

sanskrit_text: तत्री बातजं खरं क्रव्णं पहषमंनिर्मित्तानिलरजं परिस्फुटत्ति च बहुशः, पित्तजं तु पीतातभासँमीषन्मूंद्व ज्वरदाहप्रायं च; इलेष्मजं तु कर्ण्टकेरुषचितं इवेतं स्निग्धावभासं मन्दवेदनं भारिकं महाग्रेन्थिकं च्च
transliteration: tatrī bātajaṃ kharaṃ kravṇaṃ pahaṣamaṃnnimittānilarajaṃ parisphuṭatti ca bahuśaḥ, pittajaṃ tu pītātabhāsaṃmīṣanmūṃdva jvaradāhaprāyaṃ ca; ileṣmajaṃ tu karṇṭakeruṣacitaṃ ivetaṃ snigdhāvabhāsaṃ mandavedanaṃ bhārikaṃ mahāgranthikaṃ cca
commentary: In (elephantiasis) due to vāta, skin becomes uneven, black, rough, with many tracks and vātika pains occur without any reason. In (elephantiasis) due to pitta, yellowishness, slight softness, fever and burning often occur. In (elephantiasis) due to kapha, whiteness, glossiness, mild pain, heaviness and big glandular enlargements occur and skin gets studded with thorns.

sanskrit_text: तत्र संवत्सरातीतमतिमहद्वल्मीकजाते प्रेस्तिमिति वर्जनीयानि
transliteration: tatra saṃvatsarātītamatimahadvalmīkajāte prestimiti varjanīyāni
commentary: That (elephantiasis) which is one year old, is too extensive, is like an anthill, and that which discharges should be discarded (from treatment).

sanskrit_text: भवन्ति चरक्रण त्रीण्यप्येतानि जानीयाच्छ्लीपदानि कफाच्छायात्। गुरुत्वं चे मेहत्त्वं च यस्मैान्नाँस्ति विना कफात्
transliteration: bhavanti carakraṇa trīṇyapyetāni jānīyācchlīpadāni kaphācchāyāt | gurutvaṃ ce mehattvaṃ ca yasmaiānnām̐sti vinā kaphāt
commentary: Though the elephantiasis is due to the three doṣas, still it should be known to be due predominently to kapha because its heaviness and extensiveness cannot be without kapha.

sanskrit_text: प्रुराणोदकभूयिष्ठाः सर्वर्बूष्ट च श्रीतलाः। ये देशास्तेष् जायन्ते इल्वेपदानि विझेषतः
transliteration: prurāṇodakabhūyiṣṭhāḥ sarvarbūṣṭa ca śrītalāḥ | ye deśāsteṣ jāyante ilvepadāni vijheṣataḥ
commentary: Elephantiasis occurs specially in those places where there is always a collection of stagnating water and dampness round the year.

sanskrit_text: पांदवंद्वस्तफोइचापि इत्रीपदं जायले नुषाम्। कर्ण सिमाहिक्रैड्डेपू केन्विस्टिक्टिक्सि प्लेटिंदः
transliteration: pāṃdavaṃdvastaphoicāpi itrīpadaṃ jāyale nuṣām | karṇa simāhikraiḍḍepū kenvisṭikṭiksi pleṭiṃdaḥ
commentary: Elephantiasis is produced in the hands also as in the feet of human beings. Some experts say that it occurs in the ears, eyes, nose and lips also.

sanskrit_text: अथातः क्षुद्ररोगाणां निदानं व्याख्यास्यामः
transliteration: athātaḥ kṣudrarogāṇāṃ nidānaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ
commentary: Now we would expound upon 'The Diagnosis of Minor Diseases.'

sanskrit_text: यथोवाच भगवान धन्वन्तरिः
transliteration: yathovāca bhagavān dhanvantariḥ
commentary: As was described by Lord Dhanvantari.

sanskrit_text: समासेन चतुर्दवारिशत् क्षुद्ररोगा भवन्ति। तद्यथा—अज- गल्लिका, यवप्रख्या, अन्धालजी, विवृता, कच्छपिका, वल्मीकं, इन्द्रवृद्धा, विस्फोटक:, अग्निरो- हिणी, पनसिका, पाषाणगर्दभ:, जालगर्दभ:, कक्षा, इरिवेल्लिका, चिप्पं, कुनखः अनुशयी, विदारिका, हाकराबुद, पामा, अलसेन्द्रलुप्तौ, दारुणक:, विर्चचका, रकसा, पाददारिका, कदरं, अहंषिका, पलितं, मसूरिका यौवनपिडका, पद्मिनोकण्टक:, जतुमणि:, मशकः, चर्मकोलः, तिलकालकः, न्यर्च्छ, व्यड्यः, परिवर्तिका, अवपाटिका, निहद्वप्रकशः, संनिरुद्धगुदः, अहिपुतनं, वृषणकच्छुः, भ गुद भ्रंहाइचेति
transliteration: samāsena caturdavāriśat kṣudrarogā bhavanti | tadyathā—aja- gallikā, yavaprakhyā, andhālajī, vivṛtā, kacchapikā, valmīkaṃ, indravṛddhā, visphoṭaka:, agniro- hiṇī, panasikā, pāṣāṇagardabha:, jālagardabha:, kakṣā, irivellikā, cippaṃ, kunakhaḥ anuśayī, vidārikā, hākarābuda, pāmā, alasendraluptau, dāruṇaka:, vircacakā, rakasā, pādadārikā, kadaraṃ, ahaṃṣikā, palitaṃ, masūrikā yauvanapiḍakā, padminokaṇṭaka:, jatumaṇi:, maśakaḥ, carmakolaḥ, tilakālakaḥ, nyarccha, vyaḍyaḥ, parivartikā, avapāṭikā, nihadvaprakaśaḥ, saṃniruddhagudaḥ, ahipūtanaṃ, vṛṣaṇakacchuḥ, bha guda bhraṃhāiceti
commentary: The minor diseases are forty-four in number in all. They are : Ajagallikā, Yavaprakhyā, Andhālajī, Vivṛtā, Kacchapikā, Valmīka, Indravṛddhā, Panasikā, Pāṣāṇagardabha, Jālagardabha, Kakṣā, Visphotaka, Agnirohiṇī, Cippa (whitlow), Kunakha (paronychia), Anuśayī, Vidārikā, Śarkarārbuda, Pāmā, Vicarcikā, Rakasā, Pādadārikā (rhagades), Alasa, Kadara, Dāruṇaka, Indralupta (alopecia), Arunsikā, Palita, Masūrikā, Yauvanapidakā (pimples), Padminīkantaka, Jatumani, Carmakīla (warts), Masaka, Nyaccha, Tilakālaka, Vyanga, Parivartikā (paraphimosis), Avapāṭikā, Niruddhaprakaśa (phimosis), Sanniruddhaguda (anal stenosis), Ahipūtana (napkin rash), Vrsanakacchu, Guda-bhranśa (rectal prolapse), and others.

sanskrit_text: हिनग्धा सवर्णा प्रथिता मोरुजा मुक्गसन्निभा। कफवालोस्थिता जेया बालानामजगहिलका
transliteration: hinagdhā savarṇā prathitā morujā mukgasannibhā | kaphavālosthitā jeyā bālānāmajagahilkā
commentary: Ajagallikā should be known to occur in children, is produced by vitiated kapha and vāta, is glossy, has same colour as that of skin, is knotted, painless and is like a mudga.

sanskrit_text: यवाकारा सुक्रद्विना ग्रथिता मांससंश्रिता। पिडका रलेष्मकाता#यां प्रवप्रस्येति सोच्यते
transliteration: yavākārā sukradvinā grathitā māṃsasaṃśritā | piḍakā raleṣmakātā#yāṃ pravaprasyeti socyate
commentary: That eruption is called yavaprakhyā which is produced by kapha and vāta, is of the shape of barley, is very firm, knotted and is located in the muscles.

sanskrit_text: घनामवक्रां पिडकामन्नतां परिमण्डलाम। अन्धालजीमल्पप्रयां तां विद्यात् कफवातजाम
transliteration: ghanāmavakrāṃ piḍakām annatāṃ parimaṇḍalām | andhālajīmalpaprayāṃ tāṃ vidyāt kaphavātajām
commentary: That swelling is known as andhālajī which is due to kapha and vāta, is firm, without a punctum, raised, circular and contains little pus.

sanskrit_text: विव्रतास्प्रां महादाहां पक्वोदुम्बुरसन्निधाम्। विवृतामिति तां विद्यात् पित्तोत्थां परिमण्डलाम
transliteration: vivratā sprāṃ mahādāhāṃ pakvodumburasar nnidhām | vivṛtāmiti tāṃ vidyāt pittotthāṃ parimaṇḍalām
commentary: That is known as vivṛtā which arises due to pitta, has a wide mouth, excessive burning, has the colour of a ripe udumbara fruit and is circular.

sanskrit_text: ग्रथिताः पञ्च वा पङ्वा दारुणाः कच्छपीस्ताः। कफानिलाभ्यां पिडका जैया कच्छपिका बुध्नः
transliteration: grathitāḥ pañca vā paṅvā dāruṇāḥ kacchapīstāḥ | kaphānilābhyāṃ piḍakā jaiyā kacchapikā budhnaḥ
commentary: The wise call those swellings as kacchapikās which are due to kapha and vāta, are knotted, five or six in number, are hard and have a hump like that of a tortoise.

sanskrit_text: प्रप्रप्रप्रप्रदलब्रे सल्धौ प्रोवायास्प्रध्वज्ञत्रुष्पि। प्रत्यिवर्वलमीक्रमचास्तः सम्रप्रक्रवीक्ले। तोद्वलेक्षरीवाहकण्डूमिक्रिमुखेवर तः। व्याधिर्वल्मीक् इत्य्रेष क्रफ़पित्तानिक्री.दूवः
transliteration: praprapraprapradalabre saldhau provāyāspradhvajñatruṣpi | pratyivarvalamīkramacāstaḥ samraprakravīkle | todvalekṣarīvāhakaṇḍūmikrimukhevara taḥ | vyādhirvalmīk ityreṣa kraphapittānakrī.dūvaḥ
commentary: That disease is valmīka which is due to kapha, pitta and vāta, which arises on the surfaces of palms and soles, in the joints of neck, and in the regions above the clavicles, is knotted like an anthill, increases slowly and in which pricking pain, soddening, burning sensation and itching occur around the openings.

sanskrit_text: पद्मप्रष्करवन्मध्ये पिडकाभिः समाचिताम्। इन्द्रवुद्धां तु तां विद्याद्वातपित्तोत्थितां भिषक्
transliteration: padmapraṣkaravanmadhye piḍakābhiḥ samācitām | indravuddhāṃ tu tāṃ vidyādvātapittotthitāṃ bhiṣak
commentary: The physician calls that indravṛddhā which arises due to vāta and pitta and is full of small boils in the centre as in a lotus fruit.

sanskrit_text: मण्डलं वत्तमृत्सन्नं सरक्तं पिडकाचितम्। रुजाकरीं गर्दभिकां तां विद्याद्वातपित्तजाम्। कणौं परि समन्ताद्वा पष्ठे वा पिडकोग्ररुक्। शालूकवत्पनसिकां तां विद्याच्छ्लेष्मवातजाम्
transliteration: maṇḍalaṃ vattamṛtsannaṃ saraktaṃ piḍakācitam | rujākarīṃ gardabhikāṃ tāṃ vidyādvātapittajām | kaṇauṃ pari samantādvā paṣṭhe vā piḍakograruk | śālūkavatpanasikāṃ tāṃ vidyācchleṣmavātajām
commentary: Those eruptions are known as gardabhikas which are produced by vāta and pitta, are circular, raised spherically, full of blood and produce pain. That swelling is known as panasikā which is due to kapha and vāta, occurs on the ears or around them, or on the back, has severe pain and is like the root of a waterlily.

sanskrit_text: हनुसन्धा समुद्भूत शाफमल्परुज स्थिरम्। पाषाणगर्दभं विद्यादब्लासपवनात्मकम्
transliteration: hanusandhā samudbhūta śāphamalparuja sthiram | pāṣāṇagardabhaṃ vidyādablāsapavanātmakam
commentary: That is known as pāṣāṇagardabha which arises due to kapha and vāta, occurs in the region of temporomandibular joints, has inflammation, mild pain and is fixed.

sanskrit_text: विसर्पवत् सर्पति यो दाहज्वरकरस्तनः। अपाकः इवयथः पित्तात् स ज्ञेयो जालगर्दभः
transliteration: visarpavat sarpati yo dāhajvarakarastanaḥ | apākaḥ ivayathaḥ pittāt sa jñeyo jālagardabhaḥ
commentary: That is known as jālagardabha which is produced due to pitta, spreads like cellulitis, produces burning sensation and fever, is slender, non-suppurating and is oedematous.

sanskrit_text: पिडिकामत्तमाड़क्स्थां वृत्तामुग्रहजाज्वराम्। सर्वात्प्रकां, सर्वलिङ्कां जानीयादिरिवेल्लिकाम
transliteration: piḍikāmatta māḍaksthāṃ vṛttāmugrahajājvarām | sarvātprakāṃ, sarvalliṅkāṃ jānīyādirivellikāma
commentary: That swelling should be known as irivellikā which is due to all the three (vāṭa, pitta and kapha), has the features of all (the vitiated doṣas), is situated in the head, is circular and has severe pain and fever.

sanskrit_text: बाहुपाइवसिकक्षास क्वब्णरफोटाँ सवेदनाम। पित्तप्रकोपसंभुतां कक्षामिति विनिदिशोत। एकामेवंविधां दृष्टवा पिटिकां रफोटसन्निभाम्रा त्वग्गतां पित्तकोर्पन गन्धनामां प्रचक्षते
transliteration: bāhupāivasikakṣāsa kvabṇaraphoṭām̐ savedanām | pittaprakopasaṃbhutāṃ kakṣāmiti vinidiśota | ekāmevaṃvidhāṃ dṛṣṭavā piṭikāṃ raphoṭasannibhāmrā tvaggatāṃ pittakor pana gandhanāmāṃ pracakṣate
commentary: That should be known as kakṣā which is due to vitiation of pitta, occurs in the arms, lateral chest wall, shoulder and axilla, has black blisters and is associated with pain. In the same way another swelling seen with blisters of similar colour situated in the skin, due to vitiated pitta is called gandhanāmā.

sanskrit_text: अग्निदग्धनिभाः स्फोटाः सज्वराः पित्तरवंततः। क्वचित् सर्वत्र वा देहें स्मृता विस्फोटका इंति
transliteration: agnidagdhanibhāḥ sphoṭāḥ sajvarāḥ pittaravaṃtataḥ | kvacit sarvatra vā deheṃ smṛtā visphoṭakā iṃti
commentary: They are known as visphotaka which are due to pitta and rakta, occur at one place or all over the body, have blisters similar to those produced by fire cautery and are associated with fever.

sanskrit_text: कक्षाभागेष ये स्फोटा जायन्तें मांसदार ( र )णा:। अन्तदहिज्वरकरा दीप्तपावकसन्निभा:। सप्ताहाद्वा दशाहाद्वा पेक्षाद्वा घ्नन्ति मानेवसं। तामग्निरोहिणीं विद्यादसाध्यां सम्निपाततः
transliteration: kakṣābhāgeṣa ye sphoṭā jāyanteṃ māṃsadāra (ra)ṇā: | antadahijvarakarā dīptapāvakasannibhā: | saptāhādvā daśāhādvā pekṣādvā ghnanti mānevasaṃ | tāmagnirohiṇīṃ vidyādasādhyāṃ samnipātataḥ
commentary: That is known as agnirohiṇī which is due to all (the three doṣas i.e. vāta, pitta and kapha), which produces blisters in the region of axilla, tears the muscles, gives rise to burning sensation internally, and fever, is coloured like a blazing fire, kills the person in a week, ten days or fortnight and is incurable.

sanskrit_text: नखमांसमधिष्ठाय पित्तं वातइच वेदनाम्। करोति दाहपाकौ च तं व्यांधि चिप्पमादिशेत्। तदेवाक्षतरोगाख्यं तथोपनखमित्यपि
transliteration: nakhamāṃsamadhiṣṭhāya pittaṃ vātaica vedanām | karoti dāhapākau ca taṃ vyāṃdhi cippamādiśet | tadevākṣatarogākhyaṃ tathopanakhamityapi
commentary: That disease is known as cippa which is due to pitta and vāta, occurs in the nail and nail bed, is painful and produces burning and suppuration. This is also called akṣata disease and is synonymous with upanakha.

sanskrit_text: अभिघातात प्रदृष्टो यो नखो रूक्षोऽसितः खरः। भवेत्तं कुनखं विद्यात कुलीनमिति संज्ञितम्। गम्भीरामल्पसंरम्भाम् सवर्णामपरिस्थिताम। कफादन्त:प्रपाकां तां विद्यादन्हायों भिषक्
transliteration: abhighātāta pradṛṣṭo yo nakho rūkṣo'sitaḥ kharaḥ | bhavettaṃ kunakhaṃ vidyāta kulīnamiti saṃjñitam | gambhīrāmalpasaṃrambhām savarṇāmaparisthitāma | kaphādanta:prapākāṃ tāṃ vidyādanhāyom̐ bhiṣak |
commentary: That nail which is damaged by trauma, is dry, blackish and rough is known as kunakha and is called as kulīna. The physician should recognise that as anuśayī which is due to kapha, occurs on the head, is deep, mildly oedematous, is of the colour of skin, and suppurates internally.

sanskrit_text: विदारीकन्दवद्वत्तां कक्षावडक्षणसन्धिष्। रक्तां विदारिकां विद्यात् सर्वजां सर्वलक्षणाम्। प्राप्य मांसंसिरास्नाय इलेष्मा मेदस्तथाऽनिलः। प्रन्थिं कुर्वन्ति भिन्नोऽसौ मधुर्सापर्वसानिभम्। स्रवत्यास्नावमत्यर्थं तत्र वद्धिं गतोऽनिलः। मांसं विशोष्य प्रथितां शर्कराँ जनयैत पूनः। दुर्गन्धं क्लम्मत्यथं नानावणं ततः सिराः। स्रवन्ति सहसा रक्तं तद्विद्याच्छर्कराबुदम्
transliteration: vidārīkandavadvattāṃ kakṣāvaḍakṣaṇasandhiṣ | raktāṃ vidārikāṃ vidyāt sarvajāṃ sarvalakṣaṇām | prāpya māṃsasirāsnāya ileṣmā medastathā'nilaḥ | pranthiṃ kurvanti bhinno'sau madhursāparvasānibham | sravatyāsnāvamatyarthaṃ tatra vaddhiṃ gato'nilaḥ | māṃsaṃ viśoṣya prathitāṃ śarkarāṃ janayaita pūnaḥ | durgandhaṃ klam matyathaṃ nānāvaṇaṃ tataḥ sirāḥ | sravanti sahasā raktaṃ tadvidyāccharkarābudam |
commentary: That is known as vidārikā which is due to all (the three vāta, pitta and kapha) and has the features of all the doṣas, occurs within the folds of axillae and groins, is circular like the bulb of vidārī and is reddish. Muscles, vessels, ligaments, kapha, fat and vāta mixing together produce glandular swellings upon the bursting of which an excessive secretion similar to honey, ghee and fat is discharged; then, vāyu having increased, and having atrophied the muscles produces concretions in the gland again. Bad odour, excessive soddening, and sudden discharge of blood of various colours occurs from the vessels; that is known as śarkarārbuda.

sanskrit_text: पामाविचर्च्यों क्रम्टेष्ट्रेस् परिक्रमणझीलस्य वायुरत्यर्थरूक्षयोः। पादयोः कुरुते दारीं सरूज़ां तलसंश्रितः
transliteration: pāmāvicarcyom̐ kramṭeṣṭres parikramaṇajhīlasya vāyuratyartharūkṣayoḥ | pādayoḥ kurute dārīṃ sarūzāṃ talasaṃśritaḥ
commentary: Pāmā, vicarcikā, and rakasā have been described with kuṣṭha diseases. In the excessively dry feet of those who do a lot of walking, the vāyu getting located in the soles produces painful fissures.

sanskrit_text: शर्करोन्मथिते पादे क्षते वा कण्टकादिभिः। मेदोरक्तानगैश्चेव दोषैर्वा जायते नृणाम्। सकीलकठिनो ग्रन्थिनम्नमध्योन्नतोऽपि वा। कोलमात्रः सरुक् स्रावी जायतें कदरस्तु सः
transliteration: śarkaronmathite pāde kṣate vā kaṇṭakādibhiḥ | medoraktānagaishceva doṣairvā jāyate nṛṇām | sakīlakaṭhino granthinamnamadhyonnato'pi vā | kolamātraḥ saruk srāvī jāyateṃ kadarastu saḥ
commentary: When the feet get traumatised repeatedly by gravels or injured by thorns etc. the vitiated doṣas following the meda and rakta produce kadara in human beings; these lesions have a central core, are hard, knotted, depressed or else elevated in the centre, are about the size of a seed of plum, are painful and have a discharge.

sanskrit_text: क्लिन्ना ज़ुल्यन्तरौ पादौ कण्डूदाहरुगन्दितौ। दुष्टकर्दमसंस्पर्शादलसं तं विनिद्रिशेत
transliteration: klinnā zulyantarau pādau kaṇḍūdāharuganditau | duṣṭakardamasaṃsparśādalasaṃ taṃ vinidriśeta
commentary: That is called alasa which occurs in the sodden interdigital clefts of feet coming into contact with dirty mud. They are associated with itching, burning and pain.

sanskrit_text: रोमकपानगं पित्तं वातेन सह मूच्छितम्। प्रच्यावयति रोमाणि ततः इलेष्मा स्रशोणितः। रुणद्धि रोमकूपांस्तु ततोऽन्येषामसंभवः। तदिन्द्रलप्तं खालित्यं रुज्येति च विभाव्यते
transliteration: romakapānagaṃ pittaṃ vātena saha mūcchitam | pracyāvayati romāṇi tataḥ ileṣmā sraśoṇitaḥ | ruṇaddhi romakūpāṃstu tato'nyeṣāmasaṃbhavaḥ | tadindralaptaṃ khālityaṃ rujyeti ca vibhāvyate
commentary: Pitta combining with vāta and getting into the pores of hairs (hair follicles) causes fall of hairs; then kapha alongwith rakta obstructs the pores of those hairs and makes it impossible for other hairs to grow. That is known as indralupta, khālitya or rujyā.

sanskrit_text: दारुणा कण्डरा रूक्षा केशभूमिः प्रपाटचते। कफवातप्रकोपेण विद्याद्दारणकं तु तम्
transliteration: dāruṇā kaṇḍarā rūkṣā keśabhūmiḥ prapāṭacate | kaphavātaprakopeṇa vidyāddāraṇakaṃ tu tam
commentary: That should be known as dāruṇaka, in which the scalp becomes hard, itching, dry and fissured due to aggravation of kapha and vāta.

sanskrit_text: अरूंषि बहुवक्त्राणि बहुक्लेदीनि मर्धनि। कफासुक्कमिकोपेन नृणां विद्यादरुंषिकाम्
transliteration: arūṃṣi bahuvaktrāṇi bahukledīni mardhani | kaphā sukkamikopena nṛṇāṃ vidyādarūṃṣikām
commentary: When excessively sodden lesions having multiple openings are produced in the head of human beings due to vitiation of kapha, rakta and organisms, that should be known as aruṇsikā.

sanskrit_text: क्रोधशोकश्रमक्रतः शरीरोष्मा शिरोगतः। पित्तं च केशान् पचति पलितं तेन जायते
transliteration: krodhaśokaśramakrataḥ śarīroṣmā śirogataḥ | pittaṃ ca keśān pacati palitaṃ tena jāyate
commentary: Warmth produced by anger, grief and exertion in the body, having gone to the head, as also the pitta, mature the hairs; palita (grey hairs) is thus produced.

sanskrit_text: दाहज्वररुजावन्तस्ताम्प्राः स्फोटाः सपीतकाः। गात्रेषु वदने चान्तविज्ञेयास्ता मसूरिकाः
transliteration: dāhajvararujāvantastāmprāḥ sphoṭāḥ sapītakāḥ | gātreṣu vadane cāntavijñeyāstā masūrikāḥ
commentary: Blisters which are coppery as well as yellowish and are found all over the body and on the face as well as within the oral cavity and which are associated with burning sensation, fever and pain are known as masūrikā.

sanskrit_text: हाल्मलीकप्टकप्रख्या: कफमारुतशोणितः। जायन्ते पिडका यूनां वक्रे या मुखदूषिकाः
transliteration: hālmalīkapṭakaprakhyā: kaphamārut aśoṇitaḥ | jāyante piḍakā yūnāṃ vakre yā mukhadūṣikāḥ
commentary: The boils which are produced in the face of the young, which are like the thorns of śālmalī and which are due to kapha, vāta and rakta are mukhadūṣikās.

sanskrit_text: कण्टकेराचितं वर्त्त कण्डमत पाण्डमण्डलम्। पद्मिनीकण्टकप्रख्यैस्तदाख्यं कफवातजम्
transliteration: kaṇṭakerācitaṃ vartta kaṇḍamata pāṇḍamaṇḍalam | padminīkaṇṭakaprakhyaistadākhyaṃ kaphavātajam
commentary: That is known as padminī-kantaka which is full of thorns, is circular, itching, has a yellowish periphery and is like the thorns of padminī; this is produced by kapha and vāta.

sanskrit_text: नीरुजं सममत्सन्नं मण्डलं कफरक्तजम्। सहजं रक्तमीषच्च इलक्ष्णं जत्रमांण विद्रः
transliteration: nīrujaṃ samamatsannaṃ maṇḍalaṃ kapharaktajam | sahajaṃ raktamīṣacca ilakṣṇaṃ jatramāṃṇa vidraḥ
commentary: That lesion which is painless, raised evenly, circular, produced by kapha and rakta, is hereditary, reddish and smooth is called jatumani.

sanskrit_text: अवेदनं स्थिरं चैव यस्य गात्रेष् दृइयते। माषवत्क्वडणम्त्सन्नमनिलान्मषकं वदेत
transliteration: avedanaṃ sthiraṃ caiva yasya gātreṣ dṛiyate | māṣavatkvaḍaṇamtsannamanilānmaṣakaṃ vadeta
commentary: Those eruptions which are seen all over the body, are painless and fixed, are raised and blackish, like pulse of māṣa and are due to vāta are called maṣaka.

sanskrit_text: कृष्णानि तिलमात्राणि नीरुजानि समानि च। वातपित्तकफोच्छोषात्तान् विद्यात्तिलकालकान्
transliteration: kṛṣṇāni tilamātrāṇi nīrujāni samāni ca | vātapittakaphocchoṣāttān vidyāttilakālakān
commentary: Those eruptions which are blackish, are of the size and shape of sesamum, are painless, and are due to drying up of vāta, pitta and kapha are known as tilakālaka.

sanskrit_text: मण्डलं महदल्पं वा इयामं वा यदि वा सितम्। सहजं नीरुजं गात्रे न्यच्छमित्यभिधीयते
transliteration: maṇḍalaṃ mahad alpaṃ vā iyāmaṃ vā yadi vā sitam | sahajaṃ nīrujaṃ gātre nyacchamityabhidhīyate
commentary: Those circular eruptions on the body which are big or small, blackish or whitish, which are hereditary and painless are called nyaccha.

sanskrit_text: समृत्थाननिदानाभ्यां चर्मकीलं प्रकीतितम्। कोधायासप्रकुपितो वायः पित्तेन संयुतः। सहसा मुखमागत्य मण्डलं विसुजत्यतः। नीरुजं तनकं इयाबं मुखे व्यड्रं तमादिशेत्। कृऽणमेवंगूणं गात्रे मुखे वा नीलिकां विद्रः
transliteration: samṛtthānanidānābhyāṃ carmakīlaṃ prakītitam | kodhāyāsaprakupito vāyaḥ pittena saṃyutaḥ | sahasā mukhamāgatya maṇḍalaṃ visujatyataḥ | nīrujaṃ tanakaṃ iyābaṃ mukhe vyaḍraṃ tamādiśet | kṛ'ṇamevaṃgūṇaṃ gātre mukhe vā nīlikāṃ vidraḥ
commentary: Because of similarity in the pathogenesis and diagnosis, carmakīla has already been described. The vāyu aggravated by anger and exertion in combination with pitta, reaching the face suddenly produces circular patches there, which are painless, small in size and blackish and are called vyanga. Eruptions in the body and the face with same features (as vyanga) but blackish in colour are known as nīlikā.

sanskrit_text: मर्दनात् पीडनाच्चाति तथैवाप्यभिघाततः। मेढ़चर्म यदा वायर्भजते सर्वतइचर:। तदा वातोपस्‍ष्‍टं त्र चर्म प्रतिनिवर्तते। मर्णरधस्तात् कोहाइच ग्रन्थिरूपेण लम्बते। सवेदनः सदाहश्च पार्क च व्रजति क्वचित्। मारुतागन्तुसंभूतां विद्यात्तां परिर्वातकाम। सकण्ड्रः कठिना चापि सैव इलेष्मसमुत्थिता
transliteration: mardanāt pīḍanāccāti tathaivāpyabhighātataḥ | meḍhacarma yadā vā yarbhajate sarvataicaraḥ | tadā vātopaṣṣṭaṃ tra carma pratinivartate | marṇaradhastāt kohāica granthirūpeṇa lambate | savedanaḥ sadāhaśca pārka ca vrajati kvacit | mār utāgantusaṃbhūtāṃ vidyāttāṃ parirvātakāma | sakaṇḍraḥ kaṭhinā cāpi saiva ileṣmasamutthitā
commentary: Due to excessive rubbing and squeezing and also due to excessive trauma, when the all pervading (vyāna) vāyu comes to the skin of the penis, the vāyu having got located there retracts the skin leaving the glans below; and then the prepuce swells up like a gland. In some it is associated with pain, burning and suppuration. This is produced by vāta and the external factors (such as trauma etc.) and is known as parivartikā. If it is associated with itching and is hard, the same should be known to have arisen due to kapha.

sanskrit_text: अल्पीयःखां यदा हर्षाद्वालां गच्छेत् स्त्रियं नरः। हस्ताभिघातादथवा चर्मण्युद्वतिते बलात। मर्दनात्पीडनाद्वाऽपि शुक्रवेगविघाततः। यस्यावपाटचते चर्म तां विद्यादवपाटिकाम्। वातोपसृष्टमेवं तु चर्म संश्रयते मणिम्। मणिइचर्मोपनद्वस्तु मूत्रस्रोतो रुणद्धि च। निरुद्धप्रकशे तस्मिन्मन्दधारमवेदनम्। मुत्रं प्रवर्तते जन्तोर्मणिर्न च विदीर्यते। निरुद्धप्रकशं विद्याद्दुरूढां चावपाटिकाम्
transliteration: alpīyaḥkhāṃ yadā harṣādvālāṃ gacchet striyaṃ naraḥ | hastābhighātādathavā carmaṇyudvatite balāt | mardanātpīḍanādvā'pi śukravegavighātataḥ | yasyāvapāṭacate carma tāṃ vidyādavapāṭikām | vātōpasṛṣṭamevaṃ tu carma saṃśrayate maṇim | maṇicarmopanadvastu mūtrasroto ruṇaddhi ca | niruddhaprakaśe tasminmandadhāramavedanam | mutraṃ pravartate jantormaṇirna ca vidīryate | niruddhaprakaśaṃ vidyāddurūḍhāṃ cāvapāṭikām
commentary: When an excited man does sexual intercourse with an adolescent girl having narrow vaginal orifice, or due to manual trauma, the foreskin gets forcibly retracted or due to rubbing, a squeezing or also due to suppressing seminal discharge, penile skin gets torn; that is known as avapāṭikā. When the vāyu having got vitiated and located in the prepuce and the glans, produces adhesions between the two, the urinary passage gets obstructed. With the passage getting narrow he passes thin stream of urine without pain and the glans cannot be exposed. This is also known as niruddhaprakaśa and is also due to improper healing of avapāṭikā.

sanskrit_text: वेगसंधारणाद्वार्युविहतो गदमाश्रितः। निरुणद्धि महत्स्रोतः सुक्ष्मद्वारं करोति च। मार्गस्य सौक्ष्म्यात् कृच्छेण पुरीषं तस्य गच्छति। सन्निरुद्धगदं व्याधिमेनं विद्यात् सुदुस्तरम्
transliteration: vegasaṃdhāraṇādvāryuvihato gadamāśritaḥ | niruṇaddhi mahatsrotaḥ sukṣmadvāraṃ karoti ca | mārgasya saukṣmyāt kṛccheṇa purīṣaṃ tasya gacchati | sanniruddhagadaṃ vyādhimenaṃ vidyāt sudustaram |
commentary: Due to suppression of the evacuatory processes, the vāyu gets vitiated and having got located in the rectum, obstructs the large bowel and narrows its external opening. Due to the smallness of the passage, the faeces are passed with difficulty in the person and this disease is known as sanniruddhaguda and is curable with difficulty.

sanskrit_text: शक्टन्मूत्रसमायुक्तेऽधौतेऽपाने शिशोर्भवेत्। स्विग्नस्यास्नाध्यमानस्य कण्डूं रक्तकफो द्वा। कण्ड्रयनात्ततः क्षिप्रं स्फोटाः स्रावइच जायते। एकीभतं व्रणैर्घोरं तं विद्यादहिप्तनम्
transliteration: śakṭanmūtrasamāyukte'dhau te'pāne śiśorbhavet | svignasyāsnādhyamānasya kaṇḍūṃ raktakapho dvā | kaṇḍrayanāttataḥ kṣipraṃ sphoṭāḥ srāvaica jāyate | ekībhataṃ vraṇairghoraṃ taṃ vidyādahiptanam |
commentary: When the faeces and urine are present near the anus which has not been cleaned with water and in those infants to whom even after perspiration a bath has not been given, itching is produced due to rakta and kapha. Then due to itching, blisters and discharges are quickly produced and all the ulcers become one and this serious disease is called ahipūtana.

sanskrit_text: स्नानोत्सादनहीनस्य मलो वृषणसंश्रितः। यदा प्रक्लिद्यते स्वेदात् कण्डू संजनयेत्तदा। तत्र कण्डूयनात् क्षिप्रं स्फोटाः स्रावइच जायते। प्राहर्व षणकच्छं तां इलेष्मरक्तप्रकोपजाम्
transliteration: snānōtsād anahīnasya malo vṛṣaṇasaṃśritaḥ | yadā praklidyate svedāt kaṇḍū saṃjanayettadā | tatra kaṇḍūyanāt kṣipraṃ sphoṭāḥ srāvaica jāyate | prāharva ṣaṇakacchaṃ tāṃ ileṣmaraktaprakopajām |
commentary: When, in absence of baths and annointments, faeces accumulate in the scrotal region and when that becomes sodden due to sweat, itching is produced. Then due to that itching, blisters and a discharge are quickly produced. This is called vṛṣaṇakacchū and is due to aggravation of kapha and rakta.

sanskrit_text: प्रवाहणातिसाराभ्यां निर्गच्छति गदं बहिः। रूक्षदुबंलदेहस्य तं गुदभ्रंशमादिशेत्
transliteration: pravāhaṇātisārābhyāṃ nirgacchati gadaṃ bahiḥ | rūkṣadubaṃladehasya taṃ gudabhraṃśamādiśet |
commentary: Due to straining and diarrhoea the rectum comes out in the dehydrated and emaciated person; that is called prolapse rectum.

sanskrit_text: अथातः श्कदोषनिदानं व्याख्यास्यामः
transliteration: athātaḥ śkadoṣanidānaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ
commentary: Now we would expound upon 'The Diagnosis of Śūka-doṣa'.

sanskrit_text: यथोवाच भगवान् धन्वन्तरिः
transliteration: yathovāca bhagavān dhanvantariḥ
commentary: As was described by Lord Dhanvantari.

sanskrit_text: हाकदोष निमित्ता दहा लिड्मवृद्धिमिच्छतामक्रमप्रवृत्तानां अप्ठीलिका, चाष्टो च व्याधयो जायन्ते । तद्यथा—सर्षपिका, ग्रथितं, कुम्भीका, अलजी, मृदितं, संमूढपिडका, अवमन्थः, पुष्करिका, स्पर्शहानिः, उत्तमा, शतपोनकः, त्वक्पाकः शोणितार्बुदं, मांसार्बुदं, मांसपाकः, विद्रधिः, तिलकालकइचेति
transliteration: hākadoṣa nimittā dahā liḍmavṛddhimicchatāmakramapravṛttānām apṭhīlikā, cāṣṭo ca vyādhayo jāyante | tadyathā—sarṣapikā, grathitaṃ, kumbhīkā, alajī, mṛditaṃ, saṃmūḍhapiḍakā, avamanthaḥ, puṣkarikā, sparśahāniḥ, uttamā, śataponakaḥ, tvakpākaḥ śoṇitārbudaṃ, māṃsārbudaṃ, māṃsapākaḥ, vidradhiḥ, tilakālakaiceti
commentary: In those desirous of getting their penis enlarged and in those engaged in irregular procedures, eighteen diseases are produced due to śūka-doṣa. They are as follows : 1. Sarsapikā, 2. Aṣṭhilikā, 3. Grathita, 4. Kumbhikā, 5. Alajī, 6. Mṛdita, 7. Saṁmūḍhapiḍakā, 8. Avamantha, 9. Puṣkarikā, 10. Sparśahāni, 11. Uttamā, 12. Śataponaka, 13. Tvakpāka, 14. Śoṇitārbuda, 15. Māṁsārbuda, 16. Māṁsapāka, 17. Vidradhi and 18. Tilakālaka.

sanskrit_text: गौरसर्षपतुल्या तु शूकदुभंग्नहंतुका। पिडका कफरक्ताभ्यां ज्ञेया सर्षपिका बुधैः
transliteration: gaurasarṣapatulyā tu śūkadubhaṃgnahaṃtukā | piḍakā kapharaktābhyāṃ jñeyā sarṣapikā budhaiḥ
commentary: The boils which are like white mustard and which are due to (vitiated) kapha and rakta as a result of improper use of the recipes for elongating the penis are known as sarṣapikā by the wise.

sanskrit_text: कठिना विषमैरन्तैर्मारुतस्य प्रकोपतः। हाकैस्तु विषसंभग्नैः पिडकाऽप्ठीलिका भवेत
transliteration: kaṭhinā viṣamairantairmārutasya prakōpataḥ | hākaistu viṣasaṃbhagnaiḥ piḍakā'pṭhīlikā bhaveta
commentary: The boils which are hard with irregular edges and are due to vitiation of the vāta as a result of the use of recipes for enlarging the genitals, along with poisonous materials are called aṣṭhīlikā.

sanskrit_text: श्कर्मयंत् पूरितं शहवदग्रथितं तत् कफोत्थितम। कुम्भीका रक्तपित्तोत्था जाम्बवास्थिनिभाऽङ्गभा
transliteration: śkarmayaṃt pūritaṃ śahavadagrathitaṃ tat kafōtthitama | kumbhīkā raktapittotthā jāmbavāsthinibhā'ṅgabhā
commentary: Grathita is that which is produced due to constant use of śūka and arises due to vitiated kapha. Kumbhika arises due to vitiation of rakta and pitta, is like the seed of jambu, and is black.

sanskrit_text: अलजीलक्षणेर्युक्तामलजीं च वितर्कयेत। मदितं पीडितं यत्त संरब्धं वायकोपतः
transliteration: alajīlakṣaṇeryuktāmalajīṃ ca vitarkayeta | maditaṃ pīḍitaṃ yatta saṃrabdhaṃ vāyakopataḥ
commentary: Alajī has already been discussed alongwith its features. Mṛdita is that which due to compression, is associated with inflammation, and is due to vitiation of vāta.

sanskrit_text: पाणिभ्यां भ्रशसंमुढे संमुढ़पिडका भवेत्। दीर्घा बह व्यइच पिडका दीर्यन्ते मध्यतस्त्र याः। सोऽवमन्थः कफासग्भ्यां वेदनारोमहर्षक्रत्
transliteration: pāṇibhyāṃ bhraśasaṃmuḍhe saṃmuḍhapiḍakā bhavet | dīrghā baha vyaica piḍakā dīryante madhyatastra yāḥ | so'vamanthaḥ kaphāsagbhyāṃ vedanāromaharṣakrat |
commentary: Saṁmūḍha-piḍakā is produced by rubbing the penis with both hands. Those piḍakās which are large, numerous and cracked in the centre are avamanthas; they are due to vitiated kapha and blood and produce pain and horripilation.

sanskrit_text: पित्तशोणितसंभूता पिडका पिडकाचिता। पद्मपुष्करसंस्थाना ज्ञेया पुष्करिकेति सा। जनयेत् स्पर्शहार्नि त्र शोणितं श्कदूषितम्
transliteration: pittaśōṇitasaṃbhūtā piḍakā piḍakācitā | padmapuṣkarasaṃsthānā jñeyā puṣkariketi sā | janayet sparśahārni tra śoṇitaṃ śkadūṣitam |
commentary: That piḍakā which is due to vitiation of pitta and śoṇita, which is surrounded by many smaller piḍakās, and which is like a lotus seed is known as puṣkarikā. Sparśahāni (loss of sensation) is produced by vitiated śoṇita due to śūka.

sanskrit_text: मदगमाषोपमा रक्ता पिडका रक्तपित्तजा। उत्तमैषा तु विज्ञेया शुकाजीर्णनिमित्तजा
transliteration: madagamāṣopamā raktā piḍakā raktapittajā | uttamaiṣā tu vijñeyā śukājīrṇanimittajā
commentary: The piḍakās which are like mudga and māṣa are red, and are due to vitiated rakta and pitta, should be known as uttamā. They are due to repeated use of śūka for a long time.

sanskrit_text: छिद्रैरणमखैर्वस्तु चितं यस्य समन्ततः। वातशोणितजो व्याधिर्वज्ञेयः शतपोनकः
transliteration: chidrairaṇamakhairvastu citaṃ yasya samantataḥ | vātaśoṇitajo vyādhirvajñeyaḥ śataponakaḥ
commentary: That disease in which there are multiple tiny openings alround the penis and which is due to vitiation of vāta and śoṇita, is known as śataponaka.

sanskrit_text: पित्तरक्तक्रतो जेयस्त्वक्पाको ज्वरदाहवान्। कृष्णै: स्फोटैः सरक्तैइच पिडकाभिइच पीडितम्। यस्य वास्तुरुजइचोग्रा ज्ञेयं तच्छोणितार्बुदम्
transliteration: pittaraktakrato jeyastvakpāko jvaradāhavān | kṛṣṇai: sphoṭaiḥ saraktaiica piḍakābhica pīḍitam | yasya vāsturujaicogrā jñeyaṃ tacchoṇitārbudam |
commentary: That should be known as tvakpāka which is due to vitiated pitta and rakta, and which produces fever and burning sensation. Those piḍakās which are associated with black and red blisters, and in which there is severe pain in the penis should be known as śoṇitārbuda.

sanskrit_text: मांसदोषेण जानीयादबुदं मांससंभवम्। हीर्यन्ते यस्य मांसानि यत्र सर्वाइच वेदनाः। विद्यात्तं मांसपार्क तु सर्वदोषकृतं भिषक्। यथोक्तमभिनिदिनोत्। सन्निपातेन विद्रधि
transliteration: māṃsadoṣeṇa jānīyādabudaṃ māṃsasaṃbhavam | hīryante yasya māṃsāni yatra sarvāica vedanāḥ | vidyāttaṃ māṃsapārka tu sarvadoṣakṛtaṃ bhiṣak | yathoktamabhinidinōt | sannipātena vidradhi
commentary: Māṁsārbuda should be known as being produced due to the vitiation of māṁsa. That in which muscles putrefy and there is pain of all types is known as māṁsapāka by the clinician; this is due to vitiation of all the doṣas. Vidradhi is due to a combination of all the doṣas together, and has already been described.

sanskrit_text: कृष्णानि चित्राण्यथवा शुकानि सविषाणि चे। पातितानि पचन्त्याहा मेढ़ं निरवशेषतः। कालानि भूत्वा मांसानि शीर्यन्ते यस्य देहिनः। सन्निपातसम्त्थानं तं विद्यात्तिलकालकम्
transliteration: kṛṣṇāni citrāṇyathavā śukāni saviṣāṇi ce | pātitāni pacantyāhā meḍhaṃ niravaśeṣataḥ | kālāni bhūtvā māṃsāni śīryante yasya dehinaḥ | sannipātasam tthānaṃ taṃ vidyāttilakālakam |
commentary: Tilakālaka is that condition which is due to vitiation of all the doṣas where black and mottled or poisonous śūkas being used putrefy the whole penis very quickly and the muscles become black and necrosed.

sanskrit_text: तत्र मांसार्बदं यच्च मांसपाकइच यः स्मृतः। विद्रधिश्च न सिध्यन्ति ये च स्युस्तिलकालकाः
transliteration: tatra māṃsārbadaṃ yacca māṃsapākica yaḥ smṛtaḥ | vidradhiśca na sidhyanti ye ca syustilakālakāḥ
commentary: Out of all these māṁsārbuda, māṁsapāka, vidradhi and tilakālaka are incurable.

sanskrit_text: अथातो भग्नानां निदानं व्याख्यास्यामः
transliteration: athāto bhagnānāṃ nidānaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ
commentary: Hereafter we would expound upon 'The Diagnosis of Fractures and Dislocations'.

sanskrit_text: यथोवाच भगवान धन्वन्तरिः
transliteration: yathovāca bhagavān dhanvantariḥ
commentary: As was described by Lord Dhanvantari.

sanskrit_text: पतनपोडनप्रहाराक्षेपणव्यालमृगदशनप्रभृतिभिरभिघातविशेषंरनेक- विधमस्थ्नां भङ्गमुपदिशन्ति
transliteration: patanapōḍanaprahārākṣepaṇavyālamṛgadaśanaprabhṛtibhirabhighātaviśeṣaṃraneka- vidhamasthnāṃ bhaṅgamupadiśanti
commentary: Fall, compression, blows, throwing and specific traumas from teeth etc, of ferocious or docile animals are mentioned to cause various types of bony injuries.

sanskrit_text: भङ्ग (ग्न) जातमनेकविधमनुसार्यमाणं द्विविधमेवोपपद्यते तत्त् में प्रार्थ का प्रार सन्धिमक्त, काण्डभग्नं च । तत्र षडिवधं सन्धिमक्त, द्वादशविधं काण्डभग्नं भवति
transliteration: bhaṅga (gna) jātamanekavidhamanusāryamāṇaṃ dvividhamevopapadyate tatt meṃ prārtha kā prāra sandhimakta, kāṇḍabhagnaṃ ca | tatra ṣaḍivadhaṃ sandhimakta, dvādaśavidhaṃ kāṇḍabhagnaṃ bhavati
commentary: Now, bony injuries produced by various means are conventionally classified into two groups only—dislocation of joints and breaking of bones (fractures). The dislocations are of six types and the fractures are of twelve types.

sanskrit_text: तत्र सन्धिमकतम—उत्पिष्टं, विइलष्टं, विर्वाततम, अवक्षातं, अतिक्षिप्तं, तिर्यक्षिप्तमिति षड्विधम्
transliteration: tatra sandhimakatama—utpiṣṭaṃ, viilaṣṭaṃ, virvātataṃ, avakṣātaṃ, atikṣiptaṃ, tiryakṣiptamiti ṣaḍvidham
commentary: The six types of dislocations are : 1. Utpiṣṭa — Fracture-Dislocation. 2. Viśliṣṭa — Subluxation. 3. Vivartita — Dislocation with lateral displacement. 4. Avakṣipta — Dislocation with downward displacement. 5. Atikṣipta — Dislocation with overriding. 6. Tiryakkṣipta — Dislocation with oblique displacement.

sanskrit_text: प्रसारणाकुञ्चनविवर्तनाक्षेपणाहाक्तिरुग्ररजत्वं स्पशासहत्वं तत्र चेति सामान्यं सन्धिमक्तलक्षणमुक्तम
transliteration: prasāraṇākuñcanavivartanākṣepaṇāhāktirugrarajatvaṃ spaśāsahatvaṃ tatra ceti sāmānyaṃ sandhimaktalakṣaṇamuktama
commentary: Inability of extension (and abduction), flexion and movement, circumduction or any movement, severe pain and hyperaesthesia, are the general clinical features of dislocations.

sanskrit_text: वैशेषिकं त्विष्टे सन्धावुभयतः शोफो वेदनाप्रादुर्भावो विशेषतःच नानाप्रकारा वेदना रात्रौ प्रादुर्भवन्ति; विशिलष्टेऽल्पः शोफो वेदना- सातत्यं सन्धिविक्रिया च ; विर्वातते तु सन्धिपार्श्वापगमनाद्विषमाङ्गता वेदना च; अवक्षिप्ते सन्धिविइलेषस्तीव्ररजत्वं च; अतिक्षिप्ते द्वयोः सन्ध्यस्थ्नोरतिक्रान्तता वेदना च; तिर्यक्षिप्ते त्वेकास्थिपाइर्वापगमन- मत्यर्थं वेदना चेति
transliteration: vaiśeṣikaṃ tviṣṭe sandhāvubhayataḥ śopho vedanāprādurbhāvo viśeṣataśca nānāprakārā vedanā rātrau prādurbhavanti; viśileṣṭe'lpaḥ śopho vedanā- sātatyaṃ sandhivikriyā ca ; virvātate tu sandhipārśvāpagamanādviṣamāṅgatā vedanā ca; avakṣipte sandhiviileṣastīvrarajatvaṃ ca; atikṣipte dvayoḥ sandhyasthnōratikrāntatā vedanā ca; tiryakṣipte tvekāsthipāirvāpagamanam- atyarthaṃ vedanā ceti
commentary: Specifically in the utpiṣṭa variety, swelling on both sides of the joint and pain occur; various types of pain specially occur in the nights. In viśliṣṭa type, slight swelling, persistent pain and derangement of the joint occurs. And, in the vivartita type of dislocation deformity and pain occur due to lateral displacement of the joint. In avakṣipta type of dislocation separation of the joint and severe pain occur. In atikṣipta type of dislocation there is pain and overriding of both bones of the joint. In tiryakkṣipta type of dislocation one of the bones gets obliquely displaced and excessive pain occurs.

sanskrit_text: च्चणितं, काण्डभग्नमत ऊर्धवं वक्ष्यामः—कर्कटकम, अइवकण, पिच्चितम्, अस्थिच्छल्लितं, काण्डभग्नं, मज्जानुगतम्, अतिपातितं, पाटितं, स्फुटितमिति द्वादशविधम्। छिन्मं, वक्रं,
transliteration: ccaṇitaṃ, kāṇḍabhagnamata ūrdhavaṃ vakṣyāmaḥ—karkaṭakama, aivakaṇa, piccitam, asthicchallitaṃ, kāṇḍabhagnaṃ, majjānugatam, atipātitaṃ, pāṭitaṃ, sphuṭitamiti dvādaśavidham | chinmaṃ, vakraṃ,
commentary: Now we would describe the fractures which are of twelve types : 1. Karkaṭaka — Fracture with hematoma, 2. Aśvakarṇa — Oblique fracture, 3. Cūrṇita — Comminuted fracture, 4. Piccita — Compression fracture, 5. Asthicchallita — Subperiosteal hematoma, 6. Kāṇḍabhagna — Transverse fracture, 7. Majjānugata — Impacted fracture, 8. Atipātita — Complete fracture, 9. Vakra — Greenstick fracture, 10. Chinna — Incomplete fracture, 11. Pāṭita — Cracked fracture, 12. Sphuṭita — Fissured fracture.

sanskrit_text: इवयथबाहुल्यं स्पन्दनविवर्तनस्पर्शासहिष्णुत्वमवपीडचमाने स्रस्ताड्वता विविधवेदनाप्रादुर्भावः सर्वास्ववस्थास न शर्मलाभ इति समासंन काण्डभग्नलक्षणम्वतम्
transliteration: ivayathabāhulyaṃ spandanavivartanasparśāsahiṣṇutvamavapīḍacamāne srastāḍvatā vividhavedanāprādurbhāvaḥ sarvāsvavasthāsa na śarmalābha iti samāsaṃna kāṇḍabhagnalakṣaṇamvatam |
commentary: Marked swelling, inability to bear movements or rotation and touch, crepitus on squeezing, looseness of the parts, appearance of various types of pain and no relief of pain in any posture, are briefly the general clinical features of fractures.

sanskrit_text: संमुढम्भयतोऽस्थिमध्ये भ(ल)ग्नं ग्रन्थिरिवोन्नतं विशेषस्त्र कर्कटकम्, अश्वकणवदुद्गतमश्वकणक, स्पृश्यमाने शब्वच्च्र्णणतमव- गच्छेत्, पिच्चितं पृथुतां गतमनल्पशोफं, पार्वयोरस्थि हीनोद्गतमस्थि- च्छलितं, वेल्लते प्रकस्पमानं काण्डभग्नम्, अस्थ्यवयवोऽस्थिमध्यमनु- प्रविश्य मज्जानमुन्नह्यतीति मज्जानुगतम्, अस्थि निःहोषतहिछन्नमति- पातितम्, आभुग्नमविमक्तास्थि वक्रम, अन्यतरपार्वविशिष्ट छिन्नं, शूकपूर्ण मिवाध्मातं विपूलं पाटितमणबहुविदारितं वेदनावच्च, विस्फुटितं स्फुटितमिति
transliteration: saṃmuḍhambhayato'stimadhye bha(la)gnaṃ granthirivonnataṃ viśeṣastra karkaṭakam, aśvakaṇavadudgatamaśvakaṇaka, spṛśyamāne śabvaccrṇaṇatamava- gacchet, piccitaṃ pṛthutāṃ gatamanalpaśophaṃ, pār vayorasthi hīnodgatamasthi- cchalitaṃ, vellate prakaspamānaṃ kāṇḍabhagnam, asthyavayavo'stimadhyamanu- praviśya majjānamunnahyatīti majjānugatam, asthi niḥhoṣatahichannamati- pātitam, ābhugnamavimaktāsthi vakra, anyatarapārvaviśiṣṭa chinnaṃ, śūkapūrṇa mivādhmātaṃ vipūlaṃ pāṭitamaṇabahuvidāritaṃ vedanāvacca, visphuṭitaṃ sphuṭitamiti
commentary: Specifically in karkaṭaka types there is loss of function on both sides of the fracture and in the centre it is raised like a gland (fracture hematoma). In aśvakarṇaka the fracture is raised like the ears of a horse. In cūrṇita type of fracture there is sound on palpation (crepitus). In piccita type of fracture there is flattening and marked swelling. In asthicch alita type of fracture the bones are slightly elevated on the sides. In kāṇḍabhagna the fracture moves on shaking. In majjānugata type of fracture, the bony spicules get impacted into the middle of the bone and let out the bone marrow. In atipātita type of fracture, the bone is completely broken. In vakra type of fracture the bones get bent, but not broken. In chinna type of fracture the other side remains unbroken, In pāṭita type of fracture many small cracks occur along with pain. In sphuṭita the fracture is swollen as if full of bristles and has multiple cracks.

sanskrit_text: र्च्रीणतच्छिन्नातिपातितमज्जानगतानि तेषु कृच्छसाध्यानि, क्वहावृद्धबालानां क्षतक्षीणकुष्ठिहवासिनां सन्ध्यूपगतं चेति
transliteration: r crīṇatacchinnātipātitamajjānagatāni teṣu kṛcchasādhyāni, kvahāvṛddhabālānāṃ kṣatakṣīṇakuṣṭhihavāsināṃ sandhyūpagataṃ ceti
commentary: Out of them cūrṇita, chinna, atipātita and majjānugata (types of fractures) are curable with difficulty, as are also those in the weak, the old and the children and in those suffering from consumption, emaciation, leprosy (and other skin diseases) and asthma and in those in whom the joint is also involved.

sanskrit_text: भ वन्ति चात्र--- भिन्न कपालं कटचां तु सन्धिम्वतं तथा च्य्तम्। जघनं प्रति पिष्टं च वर्जयेत्तच्चिकित्सकः। असंहिलष्ट कपालं तु ललाटे चूर्णितं च यत्। भग्नं स्तनान्तरे श्र्ड्वे पृष्ठे मूधिन च वर्जयेत्
transliteration: bha vanti cātra--- bhinna kapālaṃ kaṭacāṃ tu sandhimvataṃ tathā cytam | jaghanaṃ prati piṣṭaṃ ca varjayettaccikitsakaḥ | asaṃhilaṣṭa kapālaṃ tu lalāṭe cūrṇitaṃ ca yat | bhagnaṃ stanāntare śrḍve pṛṣṭhe mūdhina ca varjayet |
commentary: These verses have been quoted in this context. Fractures of the skull and waist as well as their dislocations and subluxation, as also, the crushing of the hip bones should be discarded from treatment by the physician. Separation of skull sutures, cūrṇita fractures of the forehead, and fractures in the intermammary region, temples, back and vertex should be discarded (from treatment).

sanskrit_text: सन्धिरथापि वा। आदितो यच्च द्रजतिमस्थि सम्यग्यमितमप्यस्थि दुर्न्यसाद्दुनिबन्धनात्। संक्षोभाद्वापि यद्गच्छेद्विक्रियां तच्त्र वर्जयेत्
transliteration: sandhirathāpi vā | ādito yacca drajatimasthi samyagyamitamapyasthi durnyasād dunibandhanāt | saṃkṣobhādvāpi yadgacchedvikriyāṃ tacca varjayet
commentary: The bones and joints which were abnormal even prior to injury or were so since birth, or those fractures which even though reduced properly, have become complicated due to improper immobilisation and bandaging or due to movements should be discarded from treatment.

topic_heading: Healing of Fractures at Different Ages
sanskrit_text: मध्यस्य वयसोऽवस्थास्तिस्रो याः परिकीतिताः। तत्र स्थिरो भवेज्जन्तुरुपऋान्तो विजानता
transliteration: madhyasya vayaso'vasthāstisro yāḥ parikītitāḥ | tatra sthiro bhavejjanturupaṛānto vijānatā
commentary: If treated by the expert clinician the fractures become stable after proper treatment in the middle one of three age groups as described (elsewhere).

topic_heading: Types of Fractures in Different Bones
sanskrit_text: तरुणास्थीनि नम्यन्ते भज्यन्ते नलकानि तु। कपालानि विभिद्यन्ते स्फ़टन्ति रुचकानि च
transliteration: taruṇāsthīni namyante bhajyante nalakāni tu | kapālāni vibhidyante sphaṭanti rucakāni ca
commentary: The cartilaginous bones bend, the tubular bones break, the flat bones get fissured and the small bones get cracked.

sanskrit_text: अथातो मुखरोगाणां निदानं व्याख्यास्यामः
transliteration: athāto mukharogāṇāṃ nidānaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ
commentary: Now we would expound upon 'The Diagnosis of Oral Diseases'.

sanskrit_text: यथोवाच भगवान् धन्वन्तरिः
transliteration: yathovāca bhagavān dhanvantariḥ
commentary: As was described by Lord Dhanvantari.

sanskrit_text: मुखरोगाः पञ्चषष्टिर्भवन्ति सप्तस्वायतनेषु । तत्रायतनानि—ओष्टौ, दन्तमूलानि, दन्ताः, जिह् वा, तालु, कण्ठः, सर्वाणि चेति। तत्राष्टावो- ष्ठयोः, पञ्चदश दन्तमूलेषु, अष्टौ दन्तेषु, पञ्च जिह्वायां, नव तालुनि, सप्तदश कण्ठे, त्रयः सर्वेष्वायतनेष्
transliteration: mukharogāḥ pañcāṣaṣṭir bhavanti saptasvāyataneṣu | tatrāyatanāni—oṣṭau, dantamūlāni, dantāḥ, jihvā, tālu, kaṇṭhaḥ, sarvāṇi ceti | tatrāṣṭāvo- ṣṭhayoḥ, pañcadaśa dantamūleṣu, aṣṭau danteṣu, pañca jihvāyāṃ, nava tāluni, saptadaśa kaṇṭhe, trayaḥ sarveṣvāyataneṣ |
commentary: The diseases of oral cavity are sixty-five (in number) and they occur at seven sites. These sites are : the lips, gums, teeth, tongue, palate, throat, and the whole oral cavity. There are eight diseases of the lips, fifteen of the gums, eight of the teeth, five of the tongue, nine of the palate, seventeen of the throat and three affecting the whole oral cavity.

sanskrit_text: तत्रौष्ठप्रकोपा वातपित्तइलेष्मसन्निपातरवतमांसमेदोभिघात- निमित्ताः
transliteration: tatrāuṣṭhaprakopā vātapittail eṣmasannipātaravatamāṃsamedobhighāta- nimittāḥ
commentary: The diseases of lips are due to vāta, pitta, kapha seperately and together, śoṇita, māṁsa, medas and trauma.

topic_heading: Diseases of Lips due to Vāta
sanskrit_text: कर्कशौ परुषौ स्तब्धौ कृष्णौ तीव्रहगन्वितौ। दाल्येते परिपाटचेते हचाष्ठौ मारुतकापतः
transliteration: karkaśau paruṣau stabdhau kṛṣṇau tīvrahaganvitau | dālyete paripāṭacete hacāṣṭhau mārutakāpataḥ
commentary: The lips afflicted by vāta are rough, hard, rigid, black, acutely painful and have cracks and fissures.

topic_heading: Diseases of Lips due to Pitta
sanskrit_text: आचितौ पिडकाभिस्तु सर्षपाकृतिभिर्भ शम्। सदाहपाकसंस्नावौ नीलौ पीतौ च पित्ततः
transliteration: ācitau piḍakābhistsu sarṣapākṛtibhir bha śam | sadāhapākasaṃsnāvau nīlau pītau ca pittataḥ
commentary: The lips afflicted by pitta are full of mustard like furuncles leading quickly to burning, suppuration and discharge and they appear blue or yellow.

topic_heading: Diseases of Lips due to Kapha
sanskrit_text: सवर्णाभिस्तु चीयेते पिडकाभिरवेदनौ। कण्डूमन्तौ कफाच्छूनौ पिच्छिलौ शीतलौ ग्रू
transliteration: savarṇābhistu cīyete piḍakābhiravedanau | kaṇḍūmantau kaphācchūnau picchilau śītalau grū
commentary: The lips afflicted by (vitiated) kapha are painless and are associated with vesicles having the same colour (as that of lips), have itching and oedema, and are slimy, cold and heavy.

topic_heading: Diseases of Lips due to the Three Doṣas together
sanskrit_text: सकृत् कृष्णौ सकृत् पीतौ सकृच्छवेतौ तथैव च। सन्निपातेन विज्ञेयावनेकपिडिकाचितौ
transliteration: sakṛt kṛṣṇau sakṛt pītau sakṛcchavetau tathaiva ca | sannipātena vijñeyāvanekapiḍikācitau
commentary: The lips afflicted by all the three doṣas together are known by their being sometimes black, sometimes yellow and sometimes white and by their having vesicles of many types.

topic_heading: Diseases of Lips due to Śoṇita
sanskrit_text: खर्जूरफलवर्णाभिः पिडकाभिः समाचितौ। रक्तापसूष्टौ रुधिरं स्रवतः शोणितप्रभौ
transliteration: kharjūraphalavarṇābhiḥ piḍakābhiḥ samācitau | raktāpasūṣṭau rudhiraṃ sravataḥ śoṇitaprabhau
commentary: The lips afflicted by śoṇita have a bloody discharge, shine like blood and are associated with vesicles of the colour of date fruit.

topic_heading: Diseases of Lips due to vitiated Māṁsa
sanskrit_text: मांसद्रष्टौ ग़रू स्थलौ मांसपिण्डवदुद्गतौ। जन्तवइचात्र मूर्च्छन्ति सृककस्योभयतो मुखात्
transliteration: māṃsadraṣṭau ga rū sthalau māṃsapiṇḍavadudgatau | jantavaicātra mūrcchanti sṛkakasyobhayato mukhāt
commentary: The lips afflicted by vitiated māṁsa are heavy, thick, and raised like muscular lumps and maggots appear at both the angles of the mouth.

topic_heading: Diseases of Lips due to vitiated Medas
sanskrit_text: मेदसा घतमण्डाभौ कण्डूमन्तौ स्थिरौ मुद्दु। अच्छ स्फटिकसड्राशमास्रावं स्रवतो गुरू
transliteration: medasā ghatamaṇḍābhau kaṇḍūmantau sthirau muddu | accha sphaṭikasaḍrāśamāsrāvaṃ sravato gurū
commentary: The lips afflicted by vitiated meda are like the clear upper layers of ghṛta, have itching, are fixed, soft, and heavy with a colourless crystal like discharge.

topic_heading: Diseases of Lips due to Chronic Trauma
sanskrit_text: क्षतजाभौ विदीयेंते पाटचेते चाभिघाततः। ग्रथिती च समाख्यातावोष्ठौ कण्डसमन्वितौ
transliteration: kṣatajābhau vidīyeṃte pāṭacete cābhighātataḥ | grathitī ca samākhyātāvoṣṭhau kaṇḍasamanvitau
commentary: The lips afflicted by trauma are bloody red in colour, have cracks and fissures, have knotty swellings and are associated with itching.

sanskrit_text: दन्तमूलगतास्तु— शीतादो, दन्तपुप्पुटको, दन्तवेष्टकः, शौषिरो, महाशौषिरः, परिदर, उपकुशो, दन्तवैदर्भो, वर्धनः, अधिमांसो, नाड्यः प पञ्चेति
transliteration: dantamūlagatāstu— śītādo, dantapuppuṭako, dantaveṣṭakaḥ, śauṣiro, mahāśauṣiraḥ, paridara, upakuśo, dantavaidarbho, vardhanaḥ, adhimāṃso, nāḍyaḥ pa pañceti
commentary: The diseases of the gums are—Śītāda, dantapuppuṭaka, dantaveṣṭaka, śauṣira, mahāśauṣira, paridara, upakuśa, dantavaidarbha, vardhana, adhimāṁsa, and the five types of sinuses.

sanskrit_text: हाोणितं दन्तवेष्टेभ्यो यस्याकस्मात' प्रवर्तते। दुर्गन्धीनि सकृष्णानि प्रक्लेदीनि मृद्रुनि च। दन्तमांसानि शीर्यन्ते पचन्ति च परस्परम्। शीतादो नाम स व्याधिः कफशोणितसंभवः
transliteration: hāoṇitaṃ dantaveṣṭebhyo yasyākas māta' pravartate | durgandhīni sakṛṣṇāni prakl edīni mṛdruni ca | dantamāṃsāni śīryante pacanti ca parasparam | śītādo nāma sa vyādhiḥ kaphaśoṇitasaṃbhavaḥ
commentary: That disease in which there is sudden bleeding from the gums, in which foul smelling, black, soft and sodden gums get necrosed and start receding is called śītāda. It is produced by kapha and śoṇita.

sanskrit_text: दन्तयोस्त्रिष् वा यस्य इवयथः सरुजो महान्। दन्तपुप्पुटको ज्ञेयः कफरक्तनिमित्तजः
transliteration: dantayostriṣ vā yasya ivayathaḥ sarujo mahān | dantapuppuṭako jñeyaḥ kapharaktanimittajaḥ
commentary: That disease, in which there is a painful, big inflammatory swelling in two or three teeth together should be known as dantapuppuṭaka and is due to kapha and rakta.

sanskrit_text: स्रवन्ति प्रयरुधिरं चला दन्ता भवन्ति च। दन्तवेष्टः स विज्ञेयो द्रष्टशोणितसंभवः
transliteration: sravanti prayarudhiraṃ calā dantā bhavanti ca | dantaveṣṭaḥ sa vijñeyo draṣṭaśoṇitasaṃbhavaḥ
commentary: That disease in which pus and blood are discharged and teeth become loose, should be known as dantaveṣṭa and is produced by vitiated śoṇita.

sanskrit_text: हवयथर्दन्तमलेष् रुजावान् कफरवतजः। लालास्रावी स विज्ञेयः कण्डमाज् शौषिरो गदः
transliteration: havayathardantama leṣ rujāvān kapharavatajaḥ | lālāsrāvī sa vijñeyaḥ kaṇḍamāj śauṣiro gadaḥ
commentary: That disease in which there is swelling at the roots of teeth, which is painful, has excessive salivation and has itching should be known as śauṣira and is due to kapha and rakta.

sanskrit_text: दन्ताइचलन्ति वेष्टेभ्यस्ताल चाप्यवदीर्यते। दन्तमांसानि पच्यन्ते मुखं च परिपीडचते। यस्मिन् स सर्वजो व्याधिर्महाशौषिरसंज्ञकः। दन्तमांसानि शीर्यन्ते यस्मिन् ष्ठीवति चाप्यसुक्। पित्तासक्कफजो व्याधिर्ज्ञेयः परिदरो हि सः
transliteration: dantāicalanti veṣṭebhyastāla cāpyavadīryate | dantamāṃsāni pacyante mukhaṃ ca paripīḍacate | yasmin sa sarvajo vyādhir mahāśauṣirasaṃjñakaḥ | dantamāṃsāni śīryante yasmin ṣṭhīvati cāpyasuk | pittāsakkaphajo vyādhirjñeyaḥ paridaro hi saḥ
commentary: That disease in which the teeth become loose from their sockets, there is tearing of the palate, suppuration of gums, and pain in the mouth is called mahāśauṣira and is due to vitiation of all the three doṣas together. That disease in which the gums decay and blood comes on spitting, is known as paridara and is due to pitta, blood and kapha.

sanskrit_text: वेष्टेष् दाहः पाकइच तेभ्यो दन्ताइचलन्ति च। आघट्टिताः प्रस्त्रवन्ति शोणितं मन्दवेदनाः। आध्मायन्ते स्नुते रवते मुख पूति च जायते। यस्मिन्नु पकुशः स स्यात् पित्तरक्तक्टतो गदः। घट्टेष दन्तमलेष संरस्भो जायते महान्। भवन्ति च चला दन्ताः स वैदर्भोऽभिघातजः
transliteration: veṣṭeṣ dāhaḥ pākaica tebhyo dantāicalanti ca | āghaṭṭitāḥ prastravanti śoṇitaṃ mandavedanāḥ | ādhmāyante snute ravate mukha pūti ca jāyate | yasminnu pakuśaḥ sa syāt pittaraktakṭato gadaḥ | ghaṭṭeṣa dantama leṣa saṃrasbho jāyate mahān | bhavanti ca calā dantā sa vaidarbho'bhighātajaḥ
commentary: That disease, in which there is burning sensation and inflammation in the gums, the teeth become loose, there is bleeding with mild pain on moving them and swelling occurs after discharge of blood and there is foetid odour in the mouth, is known as upakuśa and is due to pitta and rakta. That disease, in which severe oedema is produced upon rubbing the roots of teeth, and the teeth become loose, is called vaidarbha and is due to trauma.

sanskrit_text: मारुतेनाधिको दन्तो जायते तीव्रवेदनः। वर्धनः स मतो व्याधिर्जाते रुक् च प्रशाम्यति। हानव्ये पइिवमे दन्ते महाञ्छोथो महारुजः। लालास्रावी कफक्वतो विज्ञेयः सोऽधिमांसकः। दन्तमूलगता नाडचः पञ्च ज्ञेया यथेरिताः
transliteration: mā rutenādhiko danto jāyate tīvravedanaḥ | vardhanaḥ sa mato vyādhirjāte ruk ca praśāmyati | hānavye paiivame dante mahāñchotho mahārujaḥ | lālāsrāvī kaphakvato vijñeyaḥ so'dhimāṃsakaḥ | dantamūlagatā nāḍacaḥ pañca jñeyā yatheritāḥ |
commentary: That disease, in which the supernumerary tooth is produced by vāta and is severely painful, is known as vardhana and the pain subsides upon eruption. That disease, in which there is severe inflammation, intense pain in the jaw behind the last tooth, and salivation is known as adhimāṁsa and is due to kapha. As described (earlier) five types of sinuses are known to occur in the roots of teeth.

sanskrit_text: क्रोमदन्तको, भडजनक:, दन्तहषा, दन्तगतास्तु—दालन:, दन्तशर्करा, कपालिका, इयावदन्तको, हनुमोक्षइचेति
transliteration: kromadantako, bhaḍajanaka:, dantahaṣā, dantagatāstu—dālana:, dantaśarkarā, kapālikā, iyāvadantako, hanumokṣaiceti
commentary: Diseases of the teeth are : dālana, kṛmidantaka, dantaharṣa, bhañjanaka, dantaśarkarā, kapālikā, śyāvadantaka and hanumokṣa.

sanskrit_text: दाल्यन्ते बहधा दन्ता योस्मस्तीव्ररुगन्विताः। दालनः स इति ज्ञेयः सदागतिनिमित्तजः
