transliteration: dālyante bahadhā dantā yos mastīvraruganvitāḥ | dālanaḥ sa iti jñeyaḥ sadāgatinimittajaḥ
commentary: That disease in which many teeth get cracked and in which severe pain is produced, is known as dālana and is known to be due to vāta.

sanskrit_text: कृcणइिछद्री चलः स्रावी संरम्भो महारु जः। अनिमित्तरुजो वाताद्विज्ञेयः क्टमिदन्तकः
transliteration: kṛcṇa iichadrī calaḥ srāvī saṃrambho mahāru jaḥ | animittarujo vātādvijñeyaḥ kṭamidantakaḥ
commentary: That disease in which the teeth have black colour, have cavities and become loose, have a discharge, swelling and bouts of severe pain without any apparent cause, should be known as kṛmidanta and is due to vāta.

sanskrit_text: शोतमुष्णं च दशनाः सहन्ते स्पर्शनं न च। यस्य तं इन्तहर्ष त्र व्याधि विद्यात समीरणात
transliteration: śotamuṣṇaṃ ca daśanāḥ sahante sparśanaṃ na ca | yasya taṃ intaharṣa tra vyādhi vidyāta samīraṇāta
commentary: That disease in which the teeth are unable to bear the touch of cold or hot,is known as dantaharṣa and is due to vāta.

sanskrit_text: वक्त्रं वऋं भवेद्यस्मिन दन्तभड़ुर्रच तोव्ररुक्। कफवातक्रतो व्याधिः स भञ जनकसंज्ञितः
transliteration: vaktraṃ vaṛṃ bhavedyasmin dantabhaḍurraca tōvraruk | kaphavātakrato vyādhiḥ sa bhañ janakasaṃjñitaḥ
commentary: That disease in which the mouth becomes distorted and there is fracture of teeth alongwith severe pain is called bhañjanaka and is due to kapha and vāta.

sanskrit_text: र्दार्करेव स्थिरीभतो मलो दन्तेष यस्य वै। सा दन्तानां ग़णहरी विज्ञेया दन्तशर्करा
transliteration: rdārkareva sthirībhato malo danteṣa yasya vai | sā dantānāṃ gaṇaharī vijñeyā dantaśarkarā
commentary: That disease in which tartar gets deposited on the teeth like gravel, and which destroys the qualities of the teeth should be known as dantaśarkarā.

sanskrit_text: दलन्ति दन्तवल्कानि यदा शर्करया सह। ज़ेया कपालिका सैव दहानानां विनाशिनी
transliteration: dalanti dantavalkāni yadā śarkarayā saha | zeyā kapālikā saiva dahānānāṃ vināśinī
commentary: That disease, in which enamel of the teeth alongwith gravel gets cracked, is known as kapālikā and this destroys the teeth.

sanskrit_text: योऽसङ्मिश्रेण पित्तेन दग्धो दन्तस्त्वशेषतः। हयावतां नीलतां वाऽपि गतः स इयावदन्तकः
transliteration: yo'saṅmiśreṇa pittena dagdho dantastvaśeṣataḥ | hayāvatāṃ nīlatāṃ vā'pi gataḥ sa iyāvadantakaḥ
commentary: That disease, in which the teeth gets charred due to mixed action of śoṇita and pitta and which become blackish or blue is known as śyāvadantaka.

sanskrit_text: वातेन तैस्तैर्भावैस्तु हनुसन्धिविसंहतः। हनुमोक्ष इति ज्ञेयो व्याधिर्रदितलक्षणः
transliteration: vātena taistairbhāvaistu hanusandhivisaṃhataḥ | hanumokṣa iti jñeyo vyādhirraditalakṣaṇaḥ
commentary: That disease in which the mandibular joint becomes dislocated due to vāta aggravated by its various causes is known as hanumokṣa and has the features of ardita disease.

sanskrit_text: जिह्वागतास्त्र—कण्टकास्त्रिविधास्त्रिभिर्दोषै:, अलास, उपजिह्विका चेति
transliteration: jihvāgatāstra—kaṇṭakāstridhāstribhir doṣai:, alāsa, upajihvikā ceti
commentary: Diseases of the tongue are : the three types of kantakas caused by the three doṣas, alāsa, and upajihvikā.

sanskrit_text: जिह्वाऽनिलेन स्फटिता प्रस्प्ता भवेच्च शाकच्छनदप्रकाशा। पित्तेन पीता परिदहचते च चिता सरक्तैरपि कप्टकैइच। कफेन ग्र्वी बहला चिता च मांसोद्गमैः शाल्मलिकण्टकाभैः
transliteration: jihvā'nilena sphaṭitā prasptā bhavecca śākacchanadaprakāśā | pittena pītā paridahacate ca citā saraktairapi kapṭakaica | kaphena grvī bahalā citā ca māṃsōdgamaiḥ śālmalikaṇṭakābhaiḥ |
commentary: The tongue vitiated by vāta becomes furred, loss of sensation occurs and it is rough like the leaf of śāka tree. The tongue vitiated by pitta becomes yellow, has burning sensation and is full of bloody thorns. The tongue vitiated by kapha becomes heavy, thick and is full of muscular papillae like thorns of śālmalī.

sanskrit_text: जिह्वातले यः इवयथः प्रगाढः सोऽलाससंज्ञः कफरक्तर्मुतः। जिह्वां स तु स्तम्भयति प्रवृद्धो मूले तु जिह् वा भृशमेति पाकम्
transliteration: jihvātale yaḥ ivayathaḥ pragāḍhaḥ so'lāsasaṃjñaḥ kapharaktarmutaḥ | jihvāṃ sa tu stambhayati pravṛddho mūle tu jihvā bhṛśameti pākam |
commentary: That disease which causes an indurated swelling on the undersurface of the tongue is called alāsa and is due to (vitiated) kapha and rakta. When fully developed it fixes the tongue and causes severe inflammation at the root of the tongue.

sanskrit_text: जिह्वाग्ररूप: इवयथहि जिह्वामन्नम्य जातः कफरक्तयोनिः। प्रसंककण्डूपरिदाहयुक्ता प्रकथ्यतेऽसावुपजिह्विकेति
transliteration: jihvāgrarūpa: ivayathahi jihvāmannamya jātaḥ kapharaktayoniḥ | prasaṃkakaṇḍūparidāhayuktā prakathyate'sāvupajihviketi
commentary: That disease, in which the swelling is shaped like the tip of the tongue, which by being underneath it raises the tongue, and is associated with salivation, itching and burning sensation, is called upajihvikā and this is caused by (vitiated) kapha and rakta.

sanskrit_text: अबंद, तालगतास्तु—गलहाण्डिका, तुण्डिकेरी, अध्रषः, कच्छपः, मांससङ्कातः, तालुपुप्पुट:, तालुशोष:, तालुपाक इति
transliteration: abaṃda, tālagatāstu—galahāṇḍikā, tuṇḍikerī, adhraṣaḥ, kacchapaḥ, māṃsasaṅkātaḥ, tālupuppuṭa:, tāluśoṣa:, tālupāka iti
commentary: Diseases of the palate are : galaśuṇḍikā, tuṇḍikerī, adhruṣa, kacchapa, arbuda, māṁsasaṅghāta, tāluþuþþuṭa, tāluśoṣa and tālupāka.

sanskrit_text: इलेष्मासुग्भ्यां तालुमुलात् प्रवृद्धो दीर्घः शोफो ध्मातबस्तिप्रकाशः। तष्णाकासश्वासकृत संप्रदिष्टो व्याधिवैद्यः कण्ठइाण्डोतिनाम्ना
transliteration: ileṣmāsugbhyāṃ tālumulāt pravṛddho dīrghaḥ śopho dhmātabastiprakāśaḥ | taṣṇākāsaśvāsakṛta saṃpradiṣṭo vyādhivaidyaḥ kaṇṭhaiāṇḍotināmnā
commentary: That disease, which is caused by (vitiated) kapha and rakta, which spreads from the base of the palate, produces an oblong swelling, and looks like a distended bladder, and is further complicated by thirst, cough and dyspnoea, is named kaṇṭhaśuṇḍī by the clinicians.

sanskrit_text: शोफ: स्थूलस्तोददाहप्रपाकी प्रागक्ताभ्यां त्वण्डिकेरी मता तू। शोफ: स्तब्धो लोहितस्ताल्देशो रक्ताज्जेयः सोऽध्रुषो रुग्ज्वराढचः
transliteration: śopha: sthūlastodadāhaprapākī prāgaktābhyāṃ tvaṇḍikerī matā tū | śopha: stabdho lohitastāldeśo raktājjeyaḥ so'dhruṣo rugjvarāḍhacaḥ |
commentary: That disease in which there is oedema, increase in size (of the palate), pricking pain, burning sensation and suppuration is called tuṇḍikerī and is due to the above mentioned two (kapha and rakta). That disease, in which there is oedema, fixity and redness in the region of the palate alongwith pain and fever, is called adhruṣa and is due to rakta.

sanskrit_text: कर्मोत्सन्नोऽवेदनोऽशीघाजन्माऽरक्तो ज्ञेयः कच्छपः इलेष्मणा स्यात्। पद्माकारं तालुमध्ये तु शोफं विद्याद्रक्तादर्बुदं प्रोक्तलिङ्मम्
transliteration: karmōtsanno'vedano'śīghājanmā'rakto jñeyaḥ kacchapaḥ ileṣmaṇā syāt | padmākāraṃ tālumadhye tu śophaṃ vidyādraktā darbudaṃ proktaliṅmam |
commentary: That (swelling) which is raised like a tortoise, is painless, takes a longtime to arise and is not reddish is called kacchapa; it is due to (vitiated) kapha. That swelling which is of the shape of a lotus, is in the middle of the palate, and has aforesaid features of raktārbuda is called arbuda.

sanskrit_text: द्रष्ट मांसं इलेष्मणा नीरुजं च ताल्वनःस्थं मांससङ्कातमाह्वः। नीरुक् स्थायी कोलमात्रः कफात् स्यान्मेदोयुक्तात् पुप्पुटस्तालुदेशो। शोषोऽत्यर्थ दीर्यते चापि तालुः इवासो वातात्तालुशोषः सपित्तात्। पित्तं कुर्यात् पाकमन्यर्थघोरं तालन्येनं तालपाकं वदन्ति
transliteration: draṣṭa māṃsaṃ ileṣmaṇā nīrujaṃ ca tālvanaḥsthaṃ māṃsasaṅkātamāhvaḥ | nīruk sthāyī kolamātraḥ kaphāt syānmedoyuktāt puppuṭastāludeśo | śoṣo'tyartha dīryate cāpi tāluḥ ivāso vātāttāluśoṣaḥ sapittāt | pittaṃ kuryāt pākamanyarthaghoraṃ tālan yenaṃ tālapākaṃ vadanti |
commentary: That disease in which muscles inside the palate get vitiated and which is painless, is called māṁsasaṅghāta and is due to (vitiated) kapha. That swelling in the region of the palate which is painless, fixed, is of the size of a plum is tālapuppuṭa and is due the kapha alongwith meda. That disease in which there is excessive dryness, cracks in the palate and dyspnoea is called tāluśoṣa and is due to (vitiated) vāta alongwith pitta. Pitta causes excessively severe suppuration in the palate, and this is called tālupāka.

sanskrit_text: कण्ठगतास्तु—रोहिण्यः पञ्च, कण्ठशालूकम्, अधिजिह्वो, वलयों, गलविद्रधिः, गलौघः, बलास, एकवृन्दी, वन्दः, शतघ्नी, गिलायः, स्वरघनो, मांसतानो, विदारी चेति
transliteration: kaṇṭhagatāstu—rohiṇyaḥ pañca, kaṇṭhaśālūkam, adhijihvo, valayoṃ, galavidradhiḥ, galaughaḥ, balāsa, ekavṛndī, vandaḥ, śataghnī, gilāyaḥ, svaraghano, māṃsatāno, vidārī ceti
commentary: Diseases of the throat are : Five types of rohiṇī, kaṇṭhaśālūka, adhijihvā, valaya, balāsa, ekavṛnda, vrnda, śataghnī, gilāyu, galavidradhi, galaugha, svaraghna, māṁsatāna, and vidārī.

sanskrit_text: गलडनिलः पित्तकफौ च मच्छितौ प्थक् समस्ताइच तथैव शोणितम। प्रदूष्य मांसं गलरोधिनोऽङकूरान सूजन्ति यान् साऽसुहरा हि रोहिणी
transliteration: galaḍanilaḥ pittakaphau ca macchitau pthak samastāica tathaiva śoṇitama | pradūṣya māṃsaṃ galarodhino'ṅkūrān sūjanti yān sā'suharā hi rohiṇī
commentary: The fatal disease, in which the throat is affected by (vitiated) vāta, pitta and kapha separately or all together and also by śoṇita which vitiate the muscular tissue and produce buds which obstruct the throat, is called rohiṇī.

sanskrit_text: जिह्वां समन्ताद्भंशवेदना ये मांसाङकुराः कण्ठनिरोधिनः स्यः। तां रोहिणीं वातक्रतां वदन्ति वातात्मकोपद्रवगाढयक्ताम्। क्षिप्रोद्गमा क्षिप्रविदाहपाका तीव्रज्वरा पित्तनिमित्तजा स्यात्। स्रोतोनिरोधिन्यपि मन्दपाका गुर्वी स्थिरा सा कफसंभवा वै। गम्भीरपाकाऽप्रतिवारवीर्या त्रिदोषलिङ्ज़ग त्रयसंभवा स्यात्। स्फोटाचिता पित्तसमानलिङ्गऽसाध्या प्रदिष्टा रुधिरात्मिकेयम्
transliteration: jihvāṃ samantādbhaṃśavedanā ye māṃsāṅakurāḥ kaṇṭhanirodhinaḥ syaḥ | tāṃ rohiṇīṃ vātakratāṃ vadanti vātātmakopadravagāḍhayaktām | kṣiprōdgamā kṣipravidāhapākā tīvrajvarā pittanimittajā syāt | srōtōnirodhinyapi mandapākā gurvī sthirā sā kaphasaṃbhavā vai | gambhīrapākā'prativāravīryā tridoṣaliṅzga trayasaṃbhavā syāt | sphoṭācitā pittasamānāliṅga'sādhyā pradiṣṭā rudhirātmikeyam |
commentary: That disease, in which the muscular buds are present alround the tongue, which are extremely painful and which obstruct the throat is called rohiṇī due to the action of vāta, this is accompanied with severe complications of vāta. That rohiṇī, in which (muscular buds) appear quickly and soon produce burning pain and suppuration and are accompanied with high fever is known to be due to pitta; that in which the channels get obstructed, which is mildly suppurating, heavy and localized is due to kapha. That rohiṇī, which has deep seated suppuration, which is uncontrollable by all measures and which has the features of all the doṣas, is due to all the three doṣas together; that which is full of blisters, has features like those of pitta and is incurable, is due to śoṇita.

sanskrit_text: कोलास्थिमात्रः कफसंभवो यो ग्रन्थिर्गले कण्टकइाकभ्तः। खरः स्थिरः शस्त्रनिपातसाध्यस्तं कण्ठशालूकमिति ब्रुवन्ति
transliteration: kolāsthimātraḥ kaphasaṃbhavo yo granthirgale kaṇṭaka iākabhtaḥ | kharaḥ sthiraḥ śastranipātasādhyastaṃ kaṇṭhaśālūkamiti bruvanti
commentary: That disease in which glandular swelling of the size of a plumseed occurs in the throat, has pain like that of a thorn or bristle, and which is rough, localized and curable by surgical measures only, is called kaṇṭhaśālūka and this is due to kapha.

sanskrit_text: जिह्वाप्ररूपः जेयोऽधिजिह्वः खल्ट रोग एष विवर्जेयेदागतपाकर्मनेम्
transliteration: jihvāprarūpaḥ jeyo'dhijihvaḥ khalṭa roga eṣa vivarjeyedāgatapākarmanem
commentary: That disease in which swelling of the shape of the tip of the tongue occurs at the base of the tongue due to kapha alongwith śoṇita should be known as adhijihvā. It should be discarded (from treatment) when it undergoes suppuration.

sanskrit_text: बलास एवायतमुन्नतं च शोफं करोत्यन्नगतिं निवार्य। तं सर्वथैवाप्रतिवारवीयँ विवर्जनीयं वलयं वदन्ति
transliteration: balāsa evāyatamunnataṃ ca śophaṃ karotyannagatiṃ nivārya | taṃ sarvathaivāprativāravīyaṃ vivarjanīyaṃ valayaṃ vadanti
commentary: That disease, which is due to kapha and which produces diffuse and raised swelling, which obstructs the passage of food and which is uncontrollable is called valaya and should be discarded (from treatment).

sanskrit_text: गले तु शोफं कुरुतः प्रवद्धौ इलेष्मानिलौ इवासरुजोपपन्नम्। मर्मच्छिदं द्रस्तरमेतदाहुर्बलाससंज्ञं निप्रणा विकारम्
transliteration: gale tu śophaṃ kurutaḥ pravaddhau ileṣmānilau ivāsarujopapannam | marmacchidaṃ drastarametadāhurbalāsasaṃjñaṃ nipraṇā vikāram |
commentary: That disease in which the vitiated kapha and vāta cause inflammation in the throat, and produce dyspnoea and pain, which also injures the vital spots and is treatable with great difficulty is called by the name of balāsa by the wise.

sanskrit_text: वत्तोन्नतो यः इवयथः सदाहः कण्डवन्वितोऽपाक्यमुदुर्गुर्रुइच। नाम्नैकवन्दः परिकीतितोऽसौ व्याधिर्बलासक्षतजप्रसूतः। समन्नतं वत्तममन्ददाहं तीव्रज्वरं वन्दमदाहरन्ति। तं चापि पित्तक्षतजप्रकोपाद्विद्यात् सतोदं पवनास्रजं त्र। र्वतिर्घना क्रण्ठनिरोधिनी या चिताऽतिमात्रं पिशितप्ररोहैः। नानारुजोच्छ्ायकरी त्रिदोषाज्जेया शतघ्नीव शतघ्न्यसाध्या
transliteration: vattōnnato yaḥ ivayathaḥ sadāhaḥ kaṇḍavanvito'pākyamudurgurruica | nāmnaikavandaḥ parikītito'sau vyādhirbalāsakṣatajaprasūtaḥ | samannataṃ vattamamandadāhaṃ tīvrajvaraṃ vandamadāharanti | taṃ cāpi pittakṣatajaprakopādvidyāt satodaṃ pavanāsrajaṃ tra | rvatirghanā kraṇṭhanirodhinī yā citā'timātraṃ piśitaprarohaiḥ | nānārujocchāyakārī tridoṣājjeyā śataghnīva śataghn yasādhyā |
commentary: That disease, in which raised and circular inflammation alongwith burning sensation is produced, which is associated with itching, is non-suppurating, and is hard and heavy, is known by the name of ekavṛnda and is caused by kapha and śoṇita. That disease, in which there is raised and circular swelling with severe burning sensation, and high fever is known as vṛnda, and that should be known to be caused due to vitiation of pitta and śoṇita. If pricking pain is present it is due to vāta and śoṇita. That disease in which a thick wick like swelling obstructs the throat, which is full of numerous muscular buds, which produces various types of pain, and is shaped like a śataghnī (weapon) is called śataghnī; this is due to all the three doṣas together and is incurable.

sanskrit_text: ग्रन्थिर्गले त्वामलकास्थिमात्रः स्थिरोऽल्परुक्स्यात् कफरक्तमोंतः। संलक्ष्यते सक्तमिवाहानं च स शस्त्रसाध्यस्तु गिलायुसंज्ञः
transliteration: granthirgale tvāmalakāsthimātraḥ sthiro'lparuk syāt kap haraktamoṃtaḥ | saṃlakṣyate saktamivāhānaṃ ca sa śastrasādhyastu gilāyusaṃjñaḥ
commentary: That glandular swelling in the throat, which is of the size of a seed of āmlaka, which is localised, has mild pain and is due to kapha and rakta, which feels like an obstructed bolus and is curable by surgery only, is called gilāyu.

topic_heading: Galavidradhi, Galaugha, Svaraghna, Māṁsatāna and Vidārī
sanskrit_text: सर्व गलं व्याप्य समृत्थितो यः शोफो रुजो यत्र च सन्ति सर्वाः। सर्वदोषो गलविद्रधिस्त्र स तस्येव तुल्यः खलु सवंजस्य। शोफो महानन्नजलावरोधी तीव्रज्वरो वातगर्तोनहन्ता। कफेन जातो रुधिरान्वितेन गले गलौघः परिकीर्त्यतेऽसौ। योऽतिप्रताम्यन् इवसिति प्रसक्तं भिन्नस्वरः शुष्क-विमुक्तकण्ठः। कफोपदिग्धेष्वनिलायनेष् ज्ञेयः स रोगः इवसनात् स्वरघ्नः। प्रतानवान् यः इवयथः सुकष्टो गलोपरोधं कुरुते ऋमेण। स मांसतानः कथितोऽवलम्बी प्राणप्रणुत् सर्वक्रतो विकारः। सदाहतोदं इवयथुं सरक्तमन्तर्गले पूतिविशोर्णमांसम्। पित्तेन विद्याव्वदने विदारीं पाइवें विशेषात् स तु येन शर्त
transliteration: sarva galaṃ vyāpya samṛtthito yaḥ śopho rujo yatra ca santi sarvāḥ | sarvadoṣo galavidradhistra sa tasyeva tulyaḥ khalu savaṃjasya | śopho mahānannajalāvarodhī tīvrajvaro vātagartonahantā | kaphena jāto rudhirānvitena gale galaughaḥ parikīrtyate'sau | yo'tipratāmyan ivasiti prasaktaṃ bhinnasvaraḥ śuṣka-vimuktakaṇṭhaḥ | kaphopadigdheṣvani lāyaneṣ jñeyaḥ sa rogaḥ ivas anāt svaraghnaḥ | pratānavān yaḥ ivayathaḥ sukaṣṭo galoparodhaṃ kurute ṛmeṇa | sa māṃsatānaḥ kathito'valambī prāṇapraṇut sarvakrato vikāraḥ | sadāhatodaṃ ivayathuṃ saraktamantargale pūtiviśorṇamāṃsam | pittena vidyāvvadane vidārīṃ pāiveṃ viśeṣāt sa tu yena śarta
commentary: That disease, which produces inflammation after involving the whole of the throat and has pains of all the three types of doṣas, is called galavidradhi. It is due to all the doṣas together and has their combined features also. That disease, in which there is severe inflammation in the throat, obstruction to food and water, high fever and which obstructs the movements of wind, is called galaugha and is due to kapha and śoṇita. That disease, in which (the patient) has constant dyspnoea, hoarseness of voice, dry and paralysed throat and in which kapha occupies the places normally occupied by vāta, is known as svaraghna and is due to vāta. That disease, in which the painful, spreading inflammation produces obstruction in the throat gradually is called māṁsatāna; it is pendulous, is fatal and is due to all the doṣas together. That inflammation, which is associated with burning and pricking sensation, alongwith redness and putrified sodden flesh in the throat, is known as vidārī disease of the oral cavity; it is due to (vitiated) pitta and occurs specially on the side in which the patient sleeps.

sanskrit_text: सर्वसरास्त्र वातपित्तकफशोणितनिमित्ताः। स्फोटैः सतोदैर्वदनं समन्ताद्यस्याचितं सर्वसरः स वातात्। रक्तैः सदाहैस्तनुभिः सपीतैर्यस्याचितं चापि स पित्तकोपात्। कण्ड्यूतैरल्परुजैः सवर्ण र्यस्याचितं चापि स वै कफेन। रक्तेन पिस्तोदित एक एव कैशिचत् प्रदिष्टो मुखापाकसंज्ञः
transliteration: sarvasarāstra vātapittakaphaśoṇitanimittāḥ | sphoṭaiḥ satodairvadanaṃ samantādyasyācitaṃ sarvasaraḥ sa vātāt | raktaiḥ sadāhaistanubhiḥ sapītairyasyācitaṃ cāpi sa pittakopāt | kaṇḍyūtairalparujaiḥ savarṇa ryasyācitaṃ cāpi sa vai kaphena | raktena pīstodita eka eva kaiśicat pradiṣṭo mukhāpākasaṃjñaḥ
commentary: The sarvasara diseases are due to vāta, pitta, kapha and śoṇita. Vāta and Pitta Sarvasara : That sarvasara which has blisters, alongwith pricking pain all over the mouth, is due to (vitiated) vāta. And that sarvasara which is covered with reddish, slender and yellow (blisters) associated with burning sensation is due to (vitiated) pitta. Kaphaja Sarvasara and Mukhapāka: That sarvasara which is associated with itching and mildly painful blisters of the same colour as that of the mouth is due to (vitiated) kapha. The sarvasara produced by (vitiated) śoṇita and pitta are one and the same; some call it mukhapāka.
